(وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اسْجُدُوا لِلرَّحْمنِ قالُوا وَمَا الرَّحْمنُ): the wāw is resumptive; «إذا» is an adverbial of the future containing the meaning of a condition; the clause «قيل» is genitive through the annexation of the adverbial to it; «لهم» is attached to «قيل»; the clause «اسجدوا للرحمن» is the content of the saying; the clause «قالوا» is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition and has no grammatical position. The wāw (in «وما») is redundant; «ما الرحمن»: «ما» is an interrogative noun, a fronted khabar, and «الرحمن» is a postponed mubtadaʾ, or the reverse. It is permissible that it be a question about the one so named or about its meaning.
(أَنَسْجُدُ لِما تَأْمُرُنا وَزادَهُمْ نُفُوراً): the hamza is for rhetorical (denunciatory) interrogation; «نسجد» is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we"; «لما» is attached to «نسجد», that is: how can we prostrate to what we do not know? The clause «تأمرنا» is the ṣila. It is permissible that «ما» be maṣdar (verbal-noun forming), that is, "do we prostrate because of your command?" «زادهم» is a verb and agent, the agent referring to the saying, and the hāʾ is a direct object; «نفورا» is a second direct object or a tamyīz.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ثم استوى على العرش» there is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya), which the early scholars call takhyīliyya (imaginative). The thing borrowed is istiwāʾ (settling, being level); the source of the borrowing is every level body; the one to whom it is lent is the Truth, Mighty and Majestic. This is so that the hearer, on hearing this word, imagines a king who has finished arranging his realms and consolidating his kingdom and everything his subjects and troops need, the building up of his lands and the management of his servants' affairs, and has settled on the throne of his kingship in a settling of grandeur. Thus on hearing this speech the hearer measures what is hidden from his perception of the matter of divinity against what he imagines of the matter of worldly kingship. For this reason the mention of istiwāʾ on the Throne never occurs except after the report of having finished the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, even though there is no throne set up, no perceptible sitting, and no settling in the sense indicated by the outward meaning, namely a specific posture.

Benefit:
There are two schools on istiwāʾ. The first is the school of the Salaf, which does not interpret istiwāʾ but says that it is an istiwāʾ befitting Him. The second is the school of the Khalaf, which interprets it as having mastery over it, by exercising control over it and over the rest of creation.

* Benefits:
His saying «في ستة أيام»: that is, in the measure of this period. The apparent sense is that they are of the days of this world, the first being Sunday and the last Friday. They had names for them among the Arabs, namely: al-Aḥad: Awhal; al-Ithnayn: Awhan; al-Thulāthāʾ: Jubār; al-Arbiʿāʾ: Dubār; al-Khamīs: Muʾnis; al-Jumuʿa: ʿArūba; al-Sabt: Shiyār.

farraa:1-1.t: His saying: ﴿تَبَارَكَ﴾ — it is from al-baraka (blessing). In Arabic it is like your saying "Holy is our Lord" (taqaddasa rabbunā). Blessing and holiness [here mean] greatness, and the two are, after all, the same.

farraa:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿لَوْلاۤ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ فَيَكُونَ مَعَهُ﴾ — the answer is with the fāʾ because (لولا) is equivalent to hallā (why not).

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿أَوْ يُلْقَىٰ إِلَيْهِ كَنْزٌ أَوْ تَكُونُ﴾ for him — both are nominative, referred back to (لَولاَ), like your saying in speech: "or why is there not cast to him…". It has also been read (نَأْكُلُ مِنْهَا), and (yaʾkulu, with the yāʾ and with the nūn).

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلاً﴾ — He is saying: they cannot find any stratagem in your matter.

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِيۤ إِن شَآءَ جَعَلَ لَكَ﴾ — a conditional (jazāʾ). ﴿وَيَجْعَل لَّكَ قُصُوراً﴾ is jussive, referred back to (جَعَل), and (جَعَلَ) has the sense of a jussive. It may also be nominative while being, in that [reading], jussive [in form], because it is a lām that met a lām and so was made quiescent. If you put it in a clear nominative, that is permissible; (and its accusative is permissible by ṣarf (diversion)).

farraa:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿تَغَيُّظاً وَزَفِيراً﴾ — it is like the fury of a human being when he is angry: his breast boils and it shows in his speech.

farraa:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿ثُبُوراً﴾ — al-thubūr is a maṣdar; that is why He said ﴿ثُبُوراً كثيراً﴾ [and not a plural], because maṣdars are not pluralised. Do you not see that you say "I sat a long sitting" and "I beat him a great beating", and do not pluralise? The Arabs say: "What thabaraka from this?", that is, what turned you away from it. It is as though they called out [for destruction] because of what they had done, as a man says: "O my remorse!"

farraa:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿كَانَ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ وَعْداً مَّسْئُولاً﴾ — He is saying: Allah promised them Paradise, and they asked Him for it in this world when they said ﴿رَبَّنا وآتنا مَا وعَدْتَنَا عَلَى رُسُلك﴾ — He means on the tongues of Your messengers; and on the Day of Resurrection it is not asked for. It may be in speech that you say "I will surely give you a thousand — a promise to be claimed (masʾūl)", that is, it is due to you, so you may claim it; for what is masʾūl is due, even if it is not asked for, like a debt.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ سُبْحَانَكَ مَا كَانَ يَنبَغِي لَنَآ أَن نَّتَّخِذَ مِن دُونِكَ مِنْ أَوْلِيَآءَ﴾ — the idols said: "It was not for us to worship other than You; so how could we call [people] to worship us!" Then they said: "But You, O Lord, gave them enjoyment of wealth and children until they forgot Your remembrance." So Allah said to the humans: ﴿فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوكُمْ﴾ — He is saying: ﴿كذَّبتكم الآلهة بما تقولونَ﴾ «[Translator's note: a paraphrase, "the gods have given you the lie in what you say", placed in ornate brackets in the source.]». It is also read ﴿بِمَا يقولون﴾ with the yāʾ (and the tāʾ). Whoever reads with the tāʾ, it is like your saying "He gave you the lie; he gives you the lie"; and whoever reads with the yāʾ says: they gave you the lie by their saying. The Readers are agreed on fatḥa of the nūn in (نَتَّخِذَ), except Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī, who read (أن نُتَّخَذَ) with ḍamma on the nūn ﴿مِنْ دُونِكَ﴾. Had there been no (مِنْ) with al-awliyāʾ, it would be a good way; and despite (its irregularity and) the fewness of those who read it, it may be permissible on the basis that the noun is put in ﴿مِن أوليَاء﴾, even though it occupies the position of the verb [i.e. the predicate] «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 130b]». I preferred the saying of the majority only because the Arabs bring (مِن) into the nouns [i.e. subjects and objects], not into predicates. Do you not see that they say "I did not take anything (min shayʾ)" and "I have nothing (min shayʾ)", but they do not say "I did not see ʿAbdallāh as any man (min rajul)"? But if they meant "I did not see any man (min rajul) [as] ʿAbdallāh", making ʿAbdallāh the predicate, that would be permissible. And that is the view of Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī.
His saying: ﴿قَوْماً بُوراً﴾ — al-būr is a maṣdar, singular and plural alike; al-bāʾir is that which has nothing in it. You say: "Their dwellings became būr", that is, with nothing in them. Likewise the deeds of the unbelievers are void. One says "a būr man" and "a būr people".

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ إِنَّهُمْ لَيَأْكُلُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ﴾ — (ليأكلون) is a ṣila (relative clause) of an omitted noun, [its mention] made unnecessary by "of the messengers" (min al-mursalīn); like your saying in speech: "I have not sent to you any of the people except one who indeed obeys you" — do you not see that (إنه ليطيعَكَ) is the ṣila of man? Its implication is permissible, as He said ﴿ومَا مِنَّا إلا لَهُ مَقَام مَعْلومٌ﴾, whose meaning — and Allah knows best — is: except one who has a known station; and likewise His saying ﴿وَإِن مِنْكُمْ إِلاَّ وَارِدُهَا﴾: there is none of you but one who will come to it. And had the lām not been an answer to inna, inna would still have kasra, because it is at the beginning [of its clause], since it is a ṣila.
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا بَعْضَكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ فِتْنَةً أَتَصْبِرُونَ﴾ — the nobleman of Quraysh would say, of someone beneath him: "This one has become Muslim before me; shall I then become Muslim after him, so that he has precedence?" That is how some of them were tried by others. Allah said: ﴿أَتَصْبِرُونَ﴾. Al-Farrāʾ said: He is saying: it is this that you see.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ يَرْجُونَ لِقَآءَنَا﴾ — they do not fear meeting Us. It is a Tihāma usage: they put rajāʾ (hope) in the place of fear when there is a negation with it. Of that is His saying ﴿مَا لَكُمْ لاَ تَرْجُونَ للهِ وقاراً﴾, that is, you do not fear His greatness. Someone recited to me:
لا ترتجى حينَ تلاقى الذائدا * أسَبْعةً لاقَتْ مَعاً أم وَاحِداً
(She does not fear, when she meets the defender, whether she has met seven together or one.)
He means: she does not fear and does not care. And another «[Translator's note: the source has «وقال لآخر», apparently for «وقال آخر».]» said:
إذا لسعته النحل لم يَرْجُ لَسْعَهَا * وَحَالفَهَا فى بيتِ نُوب عَوَامِلِ
(When the bees sting him he does not fear their sting, and he stays close to them in a hive of working bees.)
One says nawb and nūb; and one says awb and ūb, from returning. Al-Farrāʾ said: al-nūb are the male bees.
His saying: ﴿وَعَتَوْا عُتُوّاً كَبِيراً﴾ — al-ʿutuww came with wāw because it is an explicit maṣdar. And He said in [Sūrat] Maryam: ﴿أيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ على الرحمن عِتِيّاً﴾. Whoever makes it with wāw makes it a pure maṣdar; and whoever makes it with yāʾ says: ʿātin and [plural] ʿutiyy; when they formed the plural, their plural was built on its singular. It is also permissible for the maṣdar to be with yāʾ, because maṣdars and nouns coincide in this respect. Do you not see that they say qāʿid and "a people quʿūd (sitting)", and "I sat quʿūdan"? Since the two are identical here, in quʿūd, they did not mind their being identical in ʿutuww and ʿutiyy.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةَ لاَ بُشْرَىٰ يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ — the "day" is not attached to "good tidings" (al-bushrā) so as to be put in the accusative by it; rather, you are implying a fāʾ, as in your saying in speech: "As for today, there is no wealth (fa-lā māl)". When you drop the fāʾ, you are implying the like of "today" after lā. Similar to it in speech: "With us there is no wealth": if you meant "there is no wealth with us" and placed "with us" first, it would not be permissible; but if you implied "with us" a second time after "no wealth", it would be sound. Do you not see that you do not say "Zayd — there is no one beating (zaydan lā ḍāriba), (O you)" as you say "There is no one beating Zayd (lā ḍāriba zaydan)"?
His saying: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ حِجْراً مَّحْجُوراً﴾ — [i.e.] utterly forbidden that they should have good tidings. Al-ḥijr is the forbidden, as you say: "The merchant laid an interdiction (ḥajara) on his slave", and "He laid an interdiction on his family". Someone recited to me:
فهممتُ أن ألقى إليهَا مَحْجَراً * ولَمِثْلُها يُلْقى إِليْهِ المحجَرُ
(I was about to approach her with a forbidden thing — and it is to one like her that the forbidden is approached.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: alqā and ulqā are from laqītu (to meet); that is, through one like her the forbidden is committed.

farraa:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَدِمْنَآ إِلَىٰ مَا عَمِلُواْ مِنْ عَمَلٍ﴾ — [i.e.] ʿamadnā (We turned to), with fatḥa on the ʿayn. ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُ هَبَآءً مَّنثُوراً﴾ — that is, void. Al-habāʾ has a long final vowel and is originally without hamza; its diminutive is hubayy, as al-kisāʾ has the diminutive kusayy. But jufāʾ al-wādī (the scum of the valley) originally has hamza; if you form its diminutive you say "this is jufayʾ", like jufayʿ. Every word with a long final vowel, whether from hamza, from yāʾ or from wāw, is formed by analogy with these two.

farraa:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿أَصْحَابُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُّسْتَقَرّاً وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلاً﴾ — he said: some of the ḥadīth transmitters hold that the reckoning of people will be finished in the middle of that day, and the people of Paradise will take their midday rest (yaqīlu) in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire. That is His saying ﴿خَيْرٌ مُّسْتَقَرّاً وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلاً﴾. Now the people of kalām (dialectical theology), when a fool and a wise man are together, do not permit saying "This is the more foolish of the two men" or "the wiser of the two men"; they say: we do not say "This is the wiser of the two men" except of two wise men, one of whom is preferred over the other. Yet I have heard the saying of Allah ﴿خَيْرٌ مُّسْتَقَرّاً﴾, where He made the people of Paradise better in abode than the people of the Fire, though there is nothing of good in the abode of the people of the Fire. So recognise from this their error.

farraa:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِٱلْغَمَامِ﴾ — it is also read ﴿تَشَّقَّقُ﴾ with doubling; al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read it (تَشَقَّقُ السَّمَاءُ) with the shīn light. Whoever reads tashshaqqaqu means tatashaqqaqu, with doubling of the shīn and the qāf, and assimilated [the tāʾ], as He said ﴿لا يَسَّمّعون إلى الملأ الأعلى﴾. Its meaning — according to what they have mentioned — is: the sky will split open (from the white clouds), then the angels will descend in it. ʿAlā, ʿan and the bāʾ «[Translator's note: the source has «اليَاء» (the yāʾ), evidently for «الباء».]» in this position (have one meaning), because the Arabs say "I shot from the bow (ʿan al-qaws)", "with the bow (bi-l-qaws)" and "on the bow (ʿalā al-qaws)", meaning one thing.

farraa:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿لَّقَدْ أَضَلَّنِي عَنِ ٱلذِّكْرِ﴾ — it is said [the dhikr is] the Prophet, and it is said: the Qurʾān. There are two views about it.

farraa:30-30.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلرَّسُولُ يٰرَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِي ٱتَّخَذُواْ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ مَهْجُوراً﴾ — [i.e.] abandoned. It is also said: they made it like raving; the Arabs say (the man hajara) in his sleep when he raves or keeps repeating a word.

farraa:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوّاً﴾ — He is saying: We made some of every prophet's community harsher towards him than others. The one fiercest in enmity to the Prophet ﷺ was Abū Jahl ibn Hishām.

farraa:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿لَوْلاَ نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْآنُ جُمْلَةً وَاحِدَةً كَذَلِكَ﴾ — it is said that it [كذلك] is part of the saying of the idolaters, that is: why was the Qurʾān not sent down to him all at once, as the Torah was sent down to Mūsā? Allah said: ﴿وَرَتَّلْنَاهُ تَرْتِيلاً﴾ — so that We may make your heart firm by it. He used to send down a verse or two, so that between the revelation of its beginning and its end there were twenty years. ﴿وَرَتَّلْنَاهُ تَرْتِيلاً﴾ — We sent it down piece by piece. It is also said that (كذلك) is from the saying of Allah: their speech ends at (جملةً وَاحِدَةً), and Allah said: Thus have We sent it down, O Muḥammad, in parts, so that We may make your heart firm by it.

farraa:33-33.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَحْسَنَ تَفْسِيراً﴾ — it is like His saying ﴿أصحابُ الجنَّة يوْمَئِذٍ وأحْسَنُ مَقِيلاً﴾ in the meaning of the sentence and in the accusative [of the tamyīz, specification].

farraa:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿فَقُلْنَا ٱذْهَبَآ﴾ — in meaning, only Mūsā was commanded to go. This is like His saying ﴿نَسِيا حُوتَهُمَا﴾, and like His saying ﴿يَخرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللؤلؤُ والمَرْجان﴾, when they come out of only one of them. Its matter has already been explained.

farraa:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ لَّمَّا كَذَّبُواْ ٱلرُّسُلَ أَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ﴾ — you put them in the accusative by aghraqnāhum, or if you wish by the destruction mentioned before them.

farraa:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿وَعَاداً وَثَمُودَاْ وَأَصْحَابَ ٱلرَّسِّ وَقُرُوناً﴾ — they are accusative by the destruction. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is said that al-rass is a well.

farraa:39-39.t: His saying: ﴿وَكُلاًّ تَبَّرْنَا تَتْبِيراً﴾ — We destroyed them and annihilated them utterly.

farraa:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَـٰهَهُ هَوَاهُ﴾ — one of them would pass by a fine-looking stone and worship it; that is His saying ﴿ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَـٰهَهُ هَوَاهُ﴾.

farraa:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿كَيْفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ﴾ — [this is] what lies between the break of dawn and sunrise. His saying ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ لَجَعَلَهُ سَاكِناً﴾ — He is saying: permanent. His saying ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا ٱلشَّمْسَ عَلَيْهِ دَلِيلاً﴾ — He is saying: when there is sun in a place «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 131b]», there was shade in it before that; so the sun was made an indicator of the shade.

farraa:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ قَبَضْنَاهُ إِلَيْنَا قَبْضاً يَسِيراً﴾ — He means the shade: when the sun overtakes it, the shade is drawn in an easy drawing-in; He is saying: gentle and imperceptible.

farraa:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَرْسَلَ ٱلرِّيَاحَ بُشْرَى﴾ — the companions of ʿAbdallāh read (الرياح) in three places: two of them are words in our reading, and one is in al-Naḥl and is not in our reading, in the place of His saying ﴿والنجوم مُسَخرات بأمره﴾; this is one — he means the one in al-Furqān «[Translator's note: the source has «القرقان», a misprint for «الفرقان».]» — and the other is in al-Rūm: ﴿الرياح مُبَشِّراتٍ﴾. ʿĀṣim used to read what was of the wind's mercy as riyāḥ, and what was of punishment he read rīḥ. The Readers differed concerning mercy: some read al-rīḥ and some read al-riyāḥ; but they did not differ about punishment being with al-rīḥ. We think they chose al-riyāḥ for mercy because the winds of mercy come from the east wind (al-ṣabā), the south wind and the north wind, of the three well-known ones; while what most often brings punishment, and has no rain in it, is the west wind (al-dabūr), because the dabūr hardly ever fertilises [the clouds]. So it was called rīḥ, in the singular, because it does not circulate as the fertilising winds circulate.
Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Aswad ibn Yazīd and Masrūq ibn al-Ajdaʿ, that they both read (نَشْراً). The Readers have read (نُشُراً) and (نُشْراً), and ʿĀṣim read (بُشراً). Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Qays narrated to me from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, that he read (بُشُراً), as though [from] bashīra, [plural] bushur.

farraa:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنَاسِيَّ كَثِيراً﴾ — its singular is insiyy; or if you wish you may take it as insān and then form its plural as anāsiyy, so that the yāʾ is a substitute for the nūn. Insān is originally insiyān, because the Arabs form its diminutive as unaysiyān. When they say anāsīn, it is clear, like bustān and basātīn. And when they say (anāsiya kathīran), lightening the yāʾ, they have dropped the yāʾ that comes between the ʿayn and the lām of the word, as in qarāqīr and qarāqir. What shows the permissibility of anāsī, light, is the Arabs' saying anāsiya kathīra; but we have not heard it in the recitation.

farraa:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخاً﴾ — al-barzakh is the barrier: He placed a barrier between them so that the salt would not overcome the sweet.
His saying: ﴿وَحِجْراً مَّحْجُوراً﴾ — (of that, that is) utterly forbidden that one of them should overcome the other.

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿وَكَانَ ٱلْكَافِرُ عَلَىٰ رَبِّهِ ظَهِيراً﴾ — al-muẓāhir is the helper, and al-ẓahīr is help (or a helper).

farraa:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ وَمَا ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ﴾ — they mentioned that Musaylima used to be called al-Raḥmān; so they said: "We know no Raḥmān except the one in al-Yamāma", meaning Musaylima the Liar. So Allah revealed ﴿قُلْ ادْعُوا اللهَ أوِ ادْعُوا الرحمنَ أيَّامَّا تَدْعُوا فَلَهُ الأسْمَاءُ الحُسْنَى﴾.
His saying: ﴿أَنَسْجُدُ لِمَا يَأْمُرُنَا﴾ and ﴿وتأمرنا﴾ — whoever reads with the yāʾ means Musaylima; whoever reads with the tāʾ may (also) mean Musaylima, and it would be about the command: "Shall we prostrate to your command to us?" And whoever reads with the tāʾ and the yāʾ, Muḥammad ﷺ is meant by it, (and it is like His saying) ﴿قُلْ للذين كَفَرُوا سَتُغْلَبُونَ وتحشرون﴾ and ﴿وسَيُغلبونَ﴾, while the meaning [of the address] is to Muḥammad ﷺ.

farraa:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سُرُجاً﴾ — the reading of the general public is ﴿سِرَاجاً﴾. Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: [al-Farrāʾ] narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to me from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, that he read (سُرُجاً); and that is likewise the reading of the companions of ʿAbdallāh. Whoever reads ﴿سراجاً﴾ refers it to the sun, and that is a good way, because He said ﴿وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِرَاجاً﴾. Whoever says ﴿سُرُجاً﴾ refers it to the lamps [i.e. the stars], since one is guided by them; he made them like lamps (suruj), and the miṣbāḥ is like the sirāj in the speech of the Arabs «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 132a]»; and Allah said ﴿المِصْبَاحُ فِى زُجَاجَةٍ﴾.

farraa:62-62.t:
His saying: ﴿جَعَلَ ٱللَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ خِلْفَةً﴾ — this one goes and that one comes. Zuhayr said about that:
بِها العِينُ والآرام يَمْشِين خِلفَةً * وأطلاؤهَا يَنْهَضْنَ من كل مَجْثَم
(There the wild cows and white gazelles walk in succession, and their young rise up from every resting-place.)
The meaning of Zuhayr's khilfatan is: differing, in that they are of two kinds in colour and form; and khilfa may also be in their gait. It has been mentioned that His saying ﴿خِلْفَةً لِّمَنْ أَرَادَ﴾ means: whoever misses a deed in the night makes it up in the day, so He made this a replacement (khalaf) for that.
His saying: ﴿لِّمَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَذَّكَّرَ﴾ — in the reading of Ubayy it is (يتذكّرَ), which is evidence for whoever reads with doubling. The reading of the companions of ʿAbdallāh, of Ḥamza and of many people is (لِمَنْ أَرادَ أنْ يَذْكُر), light; yadhkuru and yatadhakkaru come with one meaning. In our reading there is ﴿واذكُرُوا ما فِيهِ﴾, and in the text of ʿAbdallāh (وَتذكَّرُوا ما فيه).

farraa:63-63.t:
His saying: ﴿عَلَىٰ ٱلأَرْضِ هَوْناً﴾ — Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Sharīk narrated to me from Jābir al-Juʿfī, from ʿIkrima and Mujāhid, concerning His saying ﴿اٱلَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَىٰ ٱلأَرْضِ هَوْناً﴾: he said: with tranquillity and dignity.
His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الجَاهِلُونَ قَالُواْ سَلاَماً﴾ — when the people of Mecca reviled the Muslims, they [the Muslims] would answer them with a fair reply, before they were commanded to fight them.

farraa:64-64.t: His saying: ﴿ وَالَّذِينَ يِبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّداً وَقِيَاماً﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that whoever recites something of the Qurʾān in prayer, however little, has spent the night prostrating and standing. They mentioned that they are the two rakʿas after the Maghrib, and after the ʿIshāʾ two rakʿas.

farraa:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَاماً﴾ — He is saying: persistent, permanent. The Arabs say: "So-and-so is mughram with women", when he is infatuated with them; and "I am mughram with you", when one cannot do without the man. We think that the creditor (al-gharīm) was called gharīm only because he claims his due and persists until he receives it.

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَنفَقُواْ لَمْ يُسْرِفُواْ وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُواْ﴾ — with kasra on the tāʾ. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and ʿĀṣim read (ولم يُقْتِروا), from aqtartu; al-Ḥasan read (وَلَمْ يَقْتِرُوا), which is from qatartu, like the saying of whoever read yaqturū with ḍamma on the yāʾ «[Translator's note: so in the source; the ḍamma meant is evidently on the tāʾ (yaqturū).]». Their difference is like the difference in His saying ﴿يَعرِشُونَ﴾ and ﴿يَعْرُشُونَ﴾, and ﴿يَعْكِفُونَ﴾ and ﴿يعكُفونَ﴾. And the meaning of ﴿لم يُسْرِفُواْ﴾ [is clear]. As for the accusative of al-qawām, there are two ways. If you wish, you put al-qawām in the accusative through an implied noun in kāna (that noun being "the spending"), that is: and the spending was ﴿قَوَاماً بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ﴾ — as you say "just, between that", that is, between extravagance and stinginess. Or if you wish, you make (بين) have the sense of a nominative, as you say "Less than this (dūna hādhā) was sufficient for you", meaning: less than this was sufficient for you; and you make ﴿وكان بينَ ذلك﴾ [mean]: the middle of that was qawām. Al-qawām is the qawām of a thing between two things. It is said of a woman: "She has a fine qawām (figure)", in her well-proportionedness. And it is said: "You are the qiwām of your family", that is, by you their affair and condition are upheld; and qiyām, qiyam and qayyim have the meaning of qiwām.

farraa:68-69.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذٰلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثَاماً﴾ ﴿يُضَاعَفْ لَهُ ٱلْعَذَابُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيامَةِ﴾ — the Readers read (يضاعف) in the jussive, and ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd read it in the nominative. The [proper] way is the jussive. That is because every jussive that you explain [with another verb], when [the second] is not an action of what precedes it, the proper way for it is the jussive; and whatever is an action of what precedes it, you put in the nominative. As for that which explains the jussive, it is His saying ﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذٰلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثَاماً﴾; then He explained al-athām, saying ﴿يُضَاعَفْ لَهُ ٱلْعَذَابُ﴾. Similar in speech: "If you speak to me — enjoin on me goodness and piety (tūṣinī) — I will accept it from you": do you not see that you explained the speaking with the piety, and it was not an action of it? Therefore you used the jussive. Had the second been an action of the first, you would put it in the nominative, as in your saying: "If you come to us, seeking (taṭlubu) good, you will find it"; do you not see that you find (تطُلب) to be an action of the coming «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 132b]», like your saying: "If you come to us as one seeking good, you will find it"?
The poet said:
مَتى تأْتِهِ تَعْشُو إلى ََضَوْءِ نَارِه * تجد خير نار عندهَا خَيْرُ موقد
(Whenever you come to him, making your way by night to the light of his fire, you will find the best of fires, with the best of kindlers beside it.)
He put (تَعْشو) in the nominative because he meant: whenever you come to him as one travelling by night. ʿĀṣim put (يُضاعف له) in the nominative because he intended a fresh start, as you say: "If you come to us we will honour you; we give you all you want", not as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

farraa:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ﴾ — He is saying: they do not attend the gatherings of falsehood and sins.
It is also said: (the festivals of the idolaters, which they do not attend), because they are falsehood and lies, since they are for other than Allah. His saying ﴿بِاللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا كِراماً﴾ — it has been mentioned that when they brought up the mention of women, they would use allusion instead of ugly speech about them; that is their passing by it.

farraa:73-73.t:
His saying: ﴿لَمْ يَخِرُّواْ عَلَيْهَا صُمّاً وَعُمْيَاناً﴾ — it is said: when the Qurʾān was recited to them, they did not remain in their former state as though they had not heard it; that is the "falling". I have heard the Arabs say "He sat down reviling me" and "He came forward reviling me" [i.e. he set about reviling me].
One of the Arabs recited to me:
لا يُقنع الجاريةَ الخِضَابُ * ولا الوشاحَان ولا الجِلبَابُ
مِن دون أن تلتِقىَ الأركَابُ * وَيَقْعُدَ الهَنُ لَهُ لُعَابُ
(The girl is not satisfied by henna, nor by two sashes, nor by a cloak, short of the private parts meeting and the "thing" coming to be wet.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: the place of the private parts is called rakab; and yaqʿudu is like your saying yaṣīru (becomes).

farraa:74-74.t:
His saying: ﴿وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا﴾ — the companions of ʿAbdallāh read (وَذُرِّيَّتِنَا), and the majority ﴿وذُرِّيَّاتِنَا﴾. His saying ﴿قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ﴾ — had it been said ﴿عَيْنٍ﴾ it would be correct, as she said ﴿قُرَّةُ عَيْنٍ لِى وَلَكَ﴾; and had it been read qurrāti aʿyun, because they are many, it would be correct. The [proper] way is the singular, ﴿قُرَّة أعين﴾, because it is a verbal notion (fiʿl), and the verbal notion (is hardly ever pluralised). Do you not see that He said ﴿لا تَدْعُوا اليَوْمَ ثُبُوراً وَاحِداً وادْعُوا ثُبُوراً كَثِيراً﴾ and did not pluralise it, though it is many? Al-qurra is a maṣdar: you say qarrat ʿaynuka qurratan.
His saying: ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَاماً﴾ — He did not say aʾimma, though it is [here] singular. It is permissible in speech to say "The companions of Muḥammad are the leaders (aʾimma) of the people" and "the leader (imām) of the people", as He said ﴿إنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ العالمينَ﴾ of two. Its meaning is: make us «[Translator's note: the source has «اجعنا», a misprint for «اجعلنا».]» leaders who are followed. Mujāhid said: make us follow those before us, so that those after us may follow us.

farraa:75-75.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَلْقَوْنَ﴾ and ﴿يُلَقَّوْنَ فِيهَا﴾ — each has been read, and ﴿يَلْقَوْنَ﴾ is more pleasing to me, because had the reading been ﴿يُلقَّونَ﴾ it would be with the bāʾ in Arabic, since you say "So-and-so is met (yutalaqqā) with greeting and with good". Yet it is correct: yulaqqawnahu and yulaqqawna bihi, as you say "I took hold of the halter (bi-l-khiṭām)" and "I took it".

farraa:77-77.t:
His saying: ﴿مَا يَعْبَأُ بِكُمْ رَبِّي﴾ — mā is interrogative, that is: what would He do with you? ﴿لَوْلاَ دُعَآؤُكُمْ﴾ — were it not for His calling you to Islam. ﴿فَقَدْ كَذَّبْتُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزَاماً﴾ — you put al-lizām in the accusative because you implied a noun in (يكون). If you wish, it is an unspecified [noun], so that it is like His saying in the reading of Ubayy (وإنْ كَانَ ذَا عُسْرَةٍ); or if you wish, you make it: your denial will be a binding punishment. It is mentioned that it is what befell them on the day of Badr. The nominative in it would be permissible had it come. The Arabs also say: "I will surely strike you a blow that will be lazāmi, O you", in the genitive [i.e. with kasra], as you say darāki and naẓāri. He recited:
لا زلتَ مُحتمِلاً علىّ ضغينَةً * حَتى المماتِ تكونُ مِنْكَ لَزَامِ
(May you never cease bearing a grudge against me until death, one that clings to you inseparably.)
He said: we recited it to him among the maṣdars.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «تبارك الذي»: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). «للعالمين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) «نذيرا».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «الذي» is a badal (substitute) of the preceding relative noun. «ولدًا» is the second object, and the implied (muqaddar) «أحدًا» is the first object. The clause «ولم يتخذ» is conjoined to the clause «له ملك». The preposition «في الملك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شريك»; the preposition «له» is attached to the khabar (predicate) of «يكن». The clause «له ملك» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the clause «ولم يكن له شريك» is conjoined to the clause «له ملك».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «واتخذوا» is resumptive; the preposition «من دونه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «اتخذ». The clause «لا يخلقون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «آلهة», and the clause «وهم يخلقون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in «يخلقون».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «إنْ» is negating; «هذا إفك» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); «إلا» is restrictive (li-l-ḥaṣr). The clause «افتراه» is a naʿt (adjective). «ظلمًا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the verb «جاء» sometimes being transitive by itself.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «أساطير»: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. هي. The clause «اكتتبها» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «أساطير»; the clause «فهي تملى» is conjoined to the clause «اكتتبها». «بكرة» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «تملى».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The preposition «في السماوات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «يعلم».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «مال هذا»: «ما» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the prepositional phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); «الرسول» is a badal (substitute), and the clause «يأكل» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الرسول». «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), and the clause after it is resumptive within the scope of the saying. The fāʾ in «فيكون» is causal (sababiyya), and the verb is in the subjunctive by an implied «أن»; the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, i.e. هلا كان نزول ملك فكونه معه نذيرا (why was there not the descent of an angel, and his being a warner with him?).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «وقال الظالمون» is conjoined to the resumptive clause {وَقَالُوا}. «إنْ» is negating.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «كيف» is an interrogative noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial). The clause «ضربوا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the [verb of] looking, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative, which carries the sense of knowing. The clause «فلا يستطيعون» is conjoined to the clause «ضلوا».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The conditional clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The preposition «لك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «جعل»; the preposition «من ذلك» is attached to «خيرًا»; «جنات» is a badal (substitute) of «خيرًا». «ويجعلْ» is jussive (majzūm), conjoined to the position of «جعل».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «كذبوا» is resumptive. The clause «وأعتدنا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: (إذا رأتهم من مكان بعيد) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is a naʿt (adjective) of {سَعِيرًا}, which is feminine.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The conditional clause is conjoined to the preceding conditional clause. «مكانًا» is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ألقوا»; the preposition «منها» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «مكانًا», having originally been an adjective of it. «مقرَّنين» is a ḥāl of the wāw in «ألقوا». «هنالك» is a demonstrative, an adverb of place attached to «دَعَوا». «ثبورا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because they say: يا ثبوراه (O destruction!).

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «لا تدعوا» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying) of an implied verb of saying.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: «جنة»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «ذلك»; «التي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «الجنة». The preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «جزاء». The clause «كانت» is a ḥāl of «جنة الخلد».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The preposition «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [notion of] settledness (istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached. «خالدين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يشاءون». The preposition «على ربك» is attached to a ḥāl of «وَعْدًا». The clause «لهم فيها ما يشاءون» is a second ḥāl of «جنة الخلد», and the clause «كان وعدًا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: «ويوم»: the wāw is a conjunction; «يوم» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied اذكر (remember), and the clause is conjoined to the preceding clause {قُلْ}. The preposition «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied returning pronoun, i.e. ما يعبدونه كائنًا من دون الله (what they worship, being other than Allah). «هؤلاء» is a naʿt (adjective) interpreted as a derived word, i.e. المشار إليهم (those pointed to). The clause «هم ضلُّوا» is conjoined to the clause «أأنتم أضللتم».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The noun of kāna is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). The interpreted maṣdar «أن نتخذ» is the fāʿil (agent) of «ينبغي»; the preposition «من دونك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «نتخذ»; the second «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), and «أولياء» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «ما كان ينبغي» is resumptive within the scope of the saying, and the clause «ولكن متعتهم» is conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying). «وآباءهم» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the hāʾ. The interpreted maṣdar «أنْ نسوا» is genitive, attached to «متعتهم».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «فقد كذَّبوكم» is resumptive, and the clause «فما تستطيعون» is conjoined to the clause «كذَّبوكم». The clause «ومن يظلم» is resumptive; «مَنْ» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition «منكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يظلم»; «عذابًا» is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The clause «وما أرسلنا» is resumptive. The preposition «من المرسلين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of the implied object, i.e. أحدًا كائنًا من المرسلين (anyone among the messengers); «إلا» is restrictive (li-l-ḥaṣr). The clause «إنهم ليأكلون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «المرسلين». The preposition «لبعض» is attached to a ḥāl of «فتنة». The clause «أتصبرون» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «وكان ...».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «وقال» is resumptive; «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); the clause «نرى» is conjoined to the clause «أنزل»; and the clause «لقد استكبروا» is the response to an implied oath. «عَتَوا»: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied ḍamma on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: «يوم» is an object of an implied اذكر (remember), and the clause is resumptive; the clause «يرون» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). «يوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «لا», and «إذٍ» is muḍāf ilayhi, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, its tanwīn compensating for a clause. The preposition «للمجرمين» is attached to the [notion of] settledness (istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached. «حجرًا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and «محجورًا» is a naʿt (adjective); the clause «حجرًا محجورا» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying).

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The preposition «من عمل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما»; «هباء» is the second object of «جعل».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The adverb «يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); «إذٍ» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «مستقرًا» is a tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: «ويوم»: the wāw is a conjunction; «يوم» is an object of an implied اذكر (remember), and the clause is conjoined to the implied اذكر in verse (22). The clause «تشقق» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: «الملك» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); its khabar (predicate) is what the preposition «للرحمن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq). «يوم» is attached to the [notion of] settledness (istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached. «الحق» is a naʿt (adjective) of «الملك». The noun of kāna is the pronoun of «اليوم», and «يومًا» is its khabar; the preposition «على الكافرين» is attached to «عسيرًا»; «عسيرا» is a naʿt of «يومًا». The clause «وكان يومًا» is conjoined to the resumptive clause «الملك للرحمن».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: «ويوم»: the wāw is a conjunction, and «يوم» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «يوم» in verse (25); the implied sense is: واذكر يوم تشقق ويوم يَعَضُّ (remember the day it splits and the day he bites). The preposition «على يديه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يعض». «يا» is for drawing attention (tanbīh); «مع» is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to the second object; and the clause «يقول» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الظالم». [Translator's note: the quotation marks are misplaced in the source text; the reading above follows the evident sense.]

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: «يا ويلتى»: a vocative (munādā) in a genitive construct, accusative with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ that was changed into an alif; this alif is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «ليتني لم أتخذ» is resumptive within the scope of the saying.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The clause «لقد أضلَّني» is the response to an oath. «إذ» is an adverbial noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, and the clause «جاءني» is muḍāf ilayhi. The clause «وكان الشيطان خذولا» is resumptive; the preposition «للإنسان» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خذولا».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The clause «وقال» is resumptive; the clause «إن قومي اتخذوا» is the response to the vocative, resumptive; «مهجورا» is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: (وكذلك جعلنا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw is resumptive; the kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the implied sense being: جعلنا جَعْلا مثلَ ذلك الجعل (We made a making like that making). The clause «جعلنا» is resumptive, and the preposition «لكل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object. The preposition «من المجرمين» is attached to «عدوا». The wāw in «وكفى» is resumptive, the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), «ربك» is the fāʿil (agent), and «هاديًا» is a tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); «جملةً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «القرآن». The kāf in «كذلك» is a preposition, and «ذا» is a genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. الأمر كذلك (the matter is thus). The genitive interpreted maṣdar in «لنثبت» is attached to an omitted verb, i.e. فَعَلْنا ذلك لنثبت (We did that in order to make firm). The clause «الأمر كذلك» is resumptive, the implied clause «فعلنا» is resumptive, and the clause «ورتَّلْناه» is conjoined to the implied clause «فعلنا».

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The clause «ولا يأتونك» is resumptive; the clause «جئناك» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of «يأتونك»; the preposition «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of «جئناك»; «أحسن» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الحق»; and «تفسيرًا» is a tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); its khabar (predicate) is the clause «أولئك شر», and the clause is resumptive. The preposition «على وجوههم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the preposition «إلى جهنم» is attached to «يحشرون»; «مكانًا» is a tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The wāw in «ولقد» is resumptive; «معه» is an adverb of place (ẓarf makān) attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعلنا»; «هارون» is a badal (substitute).

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The clause «فقلنا» is conjoined to the clause «جعلنا», and the clause «فدمَّرناهم» is conjoined to an implied clause, i.e. فكذَّبوهما فدمَّرناهم (they belied them both, so We destroyed them).

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: «وقوم نوح»: the wāw is resumptive, and «قوم» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb whose implied form is «اذكر» (remember); the clause «واذكر» is resumptive. «لما» is a particle of necessity upon necessity (wujūb li-wujūb). The preposition «للناس» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «آية». The conditional clause is a ḥāl of «قوم نوح», and the clause «أغرقناهم» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The clause «وأعتدنا» is conjoined to the clause «جعلناهم».

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: «وعادًا»: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «قوم». The adverb «بين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «قرونًا», and «كثيرًا» is a second naʿt of «قرونًا».

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: «وكلا»: the wāw is a conjunction, and «كلا» is an object of an omitted verb explained by what follows, its implied form being «أنذرنا كلا» (We warned each). The implied clause is conjoined to the clause «أعتدنا», and the clause «ضربنا» is explicative (tafsīriyya). The second «كلا» is an object placed before «تَبَّر».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The clause «ولقد أتَوْا» is resumptive; «التي» is a naʿt (adjective); «مطر» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The clause «أفلم يكونوا» is conjoined to the clause «أتوا»; the clause «كانوا» is resumptive; and «بل» is for iḍrāb (digression).

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «إنْ» is negating; «هزوًا» is the second object. «إذا» is an adverbial conditional particle (ẓarfiyya sharṭiyya) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied clause «قالوا». «رسولا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied returning pronoun, i.e. بعثه رسولا (He sent him as a messenger). The clause «إنْ يتخذونك» is parenthetical (muʿtariḍa); the implied clause «قالوا» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the clause «أهذا الذي» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying) of the implied «قالوا».

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: «إنْ» is lightened (mukhaffafa) and inoperative (muhmala); «كاد» is an abrogating verb (nāsikha), and its noun is the pronoun هو; the clause is resumptive within the scope of negation. The lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), and the clause «ليضلنا» is the khabar (predicate) of kāda. «لولا» is a particle of non-occurrence due to occurrence (imtināʿ li-wujūd); «أَنْ» and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar, a mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being موجود (exists). The clause «لولا صبرُنا موجود» is resumptive within the scope of the saying, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The clause «وسوف يعلمون» is resumptive; «حين» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يعلمون». «مَنْ أَضَلُّ»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause fills the place of the two objects of «يعلمون», which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: «مَنْ» is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The two objects of «اتخذ» are «إلهه هواه». The fāʾ in «فأنت» is redundant (zāʾida); the preposition «عليه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «وكيلا». The clause «أفأنت تكون» is the second object of «أرأيت».

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: «أم» is the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) one, and the interpreted maṣdar fills the place of the two objects of «حسب». The clause «إن هم إلا كالأنعام» is resumptive, and «إنْ» is negating. The clause «بل هم أضل» is resumptive, and «سبيلا» is a tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: «كيف» is an interrogative noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial). The clause «كيف مدَّ» is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of «ربك». The clause «ولو شاء لجعله» is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya). The clause «ثم جعلنا» is conjoined to the clause «مدَّ»; the preposition «عليه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl of «دليلا».

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: The clause «ثم قبضناه» is conjoined to the clause {جَعَلْنَا}, in the position of the genitive.

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: The clause «وهو الذي» is conjoined to the clause {أَلَمْ تَرَ}; the preposition «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعل». As for «والنوم سباتا»: «النوم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الليل», and «سباتا» is conjoined to «لباسًا».

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: The clause «وهو الذي» is conjoined to the preceding clause «هو الذي»; «بشرًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الرياح»; «بين» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أرسل».

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The genitive interpreted maṣdar «لنحيي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أنزلنا». The preposition «مما» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «أنعامًا», and «أنعامًا» is the first object of «نسقيه»; the implied sense is: ونسقي أنعامًا كائنة من الذي خلقناه الماء (and We give the water to drink to cattle, being among what We created). «أناسيّ» is the plural of إنسان; its original form is أناسين; the nūn was changed into yāʾ, and the yāʾ before it was assimilated into it.

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: The clause «ولقد صَرَّفْناه» is conjoined to the clause {وَأَنْزَلْنَا}, and the clause «فأبى» is conjoined to the clause «صَرَّفْناه». «كفورًا» is the object of «أبى»; the exception is emptied (mufarragh), preceded by the sense of negation in «أبى».

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: (ولو شئنا لبعثنا في كل قرية نذيرا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: The clause «وهو الذي» is conjoined to the clause {وَهُوَ الَّذِي} in verse (48). The clause «هذا عذب» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «البحرين», and the adverb «بينهما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: The clause «فجعله» is conjoined to the clause «خلق», and the clause «وكان ربك قديرا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The clause «ويعبدون» is resumptive; the preposition «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما», and «ما» is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «وكان ...» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: The clause «وما أرسلناك» is resumptive; «إلا» is restrictive (li-l-ḥaṣr); «مبشِّرًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the kāf.

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), and «أجر» is the second object; the preposition «عليه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «أجر». «إلا» is for exception; «مَنْ» is a relative noun, a disconnected excepted (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ). The preposition «إلى ربه» is attached to the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: «الذي» is a naʿt (adjective). The preposition «بحمده» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «سبِّح», i.e. ملتبسًا «بحمده» (accompanied by His praise). The bāʾ after «كفى» is redundant (zāʾida), and the hāʾ is the fāʿil. The preposition «بذنوب» is attached to «خبيرًا»; «خبيرًا» is a tamyīz (specification). The clause «كفى به» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: «الذي» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); its khabar (predicate) is «الرحمن». The adverb «بينهما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause). The fāʾ in «فاسأل» is resumptive. The bāʾ in «به» is attached to «خبيرًا»; «خبيرًا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «اسأل».

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: The wāw is resumptive, as is the conditional clause. The preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قيل», and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is the pronoun of the maṣdar. The maqūl al-qawl (object of saying) after «قالوا» is implied, i.e. نسجد. «ما» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «الرحمن» is the khabar (predicate). The lām is a preposition of cause, and «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), the maṣdar being genitive, i.e. أنسجد لأمرك؟ (shall we prostrate because of your command?). The fāʿil (agent) of «زادهم» is the pronoun of the saying; «نفورا» is the second object. The clause «أنسجد» is resumptive within the scope of the saying, and the clause «وزادهم» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:61-61.t: The preposition «في السماء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «جعل».

harrat-mujtaba:62-62.t: The clause «وهو الذي» is conjoined to the preceding clause {تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي}. «خلفة» is the second object. The interpreted maṣdar «أن يذَّكَّر» is the object of «أراد».

harrat-mujtaba:63-63.t: The clause «وعباد الرحمن ...» is resumptive, and the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) will come in verse (75). «هونًا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. مشيًا هَوْنًا (a gentle walking). The conditional clause is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause). «سلامًا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. نسلِّم سلامًا (we greet with a greeting of peace); it is thus a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar), the maṣdar being تسليم.

harrat-mujtaba:64-64.t: The relative noun is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding relative noun. «يبيتون» is an abrogating (nāsikh) imperfect verb with its noun; the khabar (predicate) is «سُجَّدًا», and the preposition «لربهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:65-65.t: The clause «إن عذابها كان غرامًا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:66-66.t: «مستقرًا» is a tamyīz (specification), and the [noun] specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. جهنم (Hell).

harrat-mujtaba:67-67.t: The conditional clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The noun of kāna is the pronoun of the spending; «بين» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «قواما».

harrat-mujtaba:68-68.t: The relative noun is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding one. «مع» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «إلهًا»; the preposition «بالحق» is attached to a ḥāl of the wāw in «يقتلون». The conditional clause is resumptive; «مَنْ» is a conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject).

harrat-mujtaba:69-69.t: The clause «يضاعَفْ» is a badal (substitute) of the clause {يَلْقَ}. «مهانًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يخلد».

harrat-mujtaba:70-70.t: «مَنْ» is a relative noun, a connected excepted (mustathnā muttaṣil); «عملا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «فأولئك يبدل» is resumptive, and the two objects of «يبدّل» are the two accusative nouns.

harrat-mujtaba:71-71.t: The clause «ومَنْ تاب» is resumptive; «صالحًا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «متابا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and it is a mīmī maṣdar (maṣdar mīmī).

harrat-mujtaba:72-72.t: The relative noun is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the one preceding in verse (68), and «كرامًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in «مرُّوا».

harrat-mujtaba:73-73.t: The conditional clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; «صُمًّا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in «يخرُّوا».

harrat-mujtaba:74-74.t: The clause «هب» is the response to the vocative, resumptive. The preposition «من أزواجنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «قرة», and the preposition «للمتقين» is attached to a ḥāl of «إمامًا».

harrat-mujtaba:75-75.t: The clause «أولئك يجزون» is the khabar (predicate) of «عباد» in verse (63). The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «الغرفة» is the second object; the bāʾ is a preposition, «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and the genitive maṣdar is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; «تحية» is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:76-76.t: «خالدين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) in {يُجْزَوْنَ}; the preposition «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خالدين». «مستقرًا» is a tamyīz (specification), and the [noun] specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, i.e. الغرفة. The clause «حَسُنت» is a ḥāl of {الْغُرْفَةَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:77-77.t: «ما» is negating; «ربي» is the fāʿil (agent). «لولا» is a particle of non-occurrence due to occurrence (imtināʿ li-wujūd), and «دعاؤكم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being موجود (exists). The conditional clause is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The clause «فقد كذَّبتم» is resumptive, and the clause «فسوف يكون» is conjoined to the resumptive clause; the noun of «يكون» is the pronoun of the punishment.

mekki-muskil:22-22.t:
His saying {يَوْم يرَوْنَ الْمَلَائِكَة لَا بشرى}: the governor (ʿāmil) of يَوْم is omitted, its implied form being "they will be denied the glad tidings on the day they see the angels"; لَا بشرى does not govern it, because what comes after a negation does not govern what precedes it. It is also said that the implied form is "and remember, O Muhammad, the day they see the angels". {الْملك} is a mubtadaʾ (subject), {الْحق} is its naʿt (adjective), and {للرحمن} is the khabar (predicate). Al-Zajjāj allowed الْحق in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), in which case {للرحمن} would be the khabar of {الْملك}.
His saying {حجرا}: accusative as a maṣdar.

mekki-muskil:37-37.t: His saying {وَقوم نوح}: conjoined to the pronoun in دمرناهم. It is also said that it is accusative by "remember" (اذكر), and also by an implied verb which أغرقناهم explains, i.e. "and We drowned the people of Noah; when they denied the messengers, We drowned them".

mekki-muskil:38-38.t: His saying {وعادا وَثَمُود}, and everything after it, is all conjoined to قوم نوح, if you make them accusative by an implied "remember" (اذكر), or by conjunction to the attached pronoun in دمرناهم. It is not permissible for it to be conjoined to the pronoun in جعلناهم.

mekki-muskil:39-39.t: His saying {وكلا ضربنا لَهُ الْأَمْثَال}: كلا is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "and We warned each one; We struck parables for him", because the striking of parables is the greatest of warnings, so it may serve as an explanation of "We warned" (أنذرنا).

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {بعث الله رَسُولا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is also said: as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it then means "message" (رِسَالَة).

mekki-muskil:42-42.t:
His saying {إِن كَاد ليضلنا}: its implied form according to Sībawayh is "indeed he almost led us astray" (إِنَّه كَاد ليضلنا), and according to the Kufans "he did nothing but almost lead us astray" (مَا كَاد إِلَّا يضلنا); so for them the lām means إلا and إن means مَا. According to Sībawayh it (إن) is lightened from the heavy (إنّ), and the lām is the lām of emphasis.
His saying {لَوْلَا أَن صَبرنَا}: أَن is in the position of the nominative; its explanation has already been given.

mekki-muskil:49-49.t: His saying {وأناسي كثيرا}: the singular of أناسي is إنسي. Al-Farrāʾ allowed its singular to be إنسان, its original form in his view being أناسين, after which the nūn was replaced by a yāʾ. But there is no analogy (qiyās) to support him in this; if this were permissible, then in the plural of سرحان one could say سراحي, and that is not said.

mekki-muskil:57-57.t: His saying {إِلَّا من شَاءَ أَن يتَّخذ}: من is in the position of the accusative, because it is an exception not of the same kind as the first. أَن is in the position of the accusative by شَاءَ, meaning "except whoever wills the taking (الاتخاذ)".

mekki-muskil:59-59.t: His saying {الرَّحْمَن فاسأل بِهِ خَبِيرا}: الرَّحْمَن is in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "He is the Most Merciful" (هُوَ الرَّحْمَن). It is also said that الرَّحْمَن is a mubtadaʾ and {فاسأل} is the khabar (predicate). It is also said that it is a badal (substitute) for the latent pronoun in اسْتَوَى. The genitive is permissible as a badal for الْحَيّ, and the accusative is permissible as praise (madḥ). {خَبِيرا} is accusative by His saying {فاسأل}, and it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted noun, as though He said "so ask about Him a well-informed person" (انسانا خَبِيرا). It has also been said that the Well-Informed (الْخَبِير) is Allah, there is no god but He, so the implied form would be "so ask about Him an informant who is well-informed" (مخبرا خَبِيرا). It is not good for خَبِيرا to be a ḥāl (circumstantial), because if you made it a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in فاسأل it would not be permissible, since one who is well-informed has no need to ask anyone else about anything; rather, he is the one who needs to be asked about matters because of his knowledge of them. And if you made it a ḥāl from the pronoun in بِهِ it would not be permissible, because the one asked about, namely the Most Merciful, is always Well-Informed, whereas the ḥāl is mostly for what shifts and changes. If you made it the emphatic ḥāl (al-ḥāl al-muʾakkida), which does not shift, as in {وَهُوَ الْحق مُصدقا} and {وَهَذَا صِرَاط رَبك مُسْتَقِيمًا}, it would be permissible, though there is room for consideration in it.

mekki-muskil:63-63.t:
His saying {وَعباد الرَّحْمَن الَّذين يَمْشُونَ}: عباد is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is الَّذين يَمْشُونَ. Al-Akhfash said: الَّذين يَمْشُونَ is a naʿt (adjective) of العباد and the khabar is omitted. Al-Zajjāj said: الَّذين يَمْشُونَ is a naʿt, and the khabar is أُولَئِكَ يجزون الغرفة.
His saying {قَالُوا سَلاما}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), meaning "a greeting of safety" (تَسْلِيمًا). The verb "to say" (القَوْل) was made to govern it because He did not report their exact words; He reported only the meaning of what they said. Had He reported their exact words, it would be a quoted phrase (maḥkī) and the verb "to say" would not govern it. He, exalted be His mention, only informed us that when the ignorant of Allah address these people with what they dislike, they say words of rightness (sadād); they did not answer them with the word salām itself. Sībawayh said: this is abrogated, because the verse was revealed in Mecca before they were commanded to fight. Sībawayh did not speak about anything of the abrogating and the abrogated other than this verse. So it is from al-tasallum (disassociation), not from al-taslīm (greeting). Sībawayh said: the Muslims had not been commanded at that time to greet the polytheists. So Sībawayh inferred from this that it is from al-tasallum, which is being free of evil, and not from al-taslīm, which is the greeting.

mekki-muskil:67-67.t: His saying {وَكَانَ بَين ذَلِك قواما}: the noun (ism) of كَانَ is latent in it, the implied form being "the spending was, between that, moderate" (كَانَ الانفاق بَين ذَلِك قواما), and قواما is the khabar of كَانَ. Al-Farrāʾ allowed {بَين ذَلِك} to be the ism of كَانَ while it remains with fatḥa, just as He said {وَمنا دون ذَلِك}: دون in his view is a mubtadaʾ (subject) while it has fatḥa. This is permitted only because these are words in which the use of fatḥa has become frequent, so they were left as they are in the position of the nominative. He says the same about His saying {لقد تقطع بَيْنكُم}: it is nominative by تقطع, but it was left with fatḥa because it occurs that way so often. The Basrans disagree with him on this.

mekki-muskil:69-69.t: His saying {يُضَاعف لَهُ الْعَذَاب يَوْم الْقِيَامَة ويخلد فِيهِ}: whoever reads it in the jussive (majzūm) makes it a badal (substitute) for يلق, because that is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and because meeting the penalty (لِقَاء الأثام) is the doubling of the punishment and the abiding forever; so it was substituted for it, since the meanings include one another. On this basis verbs may be substituted for one another; if their meanings differ, substituting one for another is not permissible. Whoever reads it in the nominative does so as a break (qaṭʿ, a new start) or as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:71-71.t: His saying {متابا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) carrying the sense of tawkīd (emphasis), because it comes after the wording of its own verb.

mekki-muskil:72-72.t: His saying {كراما} and {صمًّا وعميانا}: all of them are aḥwāl (circumstantial expressions).

mekki-muskil:77-77.t: His saying {فَسَوف يكون لزاما}: the noun (ism) of كَانَ is latent in it, and {لزاما} is the khabar (predicate); the implied form is "the recompense of denial will be a binding punishment". It is said this is in this world, namely the killing and capture that befell them on the day of Badr; and it is said this is in the Hereafter. Al-Farrāʾ said that in يكون there is an unspecified (majhūl, i.e. a pronoun of the matter) subject, but that is not permissible, because the majhūl is explained only by clauses, not by single words.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, the Exalted, {تبَارك}: it is تفاعل from البركة, and البركة is abundance of every good. Its meaning is "His giving is exalted", i.e. increased and became abundant. It is also said that its meaning is "His bestowal of favour is lasting and constant", and it is from برك الشيء when it is firmly fixed.
His saying {ليَكُون للْعَالمين}: the pronoun in يكون refers to the Prophet (upon him be blessing and peace); and it is said: to the Furqān.

mekki-muskil:15-15.t:
His saying {قل أذلك خير أم جنَّة الْخلد}: it is said that it refers back to His saying {إِن شَاءَ جعل لَك خيرا من ذَلِك جنَّات}; so in "Paradise" it refers back to what, had He the Exalted willed, He would have brought into being in this world; so ذلك points to the gardens and palaces mentioned in this world. It is also said that it refers back to what precedes it, the mention of the Blaze and the Fire, and the comparison between them is permissible according to what has come from the Arabs: Sībawayh reported الشَّقَاء أحب إِلَيْك أم السَّعَادَة ("Is misery dearer to you, or happiness?"). But according to the grammarians السعادة خير من الشقاء ("happiness is better than misery") is not permissible, because there is no good in misery so that comparison could occur in it. أفعل (the elative) always comes only in comparison between two things in good or evil, where in one of them there is of excellence or of evil what is not in the other, and both have excellence or evil in them, except that one of them has more excellence or evil than the other. The Kufans permitted العسل أحلى من الخل ("honey is sweeter than vinegar"), though there is no sweetness in vinegar to be compared with the sweetness of honey; the Basrans do not permit this. Nor is الْمُسلم خير من النَّصْرَانِي ("the Muslim is better than the Christian") permissible, since there is no good [Translator's note: the source has هير, evidently for خير] in the Christian; and if you said الْيَهُودِيّ خير من النَّصْرَانِي ("the Jew is better than the Christian"), it would not be permissible, since there is no good in either of them. But if you said الْيَهُودِيّ شَرّ من النَّصْرَانِي ("the Jew is worse than the Christian"), it would be permissible, since evil is present in both, and one of them may be greater in evil.
His saying {لَا بشرى يَوْمئِذٍ للمجرمين}: لا بشرى may not govern يومئذ if you make لا and بشرى like لا رجل and make it indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; rather you make يومئذ the khabar (predicate) of بشرى, because adverbs can be predicates of maṣdars (verbal nouns), and {للمجرمين} is a description of بشرى or a clarification of it. You may also make للمجرمين the khabar of بشرى and {يَوْمئِذٍ} a clarification of بشرى. If you assume that بشرى is not made indeclinable together with لا, you may make it govern يومئذ, because meanings govern adverbs.
His saying {الْملك يَوْمئِذٍ الْحق للرحمن}: you may make يومئذ accusative by الملك, so it is within its ṣila, like His saying {وَالْوَزْن يَوْمئِذٍ}. You may also make يومئذ accusative by الرحمن, assuming postponement in the adverb, its implied form being "the true dominion belongs to the Most Merciful on that day" (الْملك الْحق للرحمن يَوْمئِذٍ), i.e. the true dominion belongs to the One who on that day has mercy on His believing servants.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying {وَقَالُوا أساطير الْأَوَّلين}: they were addressing Muḥammad (peace be upon him) with that. The singular of أساطير is أسطورة; and it is said that its singular is أسطار, like أقوال and أقاويل.
His saying {ثبورا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun); and it is said to be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

mekki-muskil:7-7.t:
His saying {مَا لهَذَا الرَّسُول}: the lām occurs separated in the Muṣḥaf. The reason for that is that it was written according to the pronunciation of the one dictating, as though he used to break off his pronunciation, so the scribe wrote according to his pronunciation.
Al-Farrāʾ said: its origin is مَا بَال هَذَا ("what is the state of this one"), then بَا was dropped and the lām remained separated. It is also said that the basic rule for prepositions is that they come separated from what follows them, e.g. في, عن and على; so what consists of one letter came according to the analogy of what consists of two letters. Like it are {فَمَال هَؤُلَاءِ الْقَوْم} and {فَمَال الَّذين كفرُوا}.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t: ﴿قل أذلك خير أم جنة الخلد التي وعد المتقون كانت لهم جزاء ومصيرا﴾: قل is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is obligatorily latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت"; the hamza is interrogative; ذلك is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and خير is the khabar (predicate); أم is a conjunction; ﴿جنة الخلد﴾ is conjoined to ذلك; the relative noun is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿جنة﴾; the clause ﴿وعد المتقون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾ and has no grammatical position, and it is a verbal clause made of a verb and a nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause ﴿كانت لهم﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of ﴿جنة﴾; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally a naʿt; the noun of كانت is latent, its implied form being "هي"; جزاء is the khabar of كانت, and مصيرًا is conjoined to جزاء.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t: ﴿لهم فيها ما يشاءون خالدين كان على ربك وعدا مسئولا﴾: the clause is a second ḥāl (circumstantial) of ﴿جنة الخلد﴾; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿ما﴾ is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause يشاءون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ and has no grammatical position; خالدين is a necessary (lāzima) ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of يشاءون; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and its noun is latent, referring back to the promise understood from His words ﴿وعد المتقون﴾, or to ﴿ما يشاءون﴾; ﴿على ربك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿وعدًا﴾; and مسؤولًا is a naʿt of ﴿وعدًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿ويوم يحشرهم وما يعبدون من دون الله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿يوم﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, the implied form being "واذكر يوم يحشرهم"; the clause ﴿اذكر﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿قل أذلك خير...﴾; the clause يحشرهم is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi; ما is a relative conjoined to the hāʾ, or it is accusative (manṣūb) as an object of accompaniment (maʿiyya); the clause يعبدون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ and has no grammatical position; and ﴿من دون الله﴾ — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).

﴿فيقول أأنتم أضللتم عبادي هؤلاء أم هم ضلوا السبيل﴾: فيقول is conjoined to يحشرهم; ﴿أأنتم﴾: the hamza is interrogative, أنتم is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause أضللتم is the khabar (predicate); عبادي is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); هؤلاء is a demonstrative, a naʿt (adjective) of عبادي, or a badal (substitute) from عبادي; أم is a conjunction; ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ and the clause ضلوا is its khabar; and السبيل is an accusative (manṣūb) mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿قالوا سبحانك ما كان ينبغي لنا أن نتخذ من دونك من أولياء﴾: سبحانك is a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), made accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi; ما is negating; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the clause ينبغي is the khabar of كان; ﴿لنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينبغي﴾; أن together with what falls in its scope is the fāʿil (agent) of ينبغي; the noun of كان is latent, referring back to the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) by way of tanāzuʿ (two governors contending for one word); the fāʿil of نتخذ is latent; ﴿من دونك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted second object of نتخذ; من is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and أولياء is genitive in form and accusative in position as the first object of نتخذ — or the other way round.

﴿ولكن متعتهم وآباءهم حتى نسوا الذكر وكانوا قوما بورا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لكن is lightened (mukhaffafa) and inoperative (muhmala), for istidrāk (correction/rectification); ﴿متعتهم﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); وآباءهم: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿آباءهم﴾ is conjoined to the hāʾ, or it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); ﴿حتى﴾ is a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition; ﴿نسوا الذكر﴾ is a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿كانوا﴾: كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the wāw of the plural is its noun, قومًا is its khabar (predicate), and بورًا is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿فقد كذبوكم بما تقولون فما تستطيعون صرفا ولا نصرا﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); ﴿كذبوكم﴾: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبوكم﴾; the clause تقولون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ and has no grammatical position. ﴿فما﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction and ما is negating; تستطيعون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; صرفًا is an object; and ﴿لا نصرًا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿صرفًا﴾.

﴿ومن يظلم منكم نذقه عذابا كبيرا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; ﴿مَن﴾ is a jussive-governing conditional noun and a mubtadaʾ (subject); يظلم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being from among you, O you who are legally responsible"; نذقه is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the verb [of the condition] together with its apodosis is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿مَن﴾; the hāʾ is the first object of نذقه, عذابًا is the second object of نذقه, and كبيرًا is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿وما أرسلنا قبلك من المرسلين إلا إنهم ليأكلون الطعام ويمشون في الأسواق﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position; ما is negating; ﴿أرسلنا﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); قبلك is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿من المرسلين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿أرسلنا﴾, or to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of the object of أرسلنا, the meaning being: ﴿وما أرسلنا قبلك أحدًا من المرسلين﴾; similar to it are the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿وما منا إلا له مقام معلوم﴾, in the sense of ﴿وما منا أحد﴾; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); the clause إنهم is a ḥāl; إن is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle and ﴿هم﴾ is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the clause ﴿يأكلون الطعام﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of إن; and the clause ﴿يمشون في الأسواق﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ليأكلون الطعام﴾.

﴿وجعلنا بعضكم لبعض فتنة أتصبرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and جعلنا is conjoined to what precedes, or it is resumptive with no grammatical position; جعلنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); بعضكم is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); لبعض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of فتنة; فتنة is the second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿جعلنا﴾; the hamza is interrogative, and the meaning of the question is a command, i.e. "be patient".

﴿وكان ربك بصيرا﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or resumptive; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, ربك is its noun and بصيرًا is its khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or it is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿وقال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة أو نرى ربنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿قال الذين﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause لا يرجون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين and has no grammatical position; لقاءنا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); لولا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); أنزل is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); ﴿علينا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنزل﴾; الملائكة is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the object of their speech (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿أو﴾ is a conjunction; and the clause ﴿نرى ربنا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿أنزل علينا الملائكة﴾.

﴿لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتوا كبيرا﴾: the lām is in answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); استكبروا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿في أنفسهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿استكبروا﴾, or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); عتوا is a past verb and its fāʿil; عتوًّا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and كبيرًا is a naʿt (adjective) of it.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t: ﴿يوم يرون الملائكة لا بشرى يومئذ للمجرمين ويقولون حجرا محجورا﴾: ﴿يوم﴾ is an accusative (manṣūb) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر"; the clause ﴿يرون﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿الملائكة﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿لا بشرى﴾: لا is the lā of generic negation, and بشرى is the noun of لا; ﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of لا, and إذٍ is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied sukūn — implied because the slot is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation — in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, the tanwīn compensating for an omitted clause; ﴿للمجرمين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar of لا; the clause is the object of an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "they say: no good tidings", and the clause of saying is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the angels; ﴿يقولون﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿حجرًا﴾ is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and ﴿محجورًا﴾ is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:23-23.t: ﴿وقدمنا إلى ما عملوا من عمل فجعلناه هباء منثورا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; قدمنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿إلى ما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قدمنا﴾; the clause عملوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ and has no grammatical position; ﴿من عمل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the fāʾ is a conjunction; ﴿جعلناه﴾ is a verb, its fāʿil and the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); هباء is the second mafʿūl bihi, and منثورًا is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:24-24.t: ﴿أصحاب الجنة يومئذ خير مستقرا وأحسن مقيلا﴾: أصحاب is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and الجنة is muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خير﴾, and إذٍ is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied sukūn — implied because the slot is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation — in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, the tanwīn compensating for an omitted clause, i.e. "on the day when what was mentioned comes to pass: the withholding of good tidings, their saying حجرا محجورا, and the making of their deeds هباء منثورا"; ﴿خير﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿مستقرًّا﴾ is a tamyīz (specification); and ﴿وأحسن مقيلًا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿خير مستقرًّا﴾.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿ويوم تشقق السماء بالغمام﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿يوم﴾ is conjoined to the earlier ﴿يوم﴾ in the words of Allah the Exalted ﴿يوم يرون الملائكة﴾, i.e. "remember the day they see the angels and the day the sky is split open with the clouds"; the clause تشقق is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); السماء is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿بالغمام﴾: the bāʾ is causal, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تشقق﴾; or the bāʾ is of accompaniment (mulābasa), and the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); or the bāʾ is in the sense of عن, i.e. "from the clouds", as in His words ﴿يوم تشقق الأرض عنهم﴾, so that it is likewise attached to ﴿تشقق﴾.

﴿ونزل الملائكة تنزيلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; نزل is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); الملائكة is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and تنزيلًا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿الملك يومئذ الحق للرحمن﴾: ﴿الملك﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿الملك﴾, and إذٍ is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied sukūn — implied because the slot is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation — in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, the tanwīn compensating for an omitted clause, i.e. "on the day when the sky is split open..."; ﴿الحق﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿الملك﴾; and ﴿للرحمن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.

﴿وكان يوما على الكافرين عسيرا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; ﴿كان﴾ is a defective (nāqiṣ), abrogating (nāsikh) past verb, and its noun is a latent pronoun, the implied form being "وكان اليوم"; ﴿يومًا﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of كان; ﴿على الكافرين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿عسيرًا﴾; and ﴿عسيرًا﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿يومًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
