﴿ويوم يعض الظالم على يديه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿يوم﴾ is conjoined to the earlier ﴿يوم﴾ in the words of Allah the Exalted ﴿يوم يرون الملائكة﴾, i.e. "remember the day they see the angels, and the day the sky is split open with the clouds, and the day the wrongdoer bites his hands"; the clause ﴿يعض﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; الظالم is the fāʿil (agent) of ﴿يعض﴾; and ﴿على يديه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يعض﴾.
﴿يقول يا ليتني اتخذت مع الرسول سبيلا﴾: the clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of ﴿يعض﴾, i.e. "saying"; ﴿يا ليتني﴾: يا is a vocative particle and the one addressed is omitted, or ﴿يا﴾ is merely for drawing attention (tanbīh); ﴿ليتني﴾: ليت is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle of wishing, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the noun of ليت; the clause اتخذت is its khabar (predicate); ﴿مع الرسول﴾ is an adverb of place attached to an omitted second object of ﴿اتخذت﴾; and سبيلًا is the first object of اتخذت.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t: ﴿يا ويلتى ليتني لم أتخذ فلانا خليلا﴾: يا is a vocative particle; ﴿ويلتا﴾ is the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the first-person yāʾ, which has been turned into an alif; ﴿ليتني﴾: ليت is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle of wishing, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the noun of ليت; the clause ﴿لم أتخذ﴾ is its khabar (predicate); فلانًا is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and خليلًا is the second mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿لقد أضلني عن الذكر بعد إذ جاءني﴾: the lām is in answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); أضلني is a verb with a latent fāʿil (agent) [and the object pronoun]; ﴿عن الذكر﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أضلني﴾; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya); ﴿بعد﴾ is an adverb of time attached to ﴿أضلني﴾; ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, i.e. "after the time of its coming"; and the clause ﴿جاءني﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وكان الشيطان للإنسان خذولا﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿كان الشيطان﴾: كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and الشيطان is the noun of كان; ﴿للإنسان﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿خذولًا﴾; and خذولًا is the khabar (predicate) of كان.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t: ﴿وقال الرسول يا رب إن قومي اتخذوا هذا القرآن مهجورا﴾: conjoined to His words ﴿وقال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا﴾; ﴿قال الرسول﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); يا is a vocative particle, and رب is the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the first-person yāʾ; إن is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle, قوم is the noun of إن, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause اتخذوا is its khabar (predicate); ﴿هذا﴾ is the first object of ﴿اتخذوا﴾; القرآن is a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative; and مهجورًا is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿وكذلك جعلنا لكل نبي عدوا من المجرمين﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; ﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf is a noun in the sense of مثل, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) placed before its governor, the implied form being "جعلًا مثلَ ذلك جعلنا"; ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, the lām indicates distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; ﴿لكل نبي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿جعلنا﴾; ﴿عدوًّا﴾ is the first mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿من المجرمين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt of ﴿عدوًّا﴾.
﴿وكفى بربك هاديا ونصيرا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; كفى is a past verb; ﴿بربك﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿ربك﴾ is genitive in form and the fāʿil (agent) of كفى in position; هاديًا is a tamyīz (specification), and نصيرًا is conjoined to ﴿هاديا﴾.

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; ﴿قال الذين﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين and has no grammatical position; لولا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); نزل is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); ﴿عليه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نزل﴾; القرآن is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿جملة﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and واحدة is a naʿt (adjective).
﴿كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك ورتلناه ترتيلا﴾: ﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf is a noun in the sense of مثل, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of an implied maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasising an omitted verb, the implied sense of the speech being: "We sent it down in a sending-down like that sending-down which they disparaged and for which they proposed something different"; ﴿ذلك﴾: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, the lām indicates distance, and the kāf is a particle of address; ﴿لنثبت﴾ gives the reason for the omitted ﴿نزلناه﴾; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿نثبت﴾; the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "نحن"; فؤادك is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); رتلناه is a past verb conjoined to the omitted نزلناه; ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; and ترتيلًا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:33-33.t: ﴿ولا يأتونك بمثل إلا جئناك بالحق وأحسن تفسيرا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. لا is negating. يأتونك: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بمثل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يأتونك﴾. إلا: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿جئناك﴾: a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بالحق﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿جئناك﴾. The exception is emptied (mufarragh), [drawn] from the most general of states, so the position of the clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أحسن﴾: conjoined to ﴿الحق﴾. تفسيرًا: a tamyīz (specification).

muyesser-irab:34-34.t:
﴿الذين يحشرون على وجوههم إلى جهنم﴾: the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position. الذين: a relative noun in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are those who", or in the position of the accusative by way of censure (dhamm), i.e. "I censure those who"; or it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause ﴿أولئك شر مكانا﴾; or His words ﴿أولئك﴾ are a badal (substitute) from the relative and the khabar of the relative is His words ﴿شر مكانا﴾. The clause يحشرون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين and has no grammatical position; ﴿على وجوههم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "turned upside down onto their faces"; and ﴿إلى جهنم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يحشرون﴾.
﴿أولئك شر مكانا وأضل سبيلا﴾: أولئك: a mubtadaʾ, or a badal from ﴿الذين﴾. شر: the khabar of ﴿أولئك﴾, or the khabar of ﴿الذين﴾. مكانًا: a tamyīz (specification). ﴿وأضل سبيلًا﴾: conjoined to ﴿شر مكانًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t: ﴿ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب وجعلنا معه أخاه هارون وزيرا﴾: the wāw is resumptive; the lām is in answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); آتينا موسى is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الكتاب is the second object of ﴿آتينا﴾; the clause ﴿ولقد آتينا...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position; جعلنا is conjoined to آتينا; ﴿معه﴾ is an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted which is the second object of جعلنا; أخاه is the first object; هارون is a badal (substitute) from ﴿أخاه﴾, or a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); ﴿وزيرًا﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) — or وزيرًا is the second object, and the adverb ﴿معه﴾ is attached to something omitted that is accusative as a ḥāl.

muyesser-irab:36-36.t: ﴿فقلنا اذهبا إلى القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فدمرناهم تدميرا﴾: ﴿فقلنا﴾ is conjoined to what precedes; قلنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause اذهبا is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿إلى القوم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اذهبا﴾; الذين is a naʿt (adjective) of القوم; the clause كذبوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين and has no grammatical position; بآياتنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿كذبوا﴾; the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, i.e. "so they went to them, and they denied them both, so We destroyed them"; ﴿دمرناهم﴾ is a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and تدميرًا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:37-37.t:
﴿وقوم نوح لما كذبوا الرسل أغرقناهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; قوم نوح is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb indicated by the verb mentioned after it, i.e. "and We drowned the people of Noah", or it is conjoined to the hāʾ in دمرناهم, i.e. "and We destroyed the people of Noah"; لما is an adverb in the sense of "when" (حين), or a linking particle containing the sense of condition; كذبوا الرسل is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi; the clause أغرقناهم is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition and has no grammatical position.
﴿وجعلناهم للناس آية وأعتدنا للظالمين عذابا أليما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; جعلناهم is conjoined to what precedes; ﴿للناس﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second object of جعلناهم; آية is the first object of جعلناهم; أعتدنا is conjoined to جعلناهم; للظالمين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿أعتدنا﴾; ﴿عذابا﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi, and ﴿أليما﴾ is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:38-38.t: ﴿وعادا وثمود وأصحاب الرس وقرونا بين ذلك كثيرا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; عادًا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "أهلكنا" or "دمرنا"; ﴿ثمود وأصحاب الرس وقرونًا﴾ are conjoined to it; and كثيرًا is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قرونًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t: ﴿وكلا ضربنا له الأمثال وكلا تبرنا تتبيرا﴾: كُلًّا: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb. The clause ﴿ضربنا﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya) with no grammatical position. ضربنا: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ضربنا﴾. الأمثال: a mafʿūl bihi. كلًّا: a mafʿūl bihi fronted before ﴿تبرنا﴾. تبرنا: a verb and its fāʿil. تتبيرًا: a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:40-40.t:
﴿ولقد أتوا على القرية التي أمطرت مطر السوء﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; the lām is in answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); أتوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿على القرية﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أتوا﴾; التي is a naʿt (adjective) of القرية; the clause أمطرت is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾ and has no grammatical position; مطر: a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar); and السوء: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿أفلم يكونوا يرونها بل كانوا لا يرجون نشورا﴾: the hamza is for a question carrying the sense of disapproval (inkār); the fāʾ is a conjunction that conjoins what it enters upon to something implied that the context requires; the clause يرونها is the khabar (predicate) of يكونوا; بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the wāw of the plural is its noun, and the clause ﴿لا يرجون﴾ is its khabar; and نشورًا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:41-41.t:
﴿وإذا رأوك إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause رأوك is genitive through the adverb being annexed to it; إن is negating; يتخذونك is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and an object, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and هزوًا is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿يتخذونك﴾.
﴿أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا﴾: the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in يتخذونك, on the assumption of [an implied verb of] saying, i.e. "saying"; the hamza is interrogative; ﴿هذا﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and الذي is its khabar (predicate); the clause بعث is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي and has no grammatical position, and the referring pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. "بعثه"; the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil of ﴿بعث﴾; and ﴿رسولًا﴾ is a ḥāl of the omitted object pronoun, i.e. "as one sent".

muyesser-irab:42-42.t:
﴿إن كاد ليضلنا عن آلهتنا لولا أن صبرنا عليها﴾: إن is lightened (mukhaffafa) from the heavy [إنّ] and inoperative (muhmala); كاد: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the noun of كاد is latent, its implied form being "هو"; the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); ﴿يضلنا﴾ is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause يضلنا is the khabar (predicate) of كاد; ﴿عن آلهتنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يضلنا﴾; لولا is a particle of non-occurrence because of occurrence (imtināʿ li-wujūd), containing the sense of condition; أن together with what falls in its scope is a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿عليها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿صبرنا﴾; the khabar is omitted, i.e. "existent", and the apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, i.e. "he would have turned us away from them".
﴿وسوف يعلمون حين يرون العذاب من أضل سبيلا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; سوف is a particle of futurity; يعلمون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; حين is an adverb of time attached to ﴿يعلمون﴾; the clause يرون is in the position of the genitive through the adverb being annexed to it; مَن is interrogative and a mubtadaʾ, أضل is its khabar, and سبيلًا is a tamyīz (specification); the clause is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ﴿يعلمون﴾, which has been suspended (ʿulliqat) from governing by the interrogative.

muyesser-irab:43-43.t:
﴿أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه﴾: the hamza is interrogative; رأيت is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), i.e. "tell me"; ﴿مَن﴾ is a relative noun, the first object of رأيت; the clause اتخذ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾ and has no grammatical position; إلهه is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿اتخذ﴾, and هواه is the first mafʿūl bihi.
﴿أفأنت تكون عليه وكيلا﴾: the clause is in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿رأيت﴾; the hamza is interrogative, and the fāʾ conjoins to something implied, i.e. "you are eager for his faith"; أنت is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause ﴿تكون﴾ is its khabar (predicate); the noun of تكون is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت"; ﴿عليه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿وكيلًا﴾; and وكيلًا is the khabar of تكون.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t:
﴿أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون أو يعقلون﴾: أم: a conjunction, and it is disjoined (munqaṭiʿa), in the sense of بل together with the interrogative hamza, the implied form being "بل أتحسب ..."; the question is for disapproval (inkār); أن together with what falls in its scope stands in place of the two objects of تحسب; the clause يسمعون is the khabar (predicate) of أن; ﴿أو﴾ is a conjunction, and يعقلون is conjoined to يسمعون.
﴿إن هم إلا كالأنعام بل هم أضل سبيلا﴾: إن is negating; ﴿هم﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿كالأنعام﴾: the kāf is a noun in the sense of مثل, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as the khabar of ﴿هم﴾, and ﴿الأنعام﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿بل﴾ is a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb); ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ, أضل is its khabar, and سبيلًا is a tamyīz (specification).

muyesser-irab:45-45.t:
﴿ألم تر إلى ربك كيف مد الظل ولو شاء لجعله ساكنا﴾: the hamza is interrogative; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; ﴿تر﴾ is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾; ﴿إلى ربك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تر﴾; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause مد الظل is resumptive with no grammatical position. It has also been said that the seeing is mental (qalbiyya), the meaning being "have you not known", and ﴿كيف﴾ has suspended ﴿تر﴾ from governing, so the clause مد الظل is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ولو﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and لو is conditional; شاء is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent) is latent; the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; the clause جعله has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; the hāʾ is the first object of جعل and ساكنًا is its second object.
﴿ثم جعلنا الشمس عليه دليلا﴾: ثم is a conjunction; جعلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; الشمس is a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿عليه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, or a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿دليلا﴾; and دليلًا is the second mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:46-46.t: ﴿ثم قبضناه إلينا قبضا يسيرا﴾: ثم is a conjunction; قبضناه is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿إلينا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قبضناه﴾; قبضًا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and يسيرًا is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:47-47.t: ﴿وهو الذي جعل لكم الليل لباسا والنوم سباتا وجعل النهار نشورا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿هو﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and الذي is its khabar (predicate); the clause جعل is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي and has no grammatical position; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿لباسًا﴾; الليل is the first object of جعل and لباسًا is its second object; النوم سباتًا is conjoined to what precedes, and ﴿جعل النهار نشورًا﴾ is likewise conjoined.

muyesser-irab:48-48.t:
﴿وهو الذي أرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته﴾: ﴿هو﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and ﴿الذي﴾ is the khabar (predicate); ﴿أرسل الرياح﴾ is a verb and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent; the clause ﴿أرسل﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي and has no grammatical position; بشرًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿بين﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿بشرًا﴾, and يدي رحمته is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وأنزلنا من السماء ماء طهورا﴾: conjoined to what precedes; ﴿أنزلنا﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil; ﴿من السماء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿أنزلنا﴾; ماء is a mafʿūl bihi, and ﴿طهورا﴾ is a naʿt.

muyesser-irab:49-49.t: ﴿لنحيي به بلدة ميتا ونسقيه مما خلقنا أنعاما وأناسي كثيرا﴾: the lām of reason (taʿlīl) is a preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنزلنا﴾, to state the reason for sending it down; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿نحيي﴾; بلدة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and ميتًا is a naʿt (adjective) of بلدة; نسقيه is conjoined to نحيي; ﴿مما﴾ is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); أنعامًا is the second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿نسقيه﴾; and أناسي كثيرًا is conjoined to ﴿أنعامًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:50-50.t:
﴿ولقد صرفناه بينهم ليذكروا﴾: conjoined to what precedes; the lām is in answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); صرفناه is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the pronoun refers back to the water, or to the discourse in which the forming of clouds and the sending down of rain was mentioned; ﴿بينهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿صرفناه﴾; ﴿ليذكروا﴾: the lām is of reason (taʿlīl), and يذكروا is an imperfect verb made accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿صرفناه﴾.
﴿فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفورا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; ﴿أبى أكثر﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and كفورًا is a mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:51-51.t: ﴿ولو شئنا لبعثنا في كل قرية نذيرا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لو is conditional; شئنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the object of the willing is omitted; the lām occurs in the apodosis of ﴿لو﴾; the clause بعثنا has no grammatical position; ﴿في كل قرية﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿بعثنا﴾; and نذيرًا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:52-52.t: ﴿فلا تطع الكافرين وجاهدهم به جهادا كبيرا﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); لا is prohibitive; تطع is jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent, its implied form being "أنت"; الكافرين is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); جاهدهم is an imperative verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جاهدهم﴾, and the pronoun refers to the Quran; جهادًا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and كبيرًا is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:53-53.t:
﴿وهو الذي مرج البحرين هذا عذب فرات وهذا ملح أجاج﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the speech is conjoined to what precedes; ﴿هو﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and الذي is its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿مرج البحرين﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي and has no grammatical position; the clause ﴿هذا عذب﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position, or it is the object of an omitted verb of saying in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "it being said of them both"; ﴿هذا﴾ is a mubtadaʾ, عذب is its khabar and فرات is a second khabar; and ﴿هذا ملح أجاج﴾ is conjoined to what precedes.
﴿وجعل بينهما برزخا وحجرا محجورا﴾: conjoined to ﴿مرج﴾, falling within the scope of the ṣila; جعل is a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; ﴿بينهما﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted in the place of the second object of جعل; برزخًا is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); حجرًا محجورًا is conjoined to ﴿برزخًا﴾. It has also been said: the two are accusative by an implied verb of saying.

muyesser-irab:54-54.t:
﴿وهو الذي خلق من الماء بشرا فجعله نسبا وصهرا﴾: conjoined to what precedes; ﴿من الماء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلق﴾; بشرًا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فجعله﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and جعله is a verb, a latent fāʿil (agent) and the first mafʿūl bihi; نسبًا is the second mafʿūl bihi, and صهرًا is conjoined to ﴿نسبًا﴾.
﴿وكان ربك قديرا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ), abrogating (nāsikh) past verb, ربك is its noun and قديرًا is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:55-55.t:
﴿ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا ينفعهم ولا يضرهم﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; ﴿من دون الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿ما﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause لا ينفعهم is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ and has no grammatical position; and the clause ولا يضرهم is conjoined to the clause ﴿لا ينفعهم﴾.
﴿وكان الكافر على ربه ظهيرا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿كان الكافر﴾: كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and الكافر is the noun of كان; ﴿على ربه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿ظهيرًا﴾; and ظهيرًا is the khabar (predicate) of كان.

muyesser-irab:56-56.t: ﴿وما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا﴾: ما is negating; أرسلناك is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); مبشرًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and نذيرًا is conjoined to ﴿مبشرًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:57-57.t:
﴿قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر﴾: قل is an imperative verb; the clause ما أسألكم is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿عليه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أجر﴾ and was placed before it; من is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and أجر is genitive in form and accusative in position as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿أسألكم﴾.
﴿إلا من شاء أن يتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا﴾: إلا is a particle of exception; ﴿من شاء﴾ is a disjoined excepted (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ), because it is not of the same kind, i.e. "I do not ask you for a wage for myself, but whoever wishes to spend his wealth in the way of Allah and for His sake purely, let him do so"; أن together with what falls in its scope is the object of the wishing; ﴿إلى ربه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted second object of ﴿يتخذ﴾; and سبيلًا is the first mafʿūl bihi of ﴿يتخذ﴾.

muyesser-irab:58-58.t:
﴿وتوكل على الحي الذي لا يموت وسبح بحمده﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; توكل is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent, its implied form being "أنت"; ﴿على الحي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿توكل﴾; الذي is a naʿt (adjective); the clause ﴿لا يموت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي and has no grammatical position; سبح is conjoined to توكل; and ﴿بحمده﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "accompanied by His praise".
﴿وكفى به بذنوب عباده خبيرا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; كفى is a past verb; the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and the hāʾ is genitive in form and nominative in position as the fāʿil; بذنوب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿خبيرًا﴾; and خبيرًا is a tamyīz (specification) — it has also been said: a ḥāl.

muyesser-irab:59-59.t:
﴿الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وما بينهما في ستة أيام﴾: الذي is a naʿt (adjective), or a badal (substitute) from His word ﴿به﴾, or a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause خلق السماوات والأرض is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي and has no grammatical position; ﴿ما بينهما﴾ is conjoined to السماوات, and the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted that is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, the ṣila clause having no grammatical position; and ﴿في ستة أيام﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿خلق﴾.
﴿ثم استوى على العرش الرحمن فاسأل به خبيرا﴾: ثم is a conjunction; استوى is conjoined to خلق; ﴿على العرش﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿استوى﴾; الرحمن is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿الذي﴾, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is the Most Merciful"; ﴿فاسأل﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), and اسأل is an imperative verb; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿خبيرًا﴾, and خبيرًا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); or the bāʾ is in the sense of عن, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to His word ﴿فاسأل﴾.

muyesser-irab:60-60.t:
﴿وإذا قيل لهم اسجدوا للرحمن﴾: the wāw is resumptive; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause ﴿قيل﴾ is genitive through the adverb being annexed to it; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قيل﴾; and the clause اسجدوا للرحمن is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿قالوا وما الرحمن﴾: قالوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿قالوا﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition and has no grammatical position; the wāw is connective (ṣila); ﴿ما﴾ is an interrogative noun and a mubtadaʾ (subject), and الرحمن is the khabar (predicate). The clause ﴿وإذا قيل لهم...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿أنسجد لما تأمرنا وزادهم نفورا﴾: the hamza is interrogative; نسجد is an imperfect verb, and its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "نحن"; ﴿لما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿نسجد﴾; the clause ﴿تأمرنا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ and has no grammatical position; زادهم is a verb and a fāʿil referring back to the saying; the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and نفورًا is a second mafʿūl bihi, or a tamyīz (specification).

muyesser-irab:61-61.t: ﴿تبارك الذي جعل في السماء بروجا وجعل فيها سراجا وقمرا منيرا﴾: تبارك is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb, and الذي is its fāʿil (agent); the clause جعل is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي and has no grammatical position; ﴿في السماء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جعل﴾, or attached to an omitted second object; بروجًا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and what comes after it is conjoined to it.

muyesser-irab:62-62.t: ﴿وهو الذي جعل الليل والنهار خلفة لمن أراد أن يذكر أو أراد شكورا﴾: speech conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿هو﴾ is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and الذي is its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿جعل الليل والنهار﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي and has no grammatical position; خلفة is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of جعل if it is in the sense of "made into" (صيّر), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) if it is in the sense of "created" (خلق) — and it has been said that a muḍāf must be supplied, i.e. "possessors of succession"; ﴿لمن﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of خلفة; the clause أراد is the ṣila of ﴿مَن﴾ and has no grammatical position; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ﴿أن يذكر﴾ is accusative as the object of ﴿أراد﴾, and the object of يذكر is omitted, i.e. "what he missed in one of them"; ﴿أو﴾ is a conjunction, and أراد شكورًا is conjoined to the first أراد.

muyesser-irab:63-63.t:
﴿وعباد الرحمن الذين يمشون على الأرض هونا﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; عباد is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and الرحمن is muḍāf ilayhi; what follows it are naʿts (adjectives), and the khabar (predicate) of عباد is at the end of the surah, namely the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿أؤلئك يجزون الغرفة﴾; [or] الذين is the khabar of عباد, or a naʿt; the clause يمشون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين and has no grammatical position; على الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يمشون﴾; هونًا is a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "gently", or it is a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a description of the maṣdar, i.e. "a gentle walking".
﴿وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it, so it falls within the scope of the ṣila and has no grammatical position; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause خاطبهم الجاهلون is in the position of the genitive through the adverb being annexed to it; the clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; سلامًا: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, the implied form being "نسلم سلاما".

muyesser-irab:64-64.t: ﴿والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; الذين is conjoined to the first relative; the clause يبيتون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين and has no grammatical position; the wāw is the noun of يبيتون; ﴿لربهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سجدًا﴾; سجدًا is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿يبيتون﴾, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) if it is taken as complete (tāmma); and قياما is conjoined to ﴿سجدًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:65-65.t:
﴿والذين يقولون ربنا اصرف عنا عذاب جهنم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الذين is likewise conjoined; the clause يقولون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين and has no grammatical position; ربنا is an annexed (muḍāf) one addressed (munādā) from which the vocative particle has been omitted; اصرف is a verb of supplication (duʿāʾ); عذاب جهنم is the object of اصرف; and the clause is the object of the speech (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿إن عذابها كان غراما﴾: the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position; إن is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle and عذابها is its noun; the clause كان is the khabar (predicate) of إن; the noun of كان is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; and غرامًا is the khabar of كان.

muyesser-irab:66-66.t: ﴿إنها ساءت مستقرا ومقاما﴾: إن: an abrogating (nāsikh) particle, and ﴿ها﴾ is its noun. The clause ﴿ساءت﴾ is its khabar (predicate). ساءت: an inflexible (jāmid) past verb, the tāʾ is for the feminine, and the fāʿil (agent) of ساءت is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هي". مستقرًّا: a tamyīz (specification). مقامًا: conjoined to ﴿مستقرًّا﴾. The one specifically blamed (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted. The clause ﴿إنها ساءت...﴾ is causal (taʿlīliyya).

muyesser-irab:67-67.t:
﴿والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الذين is conjoined to what precedes; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause أنفقوا is in the position of the genitive through the adverb being annexed to it; and the clause ﴿لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
﴿وكان بين ذلك قواما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); كان is a defective (nāqiṣ), abrogating (nāsikh) past verb, and its noun is a latent pronoun, i.e. "and the spending was"; ﴿بين﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قوامًا﴾; ﴿ذلك﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi; and قوامًا is the khabar (predicate) of كان. Or ﴿بين ذلك﴾ is an adverb attached to the omitted khabar of كان, and قواما is the ḥāl.

muyesser-irab:68-68.t:
﴿والذين لا يدعون مع الله إلها آخر﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الذين is likewise conjoined to what precedes; the clause لا يدعون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين and has no grammatical position; ﴿مع الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يدعون﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; مع is an adverb, not a preposition]; إلهًا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and آخر is a naʿt (adjective).
﴿ولا يقتلون النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق ولا يزنون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ولا يقتلون is conjoined to ﴿ولا يدعون﴾; النفس is a mafʿūl bihi; التي is a naʿt; the clause حرم الله is the ṣila of ﴿التي﴾ and has no grammatical position; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿بالحق﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يقتلون﴾, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), so that the exception is from the most general of states, i.e. "except when deserving [it]"; and ﴿ولا يزنون﴾ is conjoined.
﴿ومن يفعل ذلك يلق أثاما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿مَن﴾ is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); يفعل is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; and أثامًا is a mafʿūl bihi. [Translator's note: the source does not parse ذلك or يلق (the apodosis) here.]

muyesser-irab:69-69.t: ﴿يضاعف له العذاب يوم القيامة ويخلد فيه مهانا﴾: يضاعف is a badal (substitute) from يلق, because the two have one meaning; ﴿له﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يضاعف﴾; العذاب is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); يوم القيامة is an adverb also attached to ﴿يضاعف﴾; يخلد is conjoined to يضاعف; ﴿فيه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يخلد﴾; and مهانًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of يخلد.

muyesser-irab:70-70.t:
﴿إلا من تاب وآمن وعمل عملا صالحا﴾: إلا is a particle of exception; من is an exception from the same kind (muttaṣil), in the position of the accusative; the clause تاب is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾ and has no grammatical position; آمن is conjoined to تاب, and likewise عمل; عملًا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and صالحًا is a naʿt (adjective).
﴿فأولئك يبدل الله سيئاتهم حسنات﴾: the fāʾ is linking, because of the scent of condition in the relative; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the reference being to the relative, namely من; the clause يبدل is the khabar (predicate) of أولئك; the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil (agent); سيئاتهم is an object; and حسنات is a second object of يبدل, or accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). ﴿وكان الله غفورا رحيما﴾: the wāw is resumptive; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the Name of Majesty is its noun; غفورًا is its first khabar and رحيمًا its second khabar; and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:71-71.t: ﴿ومن تاب وعمل صالحا فإنه يتوب إلى الله متابا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; ﴿مَن﴾ is a jussive-governing conditional noun and a mubtadaʾ (subject); تاب is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); عمل is conjoined to تاب; صالحًا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿عمل﴾, or a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a description of the maṣdar, i.e. "he did a righteous deed". ﴿فإنه﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis, because it is a nominal clause; إن is an abrogating (nāsikh) particle, the hāʾ is its noun, and the clause يتوب is its khabar (predicate); إلى الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يتوب﴾; متابًا is a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq because it is a mīm-maṣdar (maṣdar mīmī); and the clause ﴿ومن تاب وعمل...﴾ is conjoined, or resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:72-72.t:
﴿والذين لا يشهدون الزور﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الذين is conjoined to the preceding relatives; the clause لا يشهدون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين and has no grammatical position; الزور is accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and الزور is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). [Translator's note: the source gives both analyses back to back without «or»; they are presumably meant as alternatives.]
﴿وإذا مروا باللغو مروا كراما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause مروا is genitive through the adverb being annexed to it; مروا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿باللغو﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مروا﴾; the second clause مروا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; and كرامًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:73-73.t: ﴿والذين إذا ذكروا بآيات ربهم لم يخروا عليها صما وعميانا﴾: the clause لم يخروا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; ﴿عليها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يخروا﴾; صمًّا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and عميانًا is a second ḥāl.

muyesser-irab:74-74.t: ﴿والذين يقولون ربنا هب لنا من أزواجنا وذرياتنا قرة أعين واجعلنا للمتقين إماما﴾: conjoined to what precedes; ربنا is an annexed (muḍāf) one addressed (munādā) from which the vocative particle has been omitted; هب is a verb of supplication (duʿāʾ); ﴿لنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿هب﴾; ﴿من أزواجنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); قرة أعين is the object of هب; اجعلنا is a verb of supplication, its fāʿil (agent) is latent, and [the pronoun is] the first object; ﴿للمتقين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿إمامًا﴾; and إماما is the second object.

muyesser-irab:75-75.t: ﴿أولئك يجزون الغرفة بما صبروا ويلقون فيها تحية وسلاما﴾: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of المتقين, or the khabar (predicate) of ﴿عباد الرحمن﴾ according to one of the two views; أولئك is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause يجزون الغرفة is its khabar; الغرفة is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿يجزون﴾, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), which is the first object; ﴿بما﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يجزون﴾, ما is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar), and the bāʾ is causal; ﴿يلقون﴾ is conjoined to يجزون; ﴿فيها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿تحية﴾ is the second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿يلقون﴾, because it is built for that whose agent is not named (passive), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; and ﴿سلامًا﴾ is conjoined to تحية.

muyesser-irab:76-76.t: ﴿خالدين فيها حسنت مستقرا ومقاما﴾: خالدين is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿فيها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خالدين﴾; حسنت is a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent, referring back to الغرفة; مستقرًّا is a tamyīz (specification), and مقامًا is conjoined to ﴿مستقرًا﴾; and the clause ﴿حسنت﴾ is a second ḥāl of الغرفة.

muyesser-irab:77-77.t:
﴿قل ما يعبأ بكم ربي لولا دعاؤكم﴾: ﴿قل﴾ is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent, its implied form being "أنت"; ﴿ما﴾ is negating; ﴿يعبأ﴾ is an imperfect verb; ﴿بكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يعبأ﴾; ﴿ربي﴾ is the fāʿil; ﴿لولا﴾ is a particle of non-occurrence because of occurrence (imtināʿ li-wujūd); ﴿دعاؤكم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is obligatorily omitted; and the apodosis of لولا is omitted, understood from the context, i.e. "were it not for your supplication, He would not have cared for you".
﴿فقد كذبتم فسوف يكون لزاما﴾: ﴿فقد﴾: the fāʾ is for resumption and for giving the reason why they are not cared for; قد: a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); ﴿كذبتم﴾ is a past verb, and the attached second-person plural pronoun is in the position of the nominative as fāʿil; the clause ﴿فقد كذبتم﴾ is resumptive and causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position; ﴿فسوف﴾: the fāʾ is for consequence (tafrīʿ), and سوف is a particle of futurity; ﴿يكون﴾ is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, and the noun of يكون is latent, its implied form being "هو"; ﴿لزامًا﴾ is the khabar of يكون; and the clause ﴿سوف يكون لزاما﴾ is conjoined to ﴿فقد كذبتم﴾.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿تبارك الذي نزل الفرقان على عبده ليكون للعالمين نذيرا﴾: (تبارك) is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb, and (الذي) is its fāʿil (agent); the clause (نزل الفرقان) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذي) and has no grammatical position; (على عبده) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نزل﴾; the lām is causal (li-l-taʿlīl); (يكون) is a defective imperfect verb (of kāna and its sisters) in the subjunctive by an implied (أن) after the causal lām; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from (أن) and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿نزل﴾; ﴿للعالمين﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نذيرا﴾; the noun of (يكون) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); and (نذيرًا) is the khabar (predicate) of (يكون).

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض ولم يتخذ ولدا﴾: (الذي) is a badal (substitute) for the first relative noun, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or accusative as praise (ʿalā al-madḥ), and what follows it completes the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun; ﴿له﴾ is a khabar placed first; (ملك السماوات والأرض) is a mubtadaʾ placed after; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun and has no grammatical position; and (لم يتخذ ولدًا) is conjoined to what preceded.
﴿ولم يكن له شريك في الملك وخلق كل شيء فقدره تقديرا﴾: conjoined to what preceded; ﴿له﴾ is the khabar of (يكن), placed first; (شريك) is its noun placed after; (في الملك) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (شريك); (خلق) is also conjoined to what preceded; (كل شئ) is the object of (خلق); (فقدره): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (قدره) is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (تقديرًا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿واتخذوا من دونه آلهة لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون﴾: the wāw is resumptive; ﴿من دونه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second object of ﴿اتخذوا﴾; (آلهة) is the first object of (اتخذوا); the clause ﴿واتخذوا من دونه آلهة﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position; and the clause ﴿لا يخلقون شيئًا﴾ is an adjective (naʿt) of (آلهة). ﴿وهم يخلقون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject); and (يخلقون), built for that whose agent is not named (passive), is the khabar (predicate).
﴿ولا يملكون لأنفسهم ضرا ولا نفعا ولا يملكون موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿لا يملكون﴾ is a clause conjoined to what preceded; (لأنفسهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يملكون﴾; (ضرًّا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿لا نفعًا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ضرًّا﴾. ﴿ولا يملكون موتًا﴾: (لا) is connective (ṣila), for emphasising the negation; ﴿ولا يملكون موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا﴾ is like ﴿ولا يملكون ضرا ولا نفعا﴾.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿وقال الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا إفك افتراه﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; (الذين) is the fāʿil (agent) of (قال); the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين) and has no grammatical position; (إن) is negative; (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (إفك) is the khabar (predicate) of (هذا); and the clause (افتراه) is an adjective (naʿt) of (إفك).
﴿وأعانه عليه قوم آخرون فقد جاءوا ظلما وزورا﴾: ﴿أعانه﴾ is conjoined to ﴿افتراه﴾; (عليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعانه﴾, and the pronoun refers to the fabricated falsehood; (قوم) is the fāʿil, and (آخرون) is an adjective of (قوم); the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the "disclosing" fāʾ); (قد) is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (جاءوا) is a verb and its fāʿil; it has been made to carry the meaning of (another) verb (فعل) and so has been made transitive as that verb is, and (ظلمًا) is its object; or it — that is, the verb — keeps its own meaning and is not transitive, and (ظلمًا) is accusative by removal of the preposition, or accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) to be interpreted (muʾawwala), i.e.: wrongdoers (ظالمين); and (زورًا) is conjoined to ﴿ظلمًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t: ﴿وقالوا أساطير الأولين اكتتبها فهي تملى عليه بكرة وأصيلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (قالوا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿أساطير الأولين﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ﴿اكتتبها﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; or (أساطير الأولين) is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (اكتتبها) is the khabar. ﴿فهي﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; ﴿هي﴾ is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (تملى) is the khabar, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); (عليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تملى﴾; (بكرة) is an adverb attached to ﴿تملى﴾; and (أصيلًا) is conjoined to (بكرة).

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿قل أنزله الذي يعلم السر في السماوات والأرض﴾: (قل) is an imperative verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you" (أنت); the clause (أنزله) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الذي) is the fāʿil; the clause (يعلم السر) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun and has no grammatical position; and ﴿في السماوات والأرض﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿إنه كان غفورا رحيما﴾: (إن) is an abrogating particle (of inna and its sisters), and the hāʾ is its noun; the clause ﴿كان...﴾ is its khabar (predicate); (كان) is a defective, abrogating past verb (of kāna and its sisters), and its noun is latent; (غفورا) is a first khabar of ﴿كان﴾, and (رحيمًا) is its second khabar; and it is a clause with no grammatical position, because it is causal (taʿlīliyya).

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿وقالوا مال هذا الرسول يأكل الطعام ويمشي في الأسواق﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; (قالوا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (ما) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿لهذا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar (predicate); (الرسول) is a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative; the clause ﴿يأكل الطعام﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; ﴿يأكل الطعام﴾ is a verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause ﴿يمشي في الأسواق﴾ is conjoined to it.
﴿لولا أنزل إليه ملك فيكون معه نذيرا﴾: (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); (أنزل) is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); ﴿إليه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أنزل﴾; (ملك) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (al-sababiyya); (يكون) is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied (أن) after the fāʾ of causation, because it is the answer to the urging; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from (أن) and the verb is conjoined to a maṣdar understood from the preceding speech, i.e.: why was there not the sending down of an angel, and so its being a warner with him (هلا كان نزول ملك فكونه معه نذيرا). The noun of (يكون) is latent, its implied form being ﴿هو﴾, i.e.: the angel; (معه) is an adverb of place attached to an omitted ḥāl; and (نذيرًا) is the khabar of (يكون).

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿أو يلقى إليه كنز أو تكون له جنة يأكل منها﴾: (أو) is a conjunction; (يلقى) is an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); (كنز) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (إليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يلقى﴾. ﴿أو تكون له جنة﴾ is conjoined to what preceded; the clause ﴿يأكل منها﴾ is an adjective (naʿt) of (جنة); and these two verbs are conjoined to (أنزل).
﴿وقال الظالمون إن تتبعون إلا رجلا مسحورا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿قال الظالمون﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (إن) is negative; (تتبعون) is an imperfect verb and its agent; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (رجلًا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (مسحورًا) is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t: ﴿انظر كيف ضربوا لك الأمثال فضلوا فلا يستطيعون سبيلا﴾: ﴿انظر﴾ is an imperative verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), its implied form being "you" (أنت); (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿لك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ضربوا﴾; and (الأمثال) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فضلوا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (ضلوا) is a past verb and its agent. ﴿فلا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; and ﴿يستطيعون سبيلًا﴾ is an imperfect verb, its agent and its direct object.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿تبارك الذي إن شاء جعل لك خيرا من ذلك﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; ﴿تبارك الذي﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); it has also been said that it is on the supposition of an omitted muḍāf, i.e.: the good of the One who (خير الذي); (إن) is conditional; (شاء) is a past verb in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (جعل) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the conditional sentence is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun and has no grammatical position; ﴿لك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second object of (جعل); (خيرًا) is the first object of (جعل); and ﴿من ذلك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خيرًا﴾.
﴿جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ويجعل لك قصورا﴾: (جنات) is a badal (substitute) for ﴿خيرًا﴾; the clause (تجري) is an adjective (naʿt) of (جنات); ﴿من تحتها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تجري﴾; (الأنهار) is the fāʿil of (تجري); (يجعل) is an imperfect verb conjoined to the position of (جعل), which occurs as the apodosis; ﴿لك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second object of (جعل); and (قصورًا) is the first object.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t: ﴿بل كذبوا بالساعة وأعتدنا لمن كذب بالساعة سعيرا﴾: (بل) is a particle of turning away (iḍrāb); (كذبوا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (بالساعة) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبوا﴾; ﴿أعتدنا﴾ is a verb and its agent; (لمن) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أعتدنا﴾; the clause ﴿كذب بالساعة﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾ and has no grammatical position; and ﴿سعيرًا﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:12-12.t: ﴿إذا رأتهم من مكان بعيد سمعوا لها تغيظا وزفيرا﴾: the conditional sentence is in the position of the accusative as an adjective (naʿt) of ﴿سعيرًا﴾, because it is feminine in the sense of "the Fire"; (إذا) is a future adverb carrying the meaning of a condition; the clause ﴿رأتهم﴾ is in the position of the genitive because (إذا) is annexed to it; ﴿من مكان﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause ﴿سمعوا﴾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); ﴿لها﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective; (تغيظًا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (زفيرًا) is conjoined to it.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وإذا ألقوا منها مكانا ضيقا مقرنين دعوا هنالك ثبورا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (إذا) is a future adverb carrying the meaning of a condition; the clause ﴿ألقوا﴾ is genitive because the adverb is annexed to it, and (the adverb) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis, which is ﴿دعوا﴾; ﴿ألقوا﴾ is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (منها) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of ﴿مكانًا﴾, because it was originally an adjective (naʿt) of it; (مكانًا) is an adverb attached to ﴿ألقوا﴾; (ضيقًا) is an adjective of ﴿مكانًا﴾; (مقرنين) is a ḥāl of the wāw in ﴿ألقوا﴾; the clause (دعوا) has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) of (دعوا); (هنالك) is a demonstrative in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, and it is attached to ﴿دَعَوا﴾; and ﴿ثبورًا﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿دعوا﴾, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, the implied form being: we have perished utterly (ثبرنا ثبورا).

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿لا تدعوا اليوم ثبورا واحدا وادعوا ثبورا كثيرا﴾: the clause is the object of an omitted saying (maqūl al-qawl), its implied form being: and it will be said to them (فيقال لهم), and this omitted element is conjoined to what precedes it; (لا) is the lā of prohibition; ﴿تدعوا﴾ is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) of (تدعوا); ﴿ثبورًا﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿واحدا﴾ is an adjective (naʿt); (ادعوا) is an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; ﴿ثبورا﴾ is the direct object, or an absolute object; and (كثيرًا) is an adjective of ﴿ثبورًا﴾.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: «تَبارَكَ»: the experts in the language have spoken about its meaning. Al-Farrāʾ said: in Arabic it and تقدّس ("He is hallowed") are one and the same, and both express majesty. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: it is the form tafāʿala from al-baraka ("blessing"). He said: the meaning of al-baraka is abundance of everything good. It has been said: تبارك means "He is exalted" (تعالى); and it has been said: the meaning is "His giving is exalted", i.e. it has increased and become abundant; and it has been said: the meaning is "His favours have endured and remained firm". This last is the most fitting of them in the language, the derivation being from برك الشيء ("the thing stayed firm"), and from it برك الجمل ("the camel knelt down [and stayed]"). As for the first view, it is muddled, because التقديس comes only from purity, and this has nothing to do with that. «الَّذِي نَزَّلَ الْفُرْقانَ» is in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) by its verb. «الفرقان» is the Qur'an, because it distinguishes (farraqa) between truth and falsehood, and between the believer and the unbeliever. «عَلى عَبْدِهِ»: so that [the pronoun in «ليكون»] refers to him; it may also refer to «الفرقان». One says أنذر ("he warned") when he caused fear, and «نذير» is for intensiveness.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
«الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of, or a badal (substitute) for, the «الذي» before it.
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «فَقَدْ جاؤُ ظُلْماً», i.e. "with wrongdoing" (بظلم). Someone else said: [it means] "they have brought wrongdoing and falsehood".

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: «وَقالُوا أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ»: on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "and they said: what you have brought is the tales of the ancients". Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: its singular is أسطورة, like أحدوثة and أحاديث. Someone else said: «أساطير» is the plural of أسطار, like أقوال and أقاويل. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, that the one who said this was al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, and likewise everything in the Qur'an in which the tales (al-asāṭīr) are mentioned. Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: he used to harm the Prophet ﷺ. «اكْتَتَبَها فَهِيَ تُمْلى عَلَيْهِ»: according to the dialect of those who say أملى; those who say أملّ say تملّ عليه. «بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا».

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: «وَقالُوا مالِ هذَا الرَّسُولِ»: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «ما» is separate. The meaning is: what is the matter with this messenger in his walking and his eating? «لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ», i.e. "why not" (هلّا). «فَيَكُونَ مَعَهُ نَذِيراً» is the answer to the question.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: «أَوْ يُلْقى» is in the position of the nominative, and the meaning is: "or why is a treasure not cast down to him", or "why does he not have" «تَكُونُ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ يَأْكُلُ مِنْها»: this is the reading of the Medinans, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. The Kufans read «نَأْكُلَ مِنْها» with nūn. Both readings are good and convey two meanings, though the reading with yāʾ is clearer, because the Prophet ﷺ alone has been mentioned before, so that the pronoun referring back to him is clearer.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: «انْظُرْ كَيْفَ ضَرَبُوا لَكَ الْأَمْثالَ», i.e. they struck these comparisons for you so as to arrive at calling you a liar, «فَضَلُّوا» from the path of truth and from attaining what they wanted, «فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلًا», i.e. [a way] to making good what they said about you.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: «تَبارَكَ الَّذِي إِنْ شاءَ جَعَلَ لَكَ خَيْراً مِنْ ذلِكَ»: a condition and its requital. It is not assimilated [i.e. the lām of «جعل» into the lām of «لك»] because the two words are separate, though assimilation is permissible because two identical letters meet. «وَيَجْعَلْ لَكَ قُصُوراً» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm), conjoined to the position of «جعل»; it may also be in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the first two, and then assimilated. Al-Farrāʾ permitted the accusative on the basis of al-ṣarf ("diversion"). The people of Syria read — and it is also related from ʿĀṣim — «وَيَجْعَلْ لَكَ قُصُوراً» with the nominative, i.e. "and He will make for you palaces in the Hereafter".

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «ثُبُوراً» is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "we have perished a perishing" (ثبرنا ثبورا). Someone else said: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "they called on destruction", just as one says يا عجباه ("O wonder!"), i.e. "this is your time, so be present", and this is more eloquent than تعجّبت ("I was amazed").

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: I.e. your affliction is greater than that you should call on destruction just once; rather they will call on it many times. «الثبور» is not put in the plural because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
Just as Sībawayh relates from the Arabs: الشّقاء أحبّ إليك أم السعادة؟ ("Is misery dearer to you, or happiness?"), when it is known that happiness is dearer to him. It has been said: this is for drawing attention; and it has been said: the meaning is "is that good?" without the sense of «من» [i.e. not as a comparative], just as one says عنده خير ("he has good"). This is a good view, as [the poet] said: [al-wāfir] 309-
فشرّكما لخيركما الفداء
(So the worse of you two is a ransom for the better of you two.)
There is a third view on the verse, namely that the Kufans permit العسل أحلى من الخل ("honey is sweeter than vinegar"). This view is rejected, because the meaning of "so-and-so is better than so-and-so" is that he has more good than him, and there is no sweetness in vinegar. Nor may you say "the Christian is better than the Jew", because there is no good in either of them so that one of them should exceed the other in good; rather one says "the Jew is worse than the Christian". This is how the speech of the Arabs goes.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: Al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar read «أن نتّخذ» with ḍamma on the nūn [i.e. أن نُتَّخَذ, "that we be taken"]. The grammarians have discussed this reading and agreed that the fatḥa on the nūn is preferable. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar said: (نُتّخذ) is not permissible. Abū ʿAmr said: had it been «نُتّخذ», the second (من) would have been dropped, and you would say: أن نُتّخذ من دونك أولياء. That one such as Abū ʿAmr, with his eminence and standing, should say this is to be appreciated, because he has brought a clear reason. The explanation of what he said is that one says ما اتّخذت رجلا وليّا ("I did not take a man as a protector"), and this may apply to one particular individual; then one says ما اتخذت من رجل وليّا ("I did not take any man as a protector"), and it is a general negation. Your word «وليّا» follows what precedes it, so «من» may not enter it, because there is no point in that. Al-Farrāʾ related from the Arabs that they do not say ما رأيت عبد الله من رجل, but he then invalidated this, abandoned what he had related from the Arabs, and permitted it on his own account, saying: if they meant ما رأيت من رجل عبد الله, it would be permissible to insert «من», interpreting it as an inversion (al-qalb). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: this is a mistake and is not permissible at all — and it is as he said. Then al-Farrāʾ went back and said: the Arabs insert «من» only before nouns — and this is a clear contradiction. Al-Kisāʾī also permitted it, then said: it is ugly. «وَلكِنْ مَتَّعْتَهُمْ وَآباءَهُمْ», i.e. their lives grew long after the death of the messengers, Allah's blessings be upon them, so they forgot and perished.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: «فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوكُمْ بِما تَقُولُونَ»: Abū ʿUbayd interpreted it in the sense of "in what they say". Someone else said: this is an address to the prophets, Allah bless them and grant them peace. «فما تستطيعون صرفا ولا نصرا»: it has been said: they are not able to turn the punishment away from themselves, nor to help one another.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
When the lām enters, «إنّ» can only have kasra; and even if there were no lām, only kasra would be permissible, because it begins a new clause. This is the view of all the grammarians, except that ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān related to us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] that he said: fatḥa is permissible in this «إنّ» even though the lām comes after it — and I think that was an error on his part. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning is "We did not send before you messengers except that they ate food"; then «من» was omitted, because «من» indicates what is omitted. Al-Farrāʾ said: «من» is omitted, i.e. "except that among them there were those who ate food", and he compared it to His saying «وَما مِنَّا إِلَّا لَهُ مَقامٌ مَعْلُومٌ» [al-Ṣāffāt: 164].
Abū Isḥāq said: this is a mistake, because «من» is a relative (mawṣūla), so it may not be omitted. «وَجَعَلْنا بَعْضَكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ فِتْنَةً»: al-fitna in the language is testing, and in the hadith: "The rich man is a trial for the poor and the poor a trial for the rich; the strong is a trial for the weak and the weak a trial for the strong." The meaning of this is that each of the two is tested by his companion: the rich man is tested by the poor — he must console him and not mock him — and the poor man is tried by the rich — he must not envy him and must take from him only what he gives him — and each of them must be patient upon the truth, as al-Ḍaḥḥāk said on the meaning of «أَتَصْبِرُونَ»: i.e. upon the truth. «وَكانَ رَبُّكَ بَصِيراً», i.e. of what you do, i.e. in that with which He tried you.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
«يوم يرون» may not be accusative by «بشرى», because what is in the predicate of wonder or in the predicate of negation does not govern what precedes it. But there are two possible constructions here: the meaning may be "they are denied the good tidings on the day they see the angels", what follows indicating this omission; or the construction may be "there will be no good tidings «يوم يرون الملائكة»", with «يومئذ» as tawkīd (emphasis). It may also be that the meaning is "remember the day they see the angels".
«وَيَقُولُونَ حِجْراً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a prohibition"; from it comes حجرت على فلان ("I placed so-and-so under restriction"), and from it حجرة ("room") was said.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: I.e. it is of no benefit, i.e. We have made it void. «هباء» is not one of the words with hamza [as a root letter]; it was given a hamza only because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The diminutive is هبيّ in the position of the nominative, and among the grammarians there are some who say هبيّ in the position of the nominative. [Translator's note: translated as printed; the two forms are identical in the text as transmitted, so the difference between the two views appears to have been lost in the source.]

nahhas-irab:24-24.t:
«أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُسْتَقَرًّا» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and a khabar (predicate). We have mentioned something like it before this, in «أَذلِكَ خَيْرٌ أَمْ جَنَّةُ الْخُلْدِ» [al-Furqān: 15], and we related the view of the Kufans that they permit العسل أحلى من الخلّ ("honey is sweeter than vinegar"). Al-Farrāʾ mentioned on this verse more than this: he claimed that the meaning is:
"The companions of the Garden on that day are better in abode than the people of the Fire", while there is no good in the abode of the people of the Fire — so it is as if he refuted himself. I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say on this, relating it, that the meaning is: since you used to do the deeds of the people of the Fire, you became as though you were saying that there is good in that. It has been said: better in abode than what you are in; and it has been said: «خير» not in the sense of afʿal [the comparative], with «مستقرّ» then being an adverb (ẓarf); on what preceded, it is accusative as an explanation (bayān, i.e. tamyīz).

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: «وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ السَّماءُ بِالْغَمامِ»: the original form is تتشقّق; the tāʾ was assimilated into the shīn. The Kufans read «تَشَقَّقُ» [with a single shīn]: they omitted the tāʾ because the remaining tāʾ indicates it.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: «الْمُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْحَقُّ لِلرَّحْمنِ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and a khabar (predicate). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] permitted the accusative of «الحقّ» in the sense of "I affirm the truth" or "I mean the truth". «وَكانَ يَوْماً عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ عَسِيراً»: its verb is عسر يعسر and عسر يعسر.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: «وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ الظَّالِمُ عَلى يَدَيْهِ»: the past tense is عضضت, and al-Kisāʾī related عضَضت with fatḥa on the first ḍād. Authoritative report has come from the people of exegesis, among them Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, that the wrongdoer here is ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ and that his close friend is Umayya ibn Khalaf. ʿUqba was killed by ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and Umayya was killed by the Prophet ﷺ. This was one of the proofs of the Prophet ﷺ, because he gave news of the two of them with this, and they were killed in unbelief. They are not named in the verse because that is more effective in conveying the lesson, so that it be known that this is the way of every wrongdoer who accepts from another [a call] to disobey Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
«يا وَيْلَتى»: al-Ḥasan read «يا ويلتي» with yāʾ. The first reading is more common in the speech of the Arabs, because they omit when they say يا غلام أقبل ("O boy, come forward"), since the vocative is a place of omission. Al-Aṣmaʿī used to recite Zuhayr's verse: [al-ṭawīl] 310-
تبصّر خليل هل ترى من ظعائن ... تحمّلن بالعلياء من فوق جرثم
(Look, O friend: do you see any women in litters who have loaded up on the heights above Jurthum?)
and he rejected the version of those who relate «تبصّر خليلي», because he aimed at the sound, eloquent versions and did not turn aside to the irregular. Likewise the experts of the language relate: [al-basīṭ] 311-
قالت هريرة لمّا جئت زائرها ... ويلا عليك وويلا منك يا رجل
(Hurayra said, when I came to visit her: "Woe upon you, and woe from you, O man!")

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: «الْقُرْآنَ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «هذا», because «هذا» is qualified by what has the alif and lām, even if it is not formed from a verb. «مَهْجُوراً» is a second object.

nahhas-irab:31-32.t: «وَكَذلِكَ جَعَلْنا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوًّا»: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); likewise the kāf in «كَذلِكَ لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِ فُؤادَكَ», the meaning being "a strengthening like that strengthening". This is on the basis that the complete stop is at His saying, Mighty and Majestic, «جُمْلَةً واحِدَةً»; if the complete stop is at «كذلك», the construction is "a measured recitation like that". This is because, when the idolaters found no way to call the Prophet ﷺ a liar by any proof or argument, they said «لَوْلا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الْقُرْآنُ جُمْلَةً واحِدَةً», so they asked for something in which the right course lay elsewhere, because the Qur'an used to be sent down piecemeal in answer to what they asked about, and that was one of the signs of prophethood, because they would not ask about anything without being answered about it. This can come only from a prophet, so it was a strengthening of his heart and of their hearts, and the answer points to this.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t:
Had it been sent down all at once, it would have preceded the events concerning which the Qur'an used to be sent down; and had it been sent down all at once with the obligations it contains, that would have weighed heavily on them. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knew that the right course lay in sending it down in parts, because they are alerted by it time after time, whereas had it been sent down all at once, the sense of alerting would have disappeared. It also contains abrogating and abrogated [passages]: they would be bound to worship by a thing up to a particular time in which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knew the right course lay, and then the abrogation would be sent down after that; so it is impossible that "do such-and-such" and "do not do it" should be sent down all at once. It is preferable that the complete stop be at «جملة واحدة», because if one stops at «كذلك», the meaning becomes "like the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms", and these have not been mentioned before. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «وَرَتَّلْناهُ تَرْتِيلًا», i.e. "We sent it down". It has been said:
al-tartīl is unhurriedness, and it is the opposite of haste.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t:
«الَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلى جَهَنَّمَ» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is in the clause.
We have mentioned its meaning as related in a report traced back to the Prophet. It has also been said: it is a figure of speech, as you say "he came to me on his face", i.e. unwillingly.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: «وَجَعَلْنا مَعَهُ أَخاهُ هارُونَ»: as a badal (substitute). «وَزِيراً» is a second object. «الوزير» in the language is the helper to whom his master resorts, derived from al-wazar, which is a place of refuge. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: «كَلَّا لا وَزَرَ» [al-Qiyāma: 11].

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
Al-Farrāʾ said: in meaning, Moses ﷺ alone was ordered to go, and this is like His saying
«نَسِيا حُوتَهُما» [al-Kahf: 61], and like His saying «يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجانُ» [al-Raḥmān: 22], when they come out of only one of the two. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the kind of thing with which one ought not to be bold against the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and He, exalted be His praise, has said: «فَقُولا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَيِّناً لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشى قالا رَبَّنا إِنَّنا نَخافُ أَنْ يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنا أَوْ أَنْ يَطْغى» [Ṭā Hā: 44, 45]. The parallel of this is in His saying
«وَمِنْ دُونِهِما جَنَّتانِ» [al-Raḥmān: 62], and He, exalted be His praise, has said: «ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنا مُوسى وَأَخاهُ هارُونَ بِآياتِنا» [al-Muʾminūn: 45].

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
«وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ»: there are several views on its accusative: it may be conjoined to the pronoun in «فَدَمَّرْناهُمْ»; or it may be in the sense of "and remember"; or it may be by an implied verb explained by what follows, the construction being "and We drowned the people of Noah".
These are three views. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that it is accusative by «أغرقناهم», but this does not hold, because أغرقنا is not one of the verbs that take two objects so that it could govern both the pronoun and «قوم نوح».

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: All of this may be conjoined to «قوم نوح» if «قوم نوح» is accusative by conjunction or in the sense of "and remember". All of this may also be accusative as conjoined to the pronoun in «وَجَعَلْناهُمْ», and that is preferable because it is nearer to it.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: «وَكُلًّا ضَرَبْنا لَهُ الْأَمْثالَ»: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: "and He warned each". He said: al-tatbīr is destruction, and from it broken glass is called tibr, and likewise tibr of gold.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t:
It has been said: this is about the unbelievers who disbelieved in the Prophet ﷺ, because they had come upon the cities of the people of Lot, peace be upon him, and knew that they were destroyed for their unbelief. «أَفَلَمْ يَكُونُوا يَرَوْنَها بَلْ كانُوا لا يَرْجُونَ نُشُوراً»: whoever denies [the existence of] words with opposite meanings (al-aḍdād) says that «يرجون» has its usual sense [of hoping], because they disbelieved in the Hereafter only out of rejection of the truth, not out of certainty, so they do not hope for it. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] was one of those who denied al-aḍdād, and he said:
the meaning is: rather they did not hope for the reward of the resurrection, so they were bold in committing sins.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: «وَإِذا رَأَوْكَ إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ»: the answer to «إِذا» is «إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُواً», because its meaning is "they take you". It has been said: the answer is omitted, because the meaning is: they said, "Is this the one whom He sent?" «الَّذِي بَعَثَ اللَّهُ رَسُولًا»: «رسول» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of بعث is أرسل ("sent"), and «رسول» on this view means "a message".

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: «أَفَأَنْتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ وَكِيلًا»: it has been said that its meaning is: would you then compel him to that?

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: «أَمْ تَحْسَبُ أَنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ أَوْ يَعْقِلُونَ»: He did not say "that they", because among them there were some of whom He knew that they would believe. He, Mighty and Majestic, censured them with this: «أَمْ تَحْسَبُ أَنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ» with a hearing of acceptance, or reflect on what you say and so understand it, i.e. they are in the position of one who neither understands nor hears. It has been said: the meaning is that since they did not benefit from what they heard, it is as if they did not hear. «إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا كَالْأَنْعامِ», i.e. they do not comprehend. «بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا», because they deny the truth they hear, and cattle are not like that.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: «أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلى رَبِّكَ»: the alif was omitted because of the jussive. The origin has hamza, and the lightening [of the hamza] is obligatory in the imperfect of this [verb] because of its frequent use. We have already mentioned the meaning of the verse.

nahhas-irab:47-49.t: «وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ لِباساً»: two objects. «وَالنَّوْمَ سُباتاً» is conjoined, and «سبات» means rest. «جعل» was repeated for tawkīd (emphasis); had it been «والنهار نشورا» [without repeating the verb], it would be permissible outside the Qur'an. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: the singular of «الأناسيّ» is إنسيّ, and Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said the same; it is one of al-Farrāʾ's two views. He has another view, namely that the singular of «الأناسيّ» is إنسان, with the nūn changed into yāʾ, so that one says أناسيّ; on his view he is obliged to say, in the plural of سرحان, سراحيّ — there is no difference between them. He also related «وَأَناسِيَ كَثِيراً» with the lightened [yāʾ].

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: «وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْناهُ بَيْنَهُمْ»: it is the rain, as ʿAbdallāh ibn Masʿūd and ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAbbās said: no year has more rain than another year, but Allah directs it wherever He wills. «فَأَبى أَكْثَرُ النَّاسِ إِلَّا كُفُوراً»: no disagreement is known among the people of exegesis that the unbelief here is their saying "We were given rain by such-and-such a star", and that its parallel is the astrologer's saying "the star did such-and-such", and that everyone who attributes an action to them is an unbeliever.

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: «وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ مِنَ الْماءِ بَشَراً فَجَعَلَهُ نَسَباً وَصِهْراً»: the scholars have three views on this. The most eminent of them is what is related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: the kinship by lineage (al-nasab) is seven: «حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهاتُكُمْ وَبَناتُكُمْ وَأَخَواتُكُمْ وَعَمَّاتُكُمْ وَخالاتُكُمْ وَبَناتُ الْأَخِ وَبَناتُ الْأُخْتِ» [al-Nisāʾ: 23], and the kinship by marriage (al-ṣihr) is the seven: «وَأُمَّهاتُكُمُ اللَّاتِي أَرْضَعْنَكُمْ» [al-Nisāʾ: 23] to the end of the verse. The explanation of this is that the first seven are from lineage, so its construction in Arabic is "He made him possessed of lineage and possessed of marriage-kinship"; and the seven of marriage-kinship are those among whom marriage-kinship would occur were it not for what has arisen. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: al-nasab is the relatives, and al-ṣihr is those [women] related by suckling. The third view is that al-nasab is the male offspring and al-ṣihr the female offspring, because marriage-kinship comes about from two sides.

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: «وَكانَ الْكافِرُ عَلى رَبِّهِ ظَهِيراً»: it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that the unbeliever here is Abū Jahl and his partisans, because he sought the backing of the idol-worshippers against the friends of his Lord. ʿIkrima said: the unbeliever is Iblīs, a backer in enmity to his Lord. Maṭar said: the unbeliever here is Satan.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: «مَنْ» is in the position of [and] the accusative as an exception not of the same kind as the first [i.e. a disjoined exception]. [Translator's note: the wording «في موضع ونصب» is translated as printed; «في موضع نصب» is evidently meant.] The construction is: "but whoever wishes to spend seeking the pleasure of Allah so as to take a way to the reward of his Lord, let him do so."

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: «ثُمَّ اسْتَوى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ الرَّحْمنُ»: there are three ways of explaining its nominative: it may be a badal (substitute) for the latent pronoun in «استوى»; it may be nominative in the sense of "He is the All-Merciful"; and it may be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being «فَسْئَلْ بِهِ خَبِيراً». The genitive is also permissible, in the sense of "and rely on the Living One who does not die, the All-Merciful", being a naʿt (adjective); and the accusative is permissible as praise.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: This is the reading of the Medinans and the Basrans; al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «لما يأمرنا» with yāʾ. The first reading is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, and he interpreted the second, as we see it, as "Shall we prostrate to what the All-Merciful commands us?" He said: had they acknowledged that the All-Merciful commanded them, they would not have been unbelievers. But this far-fetched interpretation ought not to be given on behalf of the Kufans in their reading; rather the better interpretation on their behalf is "Shall we prostrate to what the Prophet ﷺ commands us?", and the reading is sound on this basis, though the first is clearer and more readily understood.
