(الواو) resumptive (ما) negating (قبلك) an adverb (ẓarf), accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلنا), (من المرسلين) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), genitive in form, accusative in position «[Note: Or attached to an adjective of the implied object, i.e. «a number of the messengers».]», the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis (في الأسواق) attached to (يمشون), (لبعض) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «فتنة» (الهمزة) for interrogation, carrying the meaning of command «[Note: Or it is for mere interrogation.]», (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). The clause «أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّهم ليأكلون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of «المرسلين».
The clause «يأكلون ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar (predicate) of «إنّ».
The clause «يمشون ...» is in the position of nominative, maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «يأكلون».
The clause «جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «تصبرون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كان ربّك بصيرا» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the agent of «تصبرون», the linking element being implied, i.e. «بكم».

* Benefits:
- Successive emphases:
In this verse emphases follow one another, to establish the status of the messengers and that they are human beings like other people, enjoying all the attributes of humans.
First: He cast the verse in the form of restriction with «ما» and «إلا», then followed that with another emphasiser, namely «إن».
Then He brought the lām in the predicate of «إنّ», and this lām's function is emphasis.
Thus we find that the Quranic style often resorts to emphasis, to establish the meanings and ideas addressed to the polytheists, that perhaps they may become certain.. We have pointed this out before.

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (لا) negating (لولا) a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) (علينا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزل), (الملائكة) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the passive verb «أنزل» (أو) a conjunction (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied (muqaddar) oath (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq) (في أنفسهم) attached to (استكبروا), with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. «في شأن أنفسهم» «[Note: The meaning is that they persisted in arrogance within themselves.]», (عتوا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb).
The clause «قال الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا يرجون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لولا أنزل ... الملائكة» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «نرى ...» is in the position of accusative, maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «أنزل»..
The clause «استكبروا ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the implied oath ...
and the implied oath clause is resumptive..
The clause «عتوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause «استكبروا».

* Morphology:
(عتوّا), a maṣdar (verbal noun) known by hearing (samāʿī) of the triliteral verb عتا; its pattern is فعول, with two ḍammas, and the wāw of فعول is assimilated (mudgham) into the lām of the word.

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(يوم) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being «اذكر», and the pronoun in (يرون) refers to «الذين لا يرجون لقاء الله» (لا) the lā of generic negation (بشرى) the noun of «لا», indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif, in the position of accusative (يومئذ) an adverb annexed to an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of «لا», and the tanwīn is a compensation for something omitted, i.e. «يوم إذ يرون الملائكة» (للمجرمين) attached to the predicate of «لا» (الواو) conjunction (حجرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb «[Note: It was said that the governing word of this maṣdar never appears and that it is not declined (lā yataṣarraf).]», (محجورا) a naʿt (adjective) of «حجر», accusative, and it reinforces the meaning.
The clause «يرون ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لا بشرى ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied verb of saying, i.e. «يقولون لا بشرى ...», and the implied clause of saying is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الملائكة».
The clause «يقولون ...» is in the position of genitive, maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «يرون الملائكة».
The clause «حجرا ...» is in the position of accusative as the reported speech.

* Morphology:
(محجورا), a passive participle from the triliteral حجر; its pattern is مفعول.

safi-cedvel:23-23.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (إلى ما) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قدمنا) (من عمل) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted referring pronoun, i.e. «إلى ما عملوه من عمل» «[Note: It may be a tamyīz (specification) of the relative noun (ما).]», (هباء) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its governing word being «جعلناه».
The clause «قدمنا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «عملوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «جعلناه ...» has no grammatical position, maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «قدمنا».

* Morphology:
(هباء), a collective noun for the dust and other particles seen in the rays of the sun; its singular is «هباءة». The hamza is changed from a wāw: its origin is هباو; [the wāw] came at the end after a quiescent alif and was changed into hamza.
(منثورا), a passive participle from the triliteral نثر; its pattern is مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
The representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in the words of the Exalted «وَقَدِمْنا إِلى ما عَمِلُوا مِنْ عَمَلٍ فَجَعَلْناهُ هَباءً مَنْثُوراً».
For the state of these disbelievers, and the state of the deeds they did in their disbelief, is represented by the state of a people who opposed their sovereign and rebelled against him, so he came upon their possessions, set out for what was in their hands, ruined it and scattered it in every direction (shazar mazar), leaving of it neither substance nor trace. In the borrowed expression, «قدم» is used in the sense of "to set out for, to intend", because it is well known in that sense; the intention that leads to the goal is called "coming" (qudūm) because it is its preliminary. The representation includes a likening of his annulled deeds to scattered dust, without metaphor.

safi-cedvel:24-24.t:
* I'rab:
(يومئذ) an adverb (ẓarf), accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) (خير), (مستقرّا) tamyīz (specification), accusative ...
The clause «أصحاب الجنّة ... خير» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(مقيلا), a noun of place from قال يقيل, meaning "to rest at midday", of the bāb of ضرب. It contains a phonological change (iʿlāl) by making quiescent: its origin is مقيل — with sukūn on the qāf and kasra on the yāʾ — the yāʾ was made quiescent because the kasra was heavy on it, and its vowel was transferred to the qāf before it; its pattern is مفعل.

* Rhetoric:
Metaphor (al-istiʿāra): in the words of the Exalted «وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلًا».
«المقيل» is originally the place of the siesta (al-qaylūla) — which is sleeping at midday — and it was transferred from that to the place of enjoyment with spouses, because it resembles it in that each of them is a place of privacy and rest; so it is a metaphor. It was also said: what is meant by it is a place of repose in general, using the restricted for the unrestricted, so it is a synecdoche (majāz mursal). It was not left on its original sense only because there is no sleep at all in Paradise.

safi-cedvel:25-25.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (يوم) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being «اذكر» (تشقق) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), with one of the two tāʾs dropped (بالغمام) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تشقّق), and the bāʾ is causal «[Note: The bāʾ may be for accompaniment (mulābasa), so that the prepositional phrase is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial).]», (تنزيلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb).
The clause «تشقّق السماء ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ونزّل الملائكة ...» is in the position of genitive, maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «تشقّق».

safi-cedvel:26-26.t:
* I'rab:
(يومئذ) attached to (mutaʿalliq) «الملك», since it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) «[Note: Or it is an adverb of the [notion of] existence (al-istiqrār), the predicate to which (للرحمن) is attached.]», (الحقّ) a naʿt (adjective) of «الملك» «[Note: Or it is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الملك), and «للرحمن» is attached to «الحقّ» or to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of it.]», (للرحمن) attached to the predicate of the subject (الواو) conjunction, and the noun of (كان) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to the day mentioned before (يوما) predicate of «كان», accusative (manṣūb) (على الكافرين) attached to (عسيرا), which is an adjective of (يوما), accusative.
The clause «الملك ... للرحمن» ... has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كان يوما ...» has no grammatical position, maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the resumptive clause.

safi-cedvel:27-29.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (يوم يعضّ) like (يوم تشقّق) «[Note: In verse (25) of this sura.]», (على يديه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يعض), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ (يا) a particle of alerting (tanbīh) (ليتني) a particle resembling the verb, for wishing (tamannī), the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the noun of «ليت» (مع) an adverb (ẓarf), accusative (manṣūb), attached to an omitted second object, its governing word being «اتّخذت».
The clause «اذكر» يوم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يعضّ الظالم ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يقول ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الظالم».
The clause «ليتني اتّخذت ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «اتّخذت» is in the position of nominative, khabar (predicate) of «ليت».
(يا) a particle of vocative and lament (taḥassur) (ويلتا) the one addressed (munādā) in lament, of the annexed type «[Note: (ويلتا) may be parsed as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb not used in the language, in which case (يا) is a particle of alerting.]», accusative, the sign of the accusative being an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the alif, and the alif, changed from a yāʾ, is muḍāf ilayhi (خليلا) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative ...
The clause «the vocative and the lament ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech.
The clause «ليتني ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative «[Note: It may be resumptive, reinforcing the first clause «ليتني», and the clause «يا ويلتا» is then parenthetical, for supplication.]».
The clause «لم أتّخذ ...» is in the position of nominative, predicate of «ليت».
(اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq) (عن الذكر) attached to (أضلّني), (بعد) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (أضلّني), (إذ) an adverbial noun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) resumptive (للإنسان) attached to (خذولا).
The clause «أضلّني ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «جاءني ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «كان الشيطان خذولا» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(فلانا), a noun used as a metonym (kināya) for the proper name of a rational being; its pattern is فعال, with ḍamma on the fāʾ. When made definite by «ال», it is a metonym for a non-rational being. It is stated in al-Muḥīṭ: «One may say to one person «يا فل», to two «يا فلان» — with kasra on the nūn — and to a group «يا فلون», with two ḍammas and a fatḥa ... Sībawayh disallowed saying «فل» to mean «فلان» except in poetry ...» end of quotation.
(خذولا), an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālagha) from the triliteral خذل; its pattern is فعول, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
Metonymy (al-kināya): in the words of the Exalted «وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ الظَّالِمُ عَلى يَدَيْهِ».
Biting the hands and the fingertips, eating the fingertips, gnashing the teeth and the like are metonymies for rage and regret, because they are among their concomitants.

* Benefits:
1- The words of the Exalted «يا وَيْلَتى لَيْتَنِي».
- The lamented noun (al-mandūb) annexed to the yāʾ of the first person: when a noun annexed to the yāʾ of the first person is lamented, as in «يا ويلتي», or addressed in the vocative, six usages are permissible in it.
a- Dropping the yāʾ and making do with the kasra; this is the best and the most frequent in the Noble Quran, as in «يا عِبادِ فَاتَّقُونِ». What applies to the one addressed applies likewise to the lamented noun.
b- Keeping the yāʾ quiescent, as in «يا عبادي لا خوف عليكم». This example, too, is of the one addressed.
c- Keeping the yāʾ with fatḥa, as in «قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا».
d- Changing the kasra into fatḥa and the yāʾ into alif, as in «يا ويلتا», as in the verse before us, and «يا حسرتا».
e- Dropping the alif changed from the yāʾ — in other words, dropping the yāʾ that was changed into alif — and making do with the fatḥa, as in the poet's words:
ولست براجع ما فات مني ... بلهف ولا بليت ولا لونّي
(I shall not bring back what has escaped me by "Alas!", nor by "Would that…", nor by "If only…".)
Its origin is «بقولي يا لهف».
And [f-] putting ḍamma on the final letter, without regard to the annexation, as single nouns take ḍamma. This is frequent in nouns that are mostly addressed only in the annexed form, such as «الأب», «الابن», «الأم» and «الرب»; their saying «يا أمّ لا تفعلي» is attested, and some read:
«رَبِّ السِّجْنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ» with the nominative (ḍamma). [Translator's note: this sixth usage carries no letter in the source; "f-" is added for clarity. The source reads «بغية الإضافة» ("aiming at the annexation"), which in context appears to stand for «بنيّة قطع الإضافة» or similar; it is rendered by the sense.]
We add to these six usages we have mentioned:
a- That the tāʾ of femininity is given in compensation for the omitted yāʾ of the first person and takes kasra, which is the most common, or fatḥa, or ḍamma. All three have been read in the words of the Exalted «يا أَبَتِ إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَباً». b- The tāʾ and the alif substituted for the yāʾ may be combined, rarely, as in «يا أبتا» and «يا أمتا». Of this is the example before us: «يا وَيْلَتى لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أَتَّخِذْ فُلاناً خَلِيلًا ...», in which the compensation and what it compensates for are combined.
2-
Among the marvels of hadith describing the singing of the wide-eyed houris are his words ﷺ, in what Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) narrates from him; he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «The wives of the people of Paradise will sing to their husbands in the most beautiful voices that anyone has ever heard. Among what they will sing is: «We are the good and beautiful ones, wives of a noble people, who look with eyes delighted»».
A benefit:
a- «فلان» is a metonym for the proper name of a rational being.
b- «فل» is a metonym for an indefinite rational male being.
c- «فلانة» is a metonym for the proper name of a rational female being.
d- «فلة» is a metonym for an indefinite rational female being.
e- «الفلان» and «الفلانة», made definite with alif and lām, are metonyms for non-rational beings. So reflect.

safi-cedvel:30-30.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) the one addressed (munādā), annexed, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the omitted yāʾ, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the sign of the accusative in (قومي) is an implied fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ (القرآن) badal (substitute) of the demonstrative — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — accusative (مهجورا) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative.
The clause «قال الرسول ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «the vocative and its response ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّ قومي اتّخذوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.
The clause «اتّخذوا ...» is in the position of nominative, khabar (predicate) of «إنّ».

* Morphology:
(مهجورا), a passive participle from the triliteral هجر; its pattern is مفعول.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (كذلك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governing word is «جعلنا», and the reference is to the making of an enemy for the Prophet «[Note: The kāf may have the sense of «مثل», in the position of accusative as an absolute object standing in for the maṣdar, being its attribute.]», (لكلّ) attached to a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (من المجرمين) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (عدوّا), (الواو) resumptive (ربّك) genitive in form, nominative in position, fāʿil (agent) of «كفى» (هاديا) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ربّك», accusative (manṣūba) «[Note: Or a tamyīz (specification), accusative.]».
The clause «جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كفى بربّك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Benefits:
- The redundancy of prepositions:
Among the prepositions, «من», «الباء», «الكاف» and «اللام» ... are added redundantly. Since the words of the Exalted «وَكَفى بِرَبِّكَ هادِياً» occur in this verse, we shall mention to you the places where the bāʾ is redundant, by hearing (samāʿan) or by analogy (qiyāsan), because the bāʾ is the most frequently redundant of the prepositions. It is added in negative and affirmative [sentences], and its redundancy occurs in five places:
a- In the agent of «كفى», as in the verse before us, and as in the words of the Exalted «وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ وَلِيًّا كَفى بِاللَّهِ نَصِيراً».
b- In the direct object, «by hearing ...», as in their saying: «أخذت بزمام الفرس ...». Of this are the words of the Exalted:
«وَلا تُلْقُوا بِأَيْدِيكُمْ إِلَى التَّهْلُكَةِ» and His words «وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ» etc. Of this also is its redundancy in the object of «كفى» when transitive to one object, as in «كفى بالمرء إثما أن يحدث بكل ما سمع»; and also its redundancy in the object of «عرف», «علم», «دري», «جهل», «سمع» and «أحسّ».
c- It is added in the subject (mubtadaʾ) when it is derived from the word «حسب», as in «بحسبك درهم», or after the word «ناهيك ...», as in «ناهيك بخالد شجاعا ...», or after «إذا» of surprise, as in «خرجت فإذا بالأستاد» [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently for «بالأستاذ» ("the teacher").], or after «كيف», as in «كيف بك إذا حصل كذا». d- It is added in the ḥāl whose governing word is negated, as in «فما رجعت بخائبة ركاب» (and the riding camels did not return disappointed); some held this redundancy to be regular (maqīsa).
e- It is frequently added in the predicate of «ليس» and «ما», and this redundancy is regular, as in «أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِكافٍ عَبْدَهُ» and the words of the Exalted «وَما رَبُّكَ بِظَلَّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ».
The bāʾ has also entered the predicate of «أنّ», as in «أو لم يروا أنّ الله بقادر على أن يحيي الموتى». [Translator's note: the source writes «ان» without hamza; the example it gives has «أنّ».]

safi-cedvel:47-49.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (لكم) attached (mutaʿalliq) to (جعل) «[Note: or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (لباسا) – an adjective that has been put before the noun it describes –]», (الواو) a conjunction (النوم سباتا) the two are conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (الليل لباسا) «[Note: or they are two objects of an implied verb jaʿala, in which case the conjunction is a conjunction of clauses.]», (نشورا) a second object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative.
Clause: «هو الذي ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «جعل ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
And the clause: «جعل (the second) » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.
(48) (الواو) a conjunction (بشرا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from (الرياح) (بين) an adverbial, accusative, attached to (بشرا), (يدي) muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct), genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ (الواو) a conjunction (من السماء) attached to (أنزلنا).
And the clause: «هو الذي ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «أرسل ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذي).
And the clause: «أنزلنا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause; it contains an iltifāt (shift of person).
(49) (اللام) the lām of cause (نحيي) an imperfect verb, accusative through an implied أن after the lām (به) attached to (نحيي), the bāʾ being causal..
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن نحيي..) is in the position of a genitive through the lām, attached to (أنزلنا).
(الواو) a conjunction (نسقيه) an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to the verb نحيي ...
And the hāʾ is a second object (mafʿūl bihi) (ممّا) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (أنعاما وأناسيّ), and ما is used in the sense of predominance (taghlīb) (أنعاما) a first object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative, of the verb نسقي, and أناسيّ is denied tanwīn because it is a broken plural on the pattern of the "furthest plurals" (muntahā al-jumūʿ).
And the clause: «نحيي ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن), which is implied.
And the clause: «نسقيه ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause of the particle-type relative.
And the clause: «خلقنا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).

* Morphology:
(سباتا) a maṣdar (verbal noun) of سبت يسبت, from the pattern of نصر and the pattern of ضرب; its wazn is فعال with ḍamma on the fāʾ.
(طهورا) a sifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from the triliteral طهر يطهر, from the pattern of نصر and the pattern of كرم; its wazn is فعول with fatḥa on the fāʾ. Or it is the maṣdar of طهر used as an adjective for intensification.
(49) بلدة: a non-derived noun (ism jāmid) for "city", which comes ending in tāʾ, and the tāʾ may be dropped; its wazn is فعلة with fatḥa followed by sukūn.
(ميتا) the word came in the masculine, though it should have been feminine, because the feminine and the masculine are alike in it; or it came in the masculine with regard to the meaning of بلدة, which is "place".
(أناسيّ) plural of إنسان; its origin is أناسين, like سرحان and سراحين; then the nūn was replaced by yāʾ and assimilated into the other yāʾ. It is also said to be the plural of إنسيّ – this is the opinion of al-Farrāʾ – so its wazn on the first opinion is فعالين, and on the second فعاليّ; the first opinion is the stronger.

* Rhetoric:
Simile (tashbīh): in His saying, the Exalted, جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ لِباساً وَالنَّوْمَ سُباتاً.
He likened the night to a covering garment, and likened sleep and waking to death and life.
Advancing and delaying (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr): in His saying, the Exalted, لِنُحْيِيَ بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَيْتاً وَنُسْقِيَهُ مِمَّا خَلَقْنا أَنْعاماً وَأَناسِيَّ كَثِيراً.
He put the giving of life to the earth and the watering of the livestock before the watering of human beings, because the life of human beings depends on the life of their land and the life of their livestock. So He put what is the cause of their life and livelihood before their being watered, and because, if they obtain what waters their land and their cattle, they will not lack their own watering.

* Benefits:
- جعل:
A verb that indicates probability (rujḥān) and takes two objects, on condition that it is not meant as creating and bringing into existence, nor as making obligatory, as in: جعلت له كذا (I assigned such-and-such to him), meaning "I made it obligatory":
a- Probability, as in:
«وَجَعَلُوا الْمَلائِكَةَ الَّذِينَ هُمْ عِبادُ الرَّحْمنِ إِناثاً» .
b- It may also indicate transformation (taṣyīr), that is, moving from one state to another, as in «فَجَعَلْناهُ هَباءً مَنْثُوراً» .
Second: it is among the verbs that alter the sentence (nawāsikh) and indicate beginning to do something, and work like kāna, except that its khabar must be a verbal clause whose verb is imperfect.
It is irregular for a nominal clause to come as its khabar, as in:
وقد جعلت قلوص بني سهيل ... من الأكوار مرتعها قريب
(The young she-camel of the Banū Suhayl has begun, from among the saddles, to have her pasture near.)
- جعل also comes as a past verb in the basic sense. The imperfect verb may also come from it, though rarely.
Third: when جعل comes in the sense of أوجد (brought into existence), it takes one object, as in His saying, the Exalted:
وَجَعَلَ الظُّلُماتِ وَالنُّورَ that is, He created them.

safi-cedvel:50-52.t:
* I'rab:
(ولقد صرّفناه) like ولقد آتينا «[Note: in verse (35) of this sūra; and the pronoun of the absent person refers to the water.]», (بينهم) attached to (صرّفناه), (اللام) for cause.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يذّكّروا) is in the position of a genitive through the lām, attached to (صرّفناه).
(الفاء) a conjunction (إلّا) a particle of restriction «[Note: the exception here came as an emptied one (mufarragh) because of the meaning of negation in (أبى).]», (كفورا) a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative.
Clause: «صرّفناه ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam).
And the clause: «يذّكّروا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن), which is implied.
And the clause: «أبى أكثر ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the response to the oath.
(51) (الواو) a conjunction (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لو (في كلّ) attached to (بعثنا) ..
And the clause: «شئنا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the response to the oath.
And the clause: «بعثنا ... » has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(52) (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition (لا) a prohibitive, jussive particle, and the sign of the jussive in (تطع) is sukūn, which was given a kasra because of the meeting of two sukūns (به) attached to (جاهد), and the pronoun refers to the Qur'an (جهادا) an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), accusative.
And the clause: «لا تطع ... » is the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if We had sent you to all people, then do not obey ..."
And the clause: «جاهدهم ... » is conjoined to the clause لا تطع ...

safi-cedvel:53-54.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (فرات) a second khabar (predicate), nominative (بينهما) an adverbial, accusative, attached to an omitted second object (الواو) a conjunction (حجرا) conjoined to (برزخا), accusative (محجورا) an adjective (naʿt) of حجر, accusative.
Clause: «هو الذي ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «مرج البحرين ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
And the clause: «هذا عذب ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) «[Note: or it is in the position of an accusative, as the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied "saying" that is a ḥāl from البحرين, that is, "it being said of them".]».
And the clause: «هذا ملح» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause هذا عذب.
And the clause: «جعل ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.
(54) (الواو) a conjunction (من الماء) attached to (خلق), (الفاء) a conjunction (نسبا) a second object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative (الواو) a conjunction.
And the clause: «هو الذي ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «خلق ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
And the clause: «جعله ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause خلق.
And the clause: «كان ربّك ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause هو الذي خلق.

* Morphology:
(عذب) a sifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) of the triliteral عذب يعذب, pattern of كرم; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa followed by sukūn.
(فرات) a sifa mushabbaha of the triliteral فرت يفرت, pattern of كرم; its wazn is فعال with ḍamma on the fāʾ; and فرت الماء means the water was sweet.
(ملح) a sifa mushabbaha of the triliteral ملح يملح, pattern of كرم, pattern of نصر and pattern of فتح; its wazn is فعل with kasra followed by sukūn; and الملح is also the name of the well-known substance, in which case it is a non-derived noun.
(أجاج) a sifa mushabbaha from the triliteral verb أجّ, meaning "to be salty and to become bitter", pattern of نصر; its wazn is فعال with ḍamma on the fāʾ.
(صهرا) a noun meaning kinship; its wazn is فعل with kasra followed by sukūn; its plural is أصهار.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative usage (majāz): in His saying, the Exalted, حِجْراً مَحْجُوراً.
This is the phrase that one seeking refuge says, and it occurs here figuratively, as if each of the two seas sought refuge from its fellow and said to it: حجرا محجورا, as He said: «لا يَبْغِيانِ», that is, neither of them transgresses against its fellow by mixing. The absence of transgression there is like the seeking of refuge here: each of them is put in the picture of one transgressing against its fellow, so it seeks refuge from it. It is among the finest and most intense of metaphors in eloquence.

safi-cedvel:55-55.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (من دون) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the relative ما, the object of يعبدون, and (كان) the wāw is resumptive (على ربه) attached to (ظهيرا), with an omitted muḍāf, that is: "against disobedience to his Lord".
And the clause: «يعبدون» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «لا ينفعهم ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause: «يضرّهم ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «كان الكافر ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive «[Note: or conjoined to the resumptive clause.]».

safi-cedvel:56-56.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (ما) negative (إلّا) a particle of restriction (مبشرا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative.
And the clause: «ما أرسلناك ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.

safi-cedvel:57-59.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative (عليه) attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of أجر, and the pronoun refers to the delivery of the message understood from His saying: أرسلناك «[Note: in the preceding verse.]», (أجر) genitive in form, accusative in position, a second object (mafʿūl bihi), its governor being أسألكم (إلّا) for a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), meaning "but" (لكن) (من) a relative noun, in the position of an accusative as a discontinuous exception (إلى ربّه) attached to an omitted second object, its governor being يتّخذ.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يتّخذ ... ) is in the position of an accusative, a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) whose governor is شاء.
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «ما أسألكم ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «شاء ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause: «يتّخذ ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
(58) (الواو) a conjunction (على الحيّ) attached to (توكّل), (الذي) a relative noun in the position of a genitive, an adjective of الحيّ (لا) negative (الواو) a conjunction (بحمده) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of سبّح, that is, "accompanied by His praise" (الواو) resumptive (الباء) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (الهاء) is the agent of كفى in its remote position (بذنوب) attached to (خبيرا), which is an accusative ḥāl from the agent of كفى.
And the clause: «توكّل ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause قل.
And the clause: «لا يموت ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
And the clause: «سبّح ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause توكّل.
And the clause: «كفى به ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
(59) (الذي) a relative noun in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الرحمن «[Note: or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو" .. or a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "أعني" (I mean), in which case (الرحمن) is a mubtadaʾ or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو".]», (الواو) a conjunction in both places (ما) a relative noun in the position of an accusative, conjoined to السموات (بينهما) an adverbial, accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila of ما (في ستة) attached to (خلق) (ثمّ) a conjunction (على العرش) attached to (استوى), (الرحمن) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ الذي «[Note: it may be a badal (substitute) for the pronoun in (استوى) if the relative is parsed as a khabar.]», (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition (به) attached to (خبيرا) «[Note: the pronoun refers to the details of what was mentioned of the creation and the istiwāʾ, or it refers to الرحمن.]».
And the clause: «الذي خلق ... الرحمن» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «خلق ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذي).
And the clause: «استوى ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause خلق.
And the clause: «اسأل ... » is the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if you wish to verify, or to learn the details of, what has been mentioned, then ask about it one who is well informed."

* Benefits:
1- Istiwāʾ (settling) upon the Throne:
The Salaf held that the istiwāʾ is as Allah knows it and as befits His majesty. The Khalaf held that the istiwāʾ means taking dominion and disposing of all beings and creatures as He wills.
2- (إذا) is an adverb of time that includes the meaning of a condition, and it also comes as an adverb that does not include the meaning of a condition, as in His saying, the Exalted: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا يَغْشى وَالنَّهارِ إِذا تَجَلَّى» .

safi-cedvel:60-60.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (لهم) attached to (قيل), (للرحمن) attached to (اسجدوا), (الواو) a conjunction «[Note: or redundant.]» (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (الرحمن), (الهمزة) for an expression of rebuke in the form of a question (ما) a maṣdar particle «[Note: or a relative noun ... or an indefinite noun qualified by a clause, in the position of a genitive, and the returning pronoun of both is omitted.]».
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما تأمرنا) is in the position of a genitive through the lām, attached to (نسجد).
(الواو) resumptive, and the agent of (زادهم) is a pronoun that refers to the saying that was said to them (نفورا) a second object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative.
Clause: «قيل ... » is in the position of a genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «اسجدوا ... » is in the position of a nominative; the deputy agent (nāʾib al-fāʿil) «[Note: it is originally a clause of the content of speech in the active verb.]».
And the clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «ما الرحمن ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the implied content of speech, that is: "What is prostration, and what is al-Raḥmān?.. or 'We prostrate', and what is al-Raḥmān" «[Note: or it is a clause of the content of speech if the wāw is redundant.]».
And the clause: «أنسجد ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive, within the scope of the saying.
And the clause: «تأمرنا ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).
And the clause: «زادهم ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.

safi-cedvel:61-62.t:
* I'rab:
(في السماء) attached to an omitted second object «[Note: or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) if (جعل) is taken to include the meaning of "created" .. and likewise it is valid to attach the preposition and noun (فيها), and to parse the noun (خلفة) with an omitted muḍāf, that is "possessing succession".]», and likewise (فيها) ...
Clause: «تبارك الذي ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «جعل (the first) » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
And the clause: «جعل (the second) has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.
(62) (الواو) a conjunction (خلفة) a second object (mafʿūl bihi) (لمن) attached to the maṣdar خلفة (ان) a maṣdar particle.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يذّكّر ... ) is in the position of an accusative, a direct object of the verb of wanting.
And the clause: «هو الذي ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause تبارك الذي ...
And the clause: «أراد ... » جعل (the third) has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذي). [Translator's note: the words «جعل (الثالثة)» after the clause label appear to be a slip in the source; translated as written.]
And the clause: «أراد ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause: «يذّكّر ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
And the clause: «أراد (the second) » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the first clause أراد.

* Morphology:
(سراجا) a name for a kind of lamp that has oil and a wick; its wazn is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ; its plural is سرج with two ḍammas; it is used in the verse figuratively.
(خلفة) a maṣdar of manner (maṣdar hayʾa) from the triliteral خلف, pattern of نصر, or an ism maṣdar meaning "difference/opposition"; its wazn is فعلة.
(شكورا) a samāʿī maṣdar (a maṣdar fixed by usage) of the triliteral verb شكر, pattern of نصر, and there are other maṣdars: شكر with ḍamma followed by sukūn, and شكران with ḍamma followed by sukūn ... and the wazn of شكور is فعول with two ḍammas.

safi-cedvel:63-76.t:
«[Translator's note: in the source, the order of the paragraphs of this entry is disturbed (the morphology section and some i'rab paragraphs are interleaved). The order of the source is kept here as written.]»

* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (عباد) a mubtadaʾ, nominative, whose khabar is the clause: أولئك يجزون «[Note: in verse (75) coming later in this sūra.]» ...
(الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, an adjective (naʿt) of عباد «[Note: it may be a khabar of the mubtadaʾ عباد ...]», (على الأرض) attached to (يمشون), (هونا) an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) standing in for the maṣdar, being its qualifier, that is: "a gentle walking" «[Note: or a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, that is, "walking leisurely".]», (الواو) a conjunction (سلاما) a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) whose governor is قالوا «[Note: it may be an absolute object of an omitted verb, that is, "we offer a greeting of peace", and the clause is the content of speech.]», and it is an adjective of an omitted noun, that is: "they said words by which they make peace with the disbelievers".
Clause: «عباد الرحمن ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «يمشون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the first relative noun (الذين).
And the clause: «خاطبهم الجاهلون ... » is in the position of a genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(64) (الواو) a conjunction (الذين) a relative noun conjoined to the first relative noun, in the position of a nominative (لربّهم) attached to (سجّدا), which is the khabar of the incomplete verb يبيتون – one of the verbs that alter the sentence (nawāsikh) – «[Note: or it is a ḥāl from the agent of يبيتون if the verb is complete.]».
And the clause: مرّوا باللغو ... is in the position of a genitive; muḍāf ilayhi ...
And the clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis, has no grammatical position; conjoined to the last ṣila clause.
And the clause: «مرّوا (the second) » has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(73) (الواو) a conjunction (الذين) a relative noun in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the first relative noun, and the wāw in (ذكّروا) is the deputy agent (nāʾib al-fāʿil) (بآيات) attached to (ذكّروا), (عليها) attached to (يخرّوا), by including in it the meaning of أكبّوا (fell upon) or أقاموا (stayed) (صمّا) an accusative ḥāl from the agent of يخرّوا..
And the clause: «ذكّروا..» is in the position of a genitive; muḍāf ilayhi ... And the clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis, has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the seventh relative noun (الذين).
And the clause: «لم يخروا» has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(74) (الواو) a conjunction (الذين) conjoined to the first relative noun (ربّنا) a vocative, a muḍāf, accusative ... and نا is muḍāf ilayhi (هب) an imperative verb of supplication, and the agent is "you" (لنا) attached to an omitted second object (mafʿūl bihi) of the verb هب (من أزواجنا) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (قرّة أعين) «[Note: it may be attached to (هب), and من would be for the beginning of the range.]», and it is the first object of the verb هب (الواو) a conjunction (للمتّقين) attached to a ḥāl of (إماما)», (إماما) a second object (mafʿūl bihi), whose governor is اجعلنا «[Note: the word (إماما) is in the singular either because it is originally a maṣdar, that is "possessors of leadership", or because it denotes the genus, that is, each one of us.. and it is also said that it is a plural.]».
And the clause: «يقولون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the eighth relative noun (الذين).
And the clause: «النداء وجوابه ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
And the clause: «هبّ لنا ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «اجعلنا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the response to the vocative.
(75) (أولئك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause يجزون, and the wāw in (يجزون) is the deputy agent (ما) a maṣdar particle (يلقّون) like يجزون (فيها) attached to (يلقّون), (تحيّة) a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative, whose governor is يلقّون, that is "they are given".
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما صبروا) is in the position of a genitive through the bāʾ, attached to (يجزون).
And the clause: «أولئك يجزون ... » is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (عباد الرحمن) «[Note: in verse (63) of this sūra.]».
And the clause: «يجزون الغرفة ... » is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
And the clause: «يلقّون ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause يجزون.
(76) (خالدين) an accusative ḥāl from the deputy agent in (يجزون), (فيها) attached to خالدين (حسنت) a past verb to originate praise, and the agent is a latent pronoun, obligatorily, its implied form being "هو" (مستقرّا) a pronoun-specification (tamyīz), accusative, and the one specially praised is omitted, that is الغرفة.
And the clause: «حسنت مستقرّا ... » is in the position of an accusative; a ḥāl from الغرفة, with an implied (قد).

* Morphology:
(63) هونا: a samāʿī maṣdar (fixed by usage) of the verb هان يهون, pattern of قال; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa followed by sukūn.
(65) غراما: an ism maṣdar from أغرمه الشيء, that is, "he obliged him to it". In al-Mukhtār: al-gharām is perpetual evil and torment; its wazn is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
And the clause: يبيتون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
(65) (الواو) a conjunction (الذين يقولون) like الذين يبيتون (ربّنا) a vocative, a muḍāf, accusative ... and نا is muḍāf ilayhi (عنّا) attached to (اصرف), and the sign of the genitive in (جهنّم) is the fatḥa, it being a diptote.
And the clause: «يقولون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the third relative noun (الذين).
And the clause: «النداء وجوابها ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
And the clause: «اصرف ... » has no grammatical position; the response to the vocative.
And the clause: «إنّ عذابها ... » has no grammatical position; explanation of cause.
And the clause: «كان غراما ... » is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of inna.
(66) And the agent of (ساءت) is a latent pronoun, obligatorily, its implied form being "هو", and the verb is to originate censure (مستقرّا) a specification (tamyīz) of the pronoun – the agent of ساءت – accusative, and the one specially censured is omitted, its implied form being "هي", that is Jahannam.
And the clause: «إنّها ساءت ... » has no grammatical position; another explanation of cause for the turning away of the punishment.
And the clause: «ساءت ... » is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of inna.
(67) (الواو) a conjunction (الذين) in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the first الذين, and the ism of (كان) is a latent pronoun referring to the spending (infāq) understood from the context of the verse (بين) an adverbial, accusative, attached to (قواما) ... or to a ḥāl from it (ذلك) muḍāf ilayhi. And the clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis, has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the fourth relative noun (الذين).
And the clause: «أنفقوا ... » is in the position of a genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «لم يسرفوا ... » has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «لم يقتروا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
And the clause: «كان ... قواما» . has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
(68) (الواو) a conjunction (الذين) in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the first relative noun (لا) negative (مع) an adverbial, accusative, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of إله, and (آخر) is denied tanwīn because it is a diptote, an adjective on the pattern of أفعل (لا يقتلون) like لا يدعون (التي) a relative noun in the position of an accusative, an adjective of النفس, and the returning pronoun is omitted, that is حرّمها (إلّا) a particle of restriction (بالحقّ) attached to a ḥāl of the agent of يقتلون, that is, "being endowed with the right" (لا يزنون) like لا يدعون (الواو) parenthetical (من) a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ, and the sign of the jussive in (يلق) is the dropping of the weak letter, and it is the apodosis of the condition.
And the clause: «لا يدعون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the fifth relative noun (الذين).
And the clause: «لا يقتلون ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause لا يدعون.
And the clause: «حرّم الله ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (التي).
And the clause: «لا يزنون ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause لا يدعون.
(67) قواما: the maṣdar of the triliteral verb قام, meaning "to be balanced and to be moderate"; its wazn is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and it has been used in the place of a description.
(68) يزنون: it has ʾiʿlāl (weak-letter change) by dropping; its origin is يزنيون; the ḍamma on the second yāʾ was found heavy, so it was made sukūn and its vowel moved to the nūn – ʾiʿlāl by sukūn – then the yāʾ was dropped because it met the plural wāw while sukūn, so it became يزنون, on the pattern يفعون.
And the clause: «من يفعل ... » has no grammatical position; parenthetical ...
And the clause: «يفعل ذلك ... » is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «[Note: it may be that the khabar is the two clauses, of the condition and the apodosis, together.]».
And the clause: «يلق ... » has no grammatical position; the apodosis of a jussive condition, not accompanied by the fāʾ.
(69) (يضاعف) an imperfect verb, jussive, a badal (substitute) for the verb (يلق), passive (له) attached to (يضاعف), (العذاب) the deputy agent, nominative (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يضاعف), (يخلد) an imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to (يضاعف), (فيه) attached to (يخلد), that is, in His punishment (مهانا) an accusative ḥāl from the agent of يخلد.
And the clause: «يضاعف ... » has no grammatical position; a badal of the clause يلق ...
And the clause: «يخلد ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause يضاعف.
(70) (إلّا) a particle of exception (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative as a continuous exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil) (عملا) a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative «[Note: this is if (عملا) means "the thing done" ... and it is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) if it is a maṣdar.]» (الفاء) redundant, because the relative resembles the condition «[Note: if (إلّا) means لكن (but), then (من) is a relative, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause أولئك يبدّل, with the fāʾ redundant.. or (من) is a conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause تاب.. and the clause أولئك يبدل is the apodosis.]», (أولئك) a mubtadaʾ, and the pointing is to the relative (من), whose meaning is taken into account in it, and the khabar is the clause يبدّل (حسنات) a second object (mafʿūl bihi), accusative, with the sign of the accusative being the kasra (الواو) resumptive (رحيما) a second khabar.
And the clause: «تاب ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause: «آمن ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause تاب.
And the clause: «عمل ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause تاب.
And the clause: «أولئك يبدّل ... » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
And the clause: «يبدّل الله ... » is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
And the clause: «كان الله غفورا ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive, with a sense of explanation of cause.
(71) (الواو) a conjunction (من) a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ (تاب) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) (صالحا) like عملا, and it is an adjective of an omitted described noun (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (إلى الله) attached to (يتوب), (متابا) an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), accusative.
And the clause: «من تاب ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the parenthetical (من يفعل ذلك).
And the clause: «تاب ... » is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And the clause: «عمل ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause تاب.
And the clause: «إنّه يتوب ... » is in the position of a jussive; the apodosis of the condition, accompanied by the fāʾ.
And the clause: «يتوب ... » is in the position of a nominative; the khabar of inna.
(72) (الواو) a conjunction (الذين) a relative noun in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the first relative noun: الذين يمشون ... (الزور) a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) whose governor is يشهدون in the sense of "they attend", or in the sense of "they give testimony" «[Note: or it is accusative by removal of the preposition, that is: "they do not testify to falsehood".]», (الواو) a conjunction (باللغو) attached to (مرّوا) (كراما) an accusative ḥāl from the agent of the second مرّوا.
And the clause: «لا يشهدون ... » has no grammatical position; the ṣila of the sixth relative noun (الذين).
(يلق) it has ʾiʿlāl by dropping, to suit the jussive; its wazn is يفع.
(أثاما) a samāʿī maṣdar from أثمه يأثمه, pattern of نصر and pattern of ضرب, meaning "he counted it against him as a sin" or "he requited him with the requital of sin"; its wazn is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ, like نكال.
(69) مهانا: a passive participle of (أهان), the quadriliteral verb; its wazn is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn. It has ʾiʿlāl by sukūn and by substitution: its origin is مهين; the fatḥa was moved to the hāʾ, and the yāʾ was turned into alif because it was originally voweled and what precedes it has fatḥa.
(72) كراما: plural of كريم, a sifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from the triliteral كرم, the fifth pattern; its wazn is فعيل, and كريم is applied to the best of a thing and to everything that pleases and is praised ... and كريم is also pluralised as كرماء, on the pattern فعلاء with ḍamma then fatḥa, and the wazn of كرام is فعال with kasra.
(74) قرّة أعين: a maṣdar that is used metonymically for joy, from (قرّت) العين, that is, "the eye cooled with joy and its tears dried and it saw what it had been longing for"; its wazn is فعلة with ḍamma followed by sukūn ... and there are other maṣdars of the verb: قرّة with fatḥa on the qāf, and قرورة with ḍamma on the qāf.
(75) الغرفة: a generic noun (ism jins) meant in the plural, intended to denote the lofty rank; its wazn is فعلة with ḍamma followed by sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- Negation and affirmation: in His saying, the Exalted, لَمْ يَخِرُّوا عَلَيْها صُمًّا وَعُمْياناً.
His saying, the Exalted, لَمْ يَخِرُّوا عَلَيْها is not a negation of falling down, but rather an affirmation of it and a negation of deafness and blindness, as you say: "Zayd does not meet me greeting", which is a negation of the greeting, not of the meeting. The meaning is that when they are reminded of them (the verses), they fall upon them out of eagerness to hear them, and turn to the one reminding them; and in their falling upon them they are hearing with attentive ears and seeing with watchful eyes, unlike those who are reminded of them and you see them falling upon them and turning to the one who reminds them, showing intense eagerness to hear them, while they are like the deaf and blind, since they neither take them in nor look into what is in them, like the hypocrites and their likes.
2- Indefiniteness and fewness: in His saying, the Exalted, قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ:
He made it indefinite and few. As for the indefiniteness, it is for the indefiniteness of القرّة, since a muḍāf has no way to be made indefinite except by making the muḍāf ilayhi indefinite, as though it were said: "Grant us joy and delight from them." And (أعين) was said rather than عيون because He meant the eyes of the God-fearing, and they are few in relation to the eyes of others. «He said, the Exalted: وَقَلِيلٌ مِنْ عِبادِيَ الشَّكُورُ» .
And it may be said, regarding the indefiniteness of (أعين), that they are particular eyes, namely the eyes of the God-fearing.

* Benefits:
1- The verb بات:
It is reported in al-Qāmūs: «وبات يفعل كذا يبيت ويبات بيتا وبياتا ومبيتا وبيتوتة» that is, he does it at night, and it is not about sleeping.
Al-Sharīf al-Raḍī said:
أتبيت ريان الجفون من الكرى ... وأبيت منك بليلة الملسوع
(Do you spend the night with eyelids sated with sleep, while I spend with you the night of one who has been stung?)
And بات is complete, sufficing with its nominative, when it has the meaning of عرّس, which is alighting at the end of the night, as in the saying of Ibn ʿUmar: «أمّا رسول الله فقد بات بمنى» (As for the Messenger of Allah, he spent the night at Minā).
So بات has two meanings: either it is incomplete, needing an ism and a khabar, and its khabar is accusative; or it is complete, sufficing with its agent, and that is when it means "he remained until morning".
2- «وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثاماً يُضاعَفْ لَهُ الْعَذابُ» .
So يضاعف is a total substitute (badal kull min kull), or a congruent badal. And the badal has other types:
a- Partial substitute (badal baʿḍ min kull).
b- Inclusive substitute (badal ishtimāl).
c- Substitute of a clause for a single word and of a single word for a clause.
3- Al-qawām is moderation in matters, and it is the virtue of virtues, because it encompasses every «character trait», so there is neither excess nor deficiency. The mention of this virtue recurs often in the Noble Qur'an. We pointed that out in the counsels of Luqmān to his son. The philosophers of Greece also praised this virtue.
4- Among the merits of sincere repentance is that it turns a person's evil deeds into good deeds, and is there any trade more profitable than that? So reflect.
5- The attributes of the servants of al-Raḥmān:
a- Turning away from the ignorant.
b- Seeking salvation from the Fire.
c- Wisdom in spending.
d- Not associating partners with Allah.
e- They do not kill except with right.
f- And they do not commit fornication.
g- Urging repentance.
h- They do not bear false witness.
i- They keep themselves above idle speech. j- They accept the reminder and receive advice.
k- Asking for righteous offspring.
l- Asking Allah to make them foremost among the God-fearing.
[Translator's note: in the source, items "ط" and "ي" run together on one line, and "و" is written "و لا يزنون" with a space; items are lettered as in the source (ط = i, ي = j, ك = k, ل = l, هـ = e, و = f, ز = g, ح = h).]

safi-cedvel:77-77.t:
* I'rab:
(ما) negative (بكم) attached to (يعبأ), (لولا) a particle of prevention due to existence, containing the meaning of a condition (دعاؤكم) a mubtadaʾ, nominative, and the khabar is omitted obligatorily, its implied form being "موجود" (existing) (الفاء) causal (قد) for affirmation (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition (سوف) a particle of the future, and the ism of (يكون) is a latent pronoun referring to the punishment understood from the context of the verses ...
And the clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «ما يعبأ بكم ربّي ... » is in the position of an accusative; the content of speech.
And the clause: «لولا دعاؤكم (موجود) » has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption ...
And the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, that is: "Were it not for your supplication ... my Lord would not care for you ..."
And the clause: «كذّبتم ... » has no grammatical position; explanation of cause ...
And the clause: «سوف يكون لزاما ... » is the apodosis of an implied condition, which is a second explanation of cause for what preceded, that is: "whoever denies, then the punishment will be binding upon him ..."

safi-cedvel:32-34.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (لولا) is a particle of urging. (عليه) attached to (نزّل). (جملة) an accusative ḥāl by interpretation as a derived word, i.e. "gathered together". (كذلك) attached to an omitted ḥāl from القرآن.
(اللام) is for justification. (به) attached to (نثبّت) ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نثبّت ... ) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to the implied verb that governs the preceding ḥāl, i.e. "He revealed the Qur'an in parts thus, that We may strengthen your heart by it".
(الواو) is conjunctive. (ترتيلا) an absolute object, accusative.
Clause: «قال الذين ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «نزّل ... القرآن» is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.
Clause: «أنزلناه كذلك ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «نثبّت ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle-like relative (أن).
Clause: «رتّلناه ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the implied clause أنزلناه [Note: or it is a ḥāl from the object, with an implied (قد).].
(الواو) is conjunctive. (لا) is negative. (بمثل) attached to (يأتونك). (إلّا) a particle of restriction. (بالحقّ) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of جئناك, or from the object, i.e. "being accompanied by the truth" in either case. (الواو) is conjunctive. (أحسن) conjoined to الحقّ, genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa, for it is a diptote on account of being an adjective and of the pattern أفعل. (تفسيرا) a tamyīz, accusative.
Clause: «لا يأتونك ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the implied clause أنزلناه.
Clause: «جئناك ... » is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from the object of يأتونك.
(34) (الذين) a relative noun, mubtadaʾ [Note: or the predicate of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هم ... or a direct object of an omitted verb in the sense of censure, its implied form being أعني.], and the (الواو) in (يحشرون) is the deputy agent. (على وجوههم) attached to a ḥāl from the deputy agent, i.e. "turned upside down". (إلى جهنّم) attached to (يحشرون), and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa; the verb implies the meaning "they are driven". (مكانا) a tamyīz, accusative, and likewise (سبيلا).
Clause: «الذين يحشرون ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «يحشرون ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «أولئك شرّ ... » is in the position of a nominative, predicate of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).

* Morphology:
(32) جملة: a noun for the gathering of a thing or its group, from the verb جمل يجمل, bāb نصر, meaning "he gathered"; its pattern is فعلة, with ḍamma then sukūn.
(ترتيلا): a qiyāsī (regular) maṣdar of the verb رتّل, quadriliteral; its pattern is تفعيل.
(33) تفسيرا: a qiyāsī maṣdar of the verb فسّر, quadriliteral; its pattern is تفعيل.

* Rhetoric:
Explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): in His saying, the Exalted, وَلا يَأْتُونَكَ بِمَثَلٍ. Here the question is likened to a "parable", on the basis of the common feature of falsity, because most parables are imagined matters.
His saying, the Exalted: أُوْلئِكَ شَرٌّ مَكاناً وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا.
Describing the place as evil and the path as astray is of the chapter of figurative attribution (isnād majāzī), for exaggeration.

safi-cedvel:35-36.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (اللام) is the lām of oath, for an implied oath. (قد) is a particle of affirmation. (الكتاب) the second direct object, accusative. (معه) an adverb, accusative, attached to (جعلنا) [Note: it is permissible that it be attached to the omitted second object, with (وزيرا) a ḥāl from (أخاه).]. (هارون) an explicative apposition - or a substitute - accusative, with tanwīn withheld because it is a proper name and foreign. (وزيرا) the second direct object, accusative.
Clause: «آتينا ... » has no grammatical position, being the response to the oath... and the implied oath clause is resumptive.
Clause: «جعلنا معه ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the response to the oath.
(36) (الفاء) is conjunctive. (إلى القوم) attached to (اذهبا). (الذين) a relative noun in the position of a genitive, an adjective of القوم. (بآياتنا) attached to (كذّبوا). (الفاء) is conjunctive. (تدميرا) an absolute object, accusative.
Clause: «قلنا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause جعلنا.
Clause: «اذهبا ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.
Clause: «كذّبوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
Clause: «دمّرناهم ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "so the two went to them, and they denied them both, so We destroyed them ..."

safi-cedvel:37-37.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is conjunctive. (قوم) a direct object of an omitted verb that what follows explains, i.e. "We drowned the people of Nūḥ". (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", stripped of the sense of condition, attached to the omitted verb. (للناس) attached to an omitted second direct object whose governor is جعلناهم. (للظالمين) attached to (أعتدنا) ...
Clause: «(أغرقنا) قوم نوح ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause آتينا [Note: in the preceding verse.].
Clause: «كذّبوا ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «أغرقناهم ... » has no grammatical position, being explicative.
Clause: «جعلناهم ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause أغرقناهم.
Clause: «أعتدنا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the implied clause أغرقنا.

safi-cedvel:38-38.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is conjunctive. (عادا) a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being «دمّرنا» or «أهلكنا». (الواو) is conjunctive in the three places. (ثمود، أصحاب ... ، قرونا) nouns conjoined to (عادا), accusative like it. (بين) an adverb, accusative, attached to an adjective of (قرونا). (كثيرا) a second adjective of (قرونا), accusative.
Clause: «دمّرنا ... » عادا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause أعتدنا [Note: in the preceding verse.].

* Morphology:
(الرسّ): a noun for an ancient well; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and its ʿayn and lām are from one letter.

safi-cedvel:39-39.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is conjunctive. (كلّا) a direct object of an omitted verb that what follows explains, i.e. "We warned" or "We frightened". (له) attached to (ضربنا). The second (كلّا) is a fronted direct object, accusative. (تتبيرا) an absolute object, accusative.
Clause: «أنذرنا» كلّا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause (دمّرنا) عادا.
Clause: «ضربنا ... » has no grammatical position, being explicative.
Clause: «تبّرنا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause (أنذرنا) كلّا.

* Benefits:
1- The i'rab of «كل»:
We have three aspects of its i'rab:
a- That it be emphasis (tawkīd) of a definite noun, which is the school of the Basrans; according to them emphasis of an indefinite noun is not permitted, contrary to Ibn Mālik, who permitted emphasizing it, as in: صمت شهرا كلّه.
It must be annexed to a pronoun referring to the emphasized word, as in: فَسَجَدَ الْمَلائِكَةُ كُلُّهُمْ. Sometimes an overt noun takes the place of the pronoun, as in: يا أشبه الناس كل الناس بالقمر.
b- That it be an adjective of a definite noun, in which case it indicates completeness, and it must be annexed to an overt noun like it in wording and meaning: «هم القوم كلّ القوم يا أم خالد».
c- That it be third, subject to governors:
It is then annexed to the overt noun, as in: كل نفس بما كسبت رهينة, or not annexed, as in this verse we are dealing with: وكلّا ضربنا له الأمثال، وكلا تبرنا تتبيرا.
It may also stand in for the maṣdar, being in the position of an accusative absolute object, as in «فَلا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ». If it is annexed to an adverb it is parsed as in the position of an accusative mafʿūl fīhi, as in «سرت كل الليل ... ».
2- The annexation of «كل ... »:
There are three aspects:
a- That it be annexed to an overt noun.
b- That it be annexed to an omitted pronoun: «وَكُلًّا ضَرَبْنا».
c- That it be annexed to a mentioned pronoun, as in «وَكُلُّهُمْ آتِيهِ».

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive. (لقد أتوا) like لقد آتينا [Note: in verse (35) of this sura, and the pronoun in (أتوا) refers to the people of Mecca.]. (على القرية) attached to (أتوا), by implying in it the meaning "they passed by". (التي) a relative noun in the position of a genitive, an adjective of القرية, and the deputy agent of the verb (أمطرت) is a pronoun referring to القرية. (مطر) an absolute object, accusative - in the sense of "raining" [Note: it is possible that it be a direct object, because the meaning is "it was pelted with stones" - which are an evil rain - so it is, as it appears, accusative by removal of the preposition.]. (الهمزة) is for interrogation. (الفاء) is conjunctive. (بل) is for the transitional iḍrāb. (لا) is negative.
Clause: «أتوا ... » has no grammatical position, being the response to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause is resumptive.
Clause: «أمطرت ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (التي).
Clause: «يكونوا يرونها ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "Do they pass by and not see it?".
Clause: «يرونها ... » is in the position of an accusative, predicate of يكونوا ...
Clause: «كانوا لا يرجون ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «لا يرجون ... » is in the position of an accusative, predicate of كانوا.

* Morphology:
(مطر): ism maṣdar of the verb أمطر; the qiyāsī maṣdar is الإمطار; the pattern of مطر is فعل, with two fatḥas.

* Rhetoric:
Majāz (figurative usage): in His saying, the Exalted, «بَلْ كانُوا لا يَرْجُونَ نُشُوراً».
By "hope" (rajāʾ) is meant expectation, figuratively, as if it were said: "rather, they did not expect the resurrection that entails the recompense of the Hereafter, and they denied it".

safi-cedvel:41-42.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is conjunctive. (إن) is negative. (إلّا) a particle of restriction. (هزوا) the second direct object, accusative, i.e. "mocked at". (الهمزة) is for interrogation. (رسولا) a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun, i.e. "Allah sent him as a messenger".
Clause: «رأوك ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «إن يتّخذونك ... » has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
Clause: «هذا الذي ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech of an implied saying, i.e. "they say: Is this the one who...", and the implied saying clause is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl from the agent of يتّخذونك ...
Clause: «بعث الله ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
(42) (إن) is the lightened form of the heavy (inna), necessarily inoperative. (اللام) is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa). (عن آلهتنا) attached to (يضلّنا), by implying in it the meaning "turns us away". (أن) is a maṣdar particle. (عليها) attached to (صبرنا).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن صبرنا ... ) is in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ, whose predicate is necessarily omitted ...
(الواو) is resumptive. (سوف) is a particle of futurity. (حين) an adverb, accusative, attached to (يعلمون). (من) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, a mubtadaʾ whose predicate is (أضلّ) [Note: or it is a relative noun in the position of an accusative, a direct object ... and (أضلّ) is the predicate of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو, the clause being the ṣila.], (سبيلا) a tamyīz, accusative.
Clause: «كاد ليضلّنا ... » has no grammatical position, being a resumption within the scope of the saying.
Clause: «يضلّنا ... » is in the position of an accusative, predicate of كاد.
Clause: «صبرنا (موجود)». has no grammatical position, being a resumption within the scope of the saying ...
The apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "we would have been turned away from them" ...
Clause: «صبرنا ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-like relative (أن).
Clause: «يعلمون ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «يرون ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «من أضلّ ... » is in the position of an accusative, a direct object - or it stands in for the two objects - of the verb يعلمون, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.

safi-cedvel:43-44.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for interrogation. (رأيت) in the sense of "tell me". (من) a relative noun in the position of an accusative, the first direct object. (إلهه) the second direct object, accusative. (هواه) the first direct object. (الهمزة) is for denial. (عليه) attached to (وكيلا).
Clause: «رأيت ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «اتخذ ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
Clause: «أنت تكون ... » is in the position of an accusative, the second direct object of the verb رأيت [Note: the fāʾ is redundant, for embellishment; or it is conjunctive, conjoining the clause أنت تكون to an implied clause that is the second object of the verb, i.e. "Are you concerned for him, so that you will be a guardian over him?"].
Clause: «تكون ... » is in the position of a nominative, predicate of the mubtadaʾ (أنت).
(44) (أم) is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, meaning "rather" (بل) and the hamza..
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ أكثرهم يسمعون ... ) is in the position of an accusative, standing in for the two objects of تحسب.
(إن) is negative. (إلّا) a particle of restriction. (كالأنعام) attached to an omitted predicate of the mubtadaʾ هم. (بل) is for the transitional iḍrāb.
Clause: «تحسب ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «يسمعون ... » is in the position of a nominative, predicate of أنّ.
Clause: «يعقلون ... » is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause يسمعون.
Clause: «إن هم كالأنعام» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «هم أضلّ سبيلا» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
1- Fronting: in His saying, the Exalted, أَرَأَيْتَ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إِلهَهُ هَواهُ.
«اتخذ» is transitive to two objects, the first of which is «هواه» and the second «إلهه», and the latter was put before the first for attention to it, in that it is the one around which the matter of wonder turns, not in that the deity deserves veneration and fronting, as has been said. That is: "Have you seen the one who made his desire a god for himself, by obeying it and building the matter of his religion upon it, turning away altogether from listening to the dazzling proof and heeding the luminous evidence?" in the sense of "look at him and wonder at him". Ibn al-Munayyir said of the fronting of the second object here: there is a fine subtlety in it, namely conveying restriction. For the speech - before the entry of (أرأيت - واتخذ) - originally was هواه إلهه, with هواه a mubtadaʾ whose predicate is إلهه; so when it is said: إلهه هواه, it is of the fronting of the predicate over the mubtadaʾ, which conveys restriction. So the meaning of the verse then is: "Have you seen one who takes as his object of worship nothing but his desire?", and that is more emphatic in censuring and reproaching him.
2- Tamthīl (representation): in His saying, the Exalted, إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا كَالْأَنْعامِ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا.
This art boils down to the speaker's wanting a meaning and not expressing it by its specific word, nor by two words of indication, nor by ridf, but by a word slightly further than the word of ridf, fit to be an example of the specific word, because an example does not resemble the exemplified in every respect; and if the two examples were alike in every respect they would be one.
And of tamthīl there is also another kind, favoured by those who came after Qudāma, which is that a thing be mentioned to serve as a model for the intended meaning, even if its meaning and wording differ from the intended meaning and wording: as if they, in their persistence in error, were in the position of cattle and beasts, indeed more astray in path, because beasts submit to whoever looks after them, and distinguish whoever does them good from whoever does them ill; as for these, they have sunk to a depth further than this.

* Benefits:
- حسب is one of the verbs of the heart, and it conveys in the predicate probability and certainty, the more frequent being probability. It governs two objects whose origin is the mubtadaʾ and the khabar.
a- An example of probability is the saying of Zufar ibn al-Ḥārith al-Kilābī:
وكنا حسبنا كل بيضاء شحمة ... ليالي لاقينا جذام وحميرا
(We used to reckon every white thing to be fat, in the nights when we met Judhām and Ḥimyar.)
b- An example of certainty: the saying of Labīd al-ʿĀmirī:
حسبت التقى والجود خير تجاره ... رباحا إذا ما المرء أصبح ثافلا
(I reckoned piety and generosity to be the best of his merchandise in profit, when a man finds himself heavy-laden.)
Its imperfect: يحسب with fatḥa or kasra on the sīn, and the maṣdar: محسبة and محسبة, with fatḥa on the sīn and also kasra, and حسبان.

safi-cedvel:45-46.t:
* I'rab
- (الهمزة) is for interrogation of wonder. (إلى ربّك) attached to (ترى) in the sense of "you look". (كيف) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative ḥāl whose governor is مدّ. (الواو) is conjunctive. (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle. (اللام) occurs in the apodosis of لو. (ساكنا) the second direct object, accusative. (عليه) attached to (دليلا).
Clause: «لم تر ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
Clause: «مدّ ... » is in the position of a genitive, a substitute for (ربّك) [Note: that is: "Have you not looked at your Lord's extending the shade?"].
Clause: «شاء ... » has no grammatical position, being parenthetical.
Clause: «جعله ساكنا» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
Clause: «جعلنا ... » is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause مدّ الظلّ. (إلينا) attached to (قبضناه). (قبضا) an absolute object, accusative.
Clause: «قبضناه ... » is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause جعلنا الشمس.

* Morphology:
(ساكنا): an active participle from سكن, meaning "he stayed" and "he became still"; its pattern is فاعل.
(دليلا): a derived adjective, its pattern is فعيل in the sense of فاعل, and it is said to be in the sense of مفعول, which is why it is not made feminine with الشمس; and دليل has come to be in the status of a noun, as one says الشمس برهان or الشمس حقّ.
(قبضا): a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral verb قبض; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {هَبَآءً}: al-habāʾ and al-habwa mean fine dust; so said Ibn ʿArafa. al-Jawharī said: "From it one says: habā yahbū when it rises, and ahbaytuhu I (made it rise), ihbāʾan." al-Khalīl and al-Zajjāj said: "It is like the dust that enters through a window opening and is seen with the light of the sun." It was also said: al-habāʾ is what flies off of the sparks of fire when it is kindled. The singular is habāʾa, on the pattern of tamr and tamra. {مَنْثُوراً} means scattered; I scattered (nathartu) the thing: I dispersed it. al-Nathra: scattered stars. al-Nathr: speech that is not in verse, as the counterpart of poetry. The benefit of describing it so is that you see al-habāʾ arranged in order with the light, but when you stir it, it disperses; so this description was brought to convey that. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or it is a third object of {جَعَلْنَاهُ}, that is: We made it combine the paltriness of al-habāʾ and its scatteredness, like His saying the Exalted: {كُونُواْ قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ} [al-Baqara: 65], that is: combining the transformation and the abasement." The Shaykh said: "Ibn Durustawayh, who differed with the grammarians in forbidding kāna to have two or more predicates, differed here; and the analogy of his position regarding {جَعَلَ} is that he would forbid it to have a third predicate." I said: His point is that al-Zamakhsharī's statement is refuted by analogy with what Ibn Durustawayh forbade, namely the enumeration of several predicates of kāna.

[Translator's note: the source has a slash mark ("/") in the middle of the sentence about the light; it is probably a printing artefact and is not translated.]

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {خَيْرٌ مُّسْتَقَرّاً وَأَحْسَنُ}: there are two views on afʿal (the elative form) here. One: that it is used in its usual sense of comparison. The meaning is that the believers are better in the Hereafter in their abode than the abode of the disbelievers, and finer in their resting-place (maqīl) than their resting-place, supposing they had one; or that they are better off in the Hereafter than they were in this world. The second: that it is merely descriptive, without any comparison.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ}: the operative (ʿāmil) of {يَوْمَ} is either "Remember!" (udhkur), or "Allah alone holds the dominion on the day when …", as indicated by His saying: {الملك يَوْمَئِذٍ الحق للرحمن} [al-Furqān: 26].

The Kufans and Abū ʿAmr read {تَشَقَّقُ} here and in Sūrat Qāf with lightening (of the shīn), and the rest with doubling (tashdīd). Both are clear. The former group dropped the imperfect-prefix tāʾ, or the tāʾ of the form tafaʿʿul, there being disagreement on that; the others assimilated the tāʾ of tafaʿʿul into the shīn because of their closeness (in articulation). They are like tazāharūn and tazzāharūn, one with omission and the other with assimilation. This has already been dealt with in al-Baqara.

His saying: {بالغمام}: there are three views on this bāʾ.
