First: that it is causal, that is, "because of the clouds", meaning because of the sky's being split by them, like {السَّمَآءُ مُنفَطِرٌ بِهِ} [al-Muzzammil: 18], as though it were that by which the sky is split. Second: that it indicates ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "accompanied by the clouds". Third: that it means ʿan ("from"), that is, "from the clouds", like His saying: {يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ الأرض عَنْهُمْ} [Qāf: 44].

His saying: {وَنُزِّلَ الملائكة}: there are twelve readings of it: two among the mutawātir ones and ten among the shādhdh (irregular) ones. Ibn Kathīr, of the Seven, read {وَنُنْزِلُ} with a nūn with ḍamma, then another nūn with sukūn, a light zāy with kasra, the imperfect of anzala, and {الملائكةَ} in the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). By rights the verbal noun after this reading should have come as inzāl. Abū ʿAlī said: "Since anzala and nazzala run the same course, he made the verbal noun of one follow the verbal noun of the other," and he cited as a line of poetry:

3482 - وقد تَطَوَّيْتُ انْطِواءَ الحِضْبِ ... (And I coiled myself up as the serpent coils)

"because taṭawwaytu and inṭawaytu have the same meaning." I said: Similar to it is {وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلاً} [al-Muzzammil: 8], that is, tabattulan. The rest of the Seven read {وَنُزِّلَ} with ḍamma on the nūn, kasra on the doubled zāy and fatḥa on the lām, a passive past verb; {الملائكةُ} is nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). It agrees with its verbal noun.

Ibn Masʿūd and Abū Rajāʾ read {وَنَزَّلَ} with doubling, a past verb in the active, the agent being Allah the Exalted, and {الملائكةَ} a direct object. On his authority also is {وَأَنْزَلَ} in the active, making it transitive by doubling in the one reading and by the hamza in the other. The excuse for its verbal noun's coming on the pattern tafʿīl is like the excuse offered for Ibn Kathīr. On his authority also is {وَأُنْزِلَ} in the passive.

Hārūn, on the authority of Abū ʿAmr, read {وَتُنَزِّل الملائكةُ} with tāʾ from above (i.e. the two-dotted tāʾ), doubled zāy and a ḍamma on the lām, an imperfect in the active, with {الملائكةُ} nominative, the imperfect of nazzala with doubling; on this reading the object is omitted, that is: "the angels send down what they were commanded to send down."

al-Khaffāf, on his authority, and Janāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh read {وَنَزَلَ} lightened, active, with {الملائكةُ} nominative. Khārija, on the authority of Abū ʿAmr also, and Abū Muʿādh read {وَنُزِّلُ} with ḍamma on the nūn and a doubled zāy, and {الملائكةَ} accusative. The original is wa-nunazzilu with two nūns, one of which was omitted.

Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr, in a transmission from them, read this original form {وَنُنَزِّل} with two nūns and a doubled zāy. Ubayy read {وَنُزِّلَتْ} with doubling, passive, and {وَتَنَزَّلَتْ} with an added tāʾ at its beginning, and the tāʾ of the feminine in both.

Abū ʿAmr, by the route of al-Khaffāf from him, read {وَنُزِلَ} with ḍamma on the nūn and a light kasra on the zāy, passive. The author of al-Lawāmiḥ said: "If the reading is sound, then the muḍāf (the first term of the genitive construct) has been dropped and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place; the implied form is: wa-nuzila nuzūlu l-malāʾikati ('the descent of the angels was sent down'), so al-nuzūl was dropped and its case-ending transferred to al-malāʾika, the sense being: nuzila nāzilu l-malāʾikati, because the verbal noun can come in the sense of a noun. This is among what follows Sībawayh's position, in the arrangement of building the intransitive for the direct object, because the verb indicates its verbal noun." I said: This is a great deal of contrivance, to which the necessity of the craft drove him. Ibn Jinnī said: "This is not well known, because nazala does not take a direct object so as to be built (in the passive) here for the angels. Its justification is that it be like zukima l-rajulu ('the man was given a cold') and junna ('he was driven mad'), for it is only said: azkamahu and ajannahu Allāh, and this is a matter of transmission, not of analogy." I said: The like of this reading is what came earlier in Sūrat al-Kahf, in the reading of the one who read {فَلاَ يقوم له يَوْمَ القيامة وَزْناً} [verse 105] with the accusative of {وَزْناً}, in respect of making an intransitive verb transitive, and what is said about it has already been presented.

[Translator's note: the source has a slash mark ("/") after "Sībawayh" in the passage quoted from al-Lawāmiḥ; it appears to be a printing artefact and is not translated. The source also has the misprint "لقيامةِ" for "لقيامِه" ("for its standing") in the discussion of the reading of the rest of the Seven, and "أَْنْ" for "أَنْ" in Ibn Jinnī's passage; neither affects the sense.]

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {الملك يَوْمَئِذٍ}: there are several views on it. First: that {الْمُلْكُ} is mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is {الْحَقُّ}, with {يَوْمَئِذٍ} attached to {الْمُلْكُ}; and {لِلرَّحْمَنِ} is attached to {الْحَقُّ}, or to an omitted element by way of clarification, or to an omitted element as an adjective of {الْحَقُّ}. Second: that the khabar is {يَوْمَئِذٍ} and {الْحَقُّ} is a naʿt (adjective) of {الْمُلْكُ}, with {لِلرَّحْمَنِ} as above. Third: that the khabar is {لِلرَّحْمَنِ}, with {يَوْمَئِذٍ} attached to {الْمُلْكُ}, and {الْحَقُّ} an adjective of {الْمُلْكُ}.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ}: it is governed by an omitted verb, or it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to {يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ}. {يَعَضُّ} is the imperfect of ʿaḍḍa, and its pattern is faʿila with kasra on the ʿayn, by the evidence of their saying ʿaḍiḍtu aʿaḍḍu; al-Kisāʾī reported a fatḥa on it in the past tense, and on that basis one would say aʿiḍḍu with kasra in the imperfect. Biting here is a figurative expression (kināya) for the intensity of clinging. Similar is "he burned his canine tooth" (ḥaraqa nābahu); the poet said:

3483 - أبى الضَّيْمَ والنُّعمانُ يَحْرِقُ نابَه ... عليه فأفضى والسيوفُ مَعاقِلُهْ (He refused humiliation while al-Nuʿmān ground his canine against him; so he went out, his refuges being swords)

This figurative expression is more eloquent than stating the thing alluded to outright. The al- in {الظالم} may be for a specific referent (ʿahd) or for the genus, depending on the disagreement about that.

His saying: {يَقُولُ}: this clause is ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of {يَعَضُّ}. The clause of wishing after the saying is quoted by it (maḥkiyya). The discussion of the direct attachment of yā to layta has already been given in al-Nisāʾ.

fulān is a figurative expression for the proper name of a rational being, and it is fully declinable (munṣarif). fulu is a figurative expression for an indefinite rational male, and fulatu for a rational female; al-fulān and al-fulāna, with the definite article, are for a non-rational. fulu and fulatu are restricted to the vocative except in poetic necessity, as in his saying:

3484 - في لَجَّةٍ أَمْسِكْ فُلاناً عن فُلِ (In a tumult, hold So-and-so back from So-and-so)

fulu is not a shortened form (murakhkham) of fulān, contrary to al-Farrāʾ. The Shaykh claimed that Ibn ʿUṣfūr, Ibn Mālik and Ibn al-ʿIlj erred in making fulu a figurative expression for the proper name of a rational being like fulān. The lām of fulu and fulān has two views: one, that it is a wāw; the other, that it is a yāʾ. al-Ḥasan read {يا ويلتي} with kasra on the tāʾ and an explicit yāʾ after it, which is the original. al-Dūrī read it with imāla. Abū ʿAlī said: "Leaving off imāla is better, because the origin of this word is the yāʾ, so the kasra was replaced by a fatḥa and the yāʾ by an alif, in flight from the yāʾ. So the one who uses imāla returns to what he first fled from." I said: This is refuted by the like of bāʿa ('he sold'), whose origin is the yāʾ and yet they used imāla; and they used imāla in {يا حسرتى عَلَى مَا فَرَّطَتُ} [al-Zumar: 56] and {يَا أَسَفَى} [Yūsuf: 84], both of which are like {يا ويلتى} in that their alif stands for the yāʾ of the first-person speaker.

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying: {وَكَانَ الشيطان}: it is possible that this clause is part of what the wrongdoer says, in which case it is accusative in position as the object of the saying; and it is possible that it is part of what the Lord the Exalted says, in which case it has no grammatical position because it is resumptive.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {مَهْجُوراً}: the second object of {اتَّخَذُوا}, or a ḥāl. It is a passive participle from al-hajr with fatḥa on the hāʾ, which means abandoning and distancing; that is, they made it abandoned and distant.
It was also said: it is from al-hujr with ḍamma, that is, "spoken of foolishly" (mahjūran fīhi), in that they say of it: it is poetry and tales of the ancients. al-Zamakhsharī made mafʿūl here a verbal noun in the sense of al-hajr, saying: "like al-majlūd and al-maʿqūl." I said: That is not analogical; the lexicographers fixed it in a few small words, and these are not extended except by transmission.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {هَادِياً}: ḥāl or tamyīz (specification). The i'rab of a clause like this has already been given.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {جُمْلَةً}: ḥāl from the Qurʾān, since it is in the sense of "gathered together" (mujtamaʿan).

His saying: {كَذَلِكَ}: it is either nominative in position, that is, "the matter is thus"; and {لِنُثَبِّتَ} gives the reason for an omitted element, that is, "We did that in order to strengthen"; or it is accusative as a ḥāl, that is, "He sent down the like of that"; or as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), with {لِنُثَبِّتَ} attached to that omitted verb. Abū Ḥātim said: "It is the answer to an oath." This is a weaker view toward which al-Akhfash inclined, and he took from it {وَلِتَصْغَى}; it has already been presented in al-Anʿām.

ʿAbd Allāh read {لِيُثَبِّتَ} with yāʾ, that is, Allah the Exalted.

al-Tartīl: separation, and the coming of one word after another with slight pause, without cutting the breath. From it comes "a rattal (well-spaced) and murattal mouth", that is, with gapped teeth, between whose teeth are slight gaps.

al-Zamakhsharī said: "{نُزِّلَ} here means anzala and nothing else, like khabbara in the sense of akhbara; otherwise the two would conflict." He means that nazzala with doubling in its origin implies gradual and separated sending down, so if it were not made to mean anzala, which does not imply that, it would conflict with His saying {جُمْلَةً}, because "all at once" is the opposite of separation. This is built on his own doctrine, that doubling indicates separation; he stated this explicitly in several places in his book al-Kashshāf. That was presented in al-Baqara, at the beginning of Āl ʿImrān and at the end of al-Isrāʾ, and there he reported from Ibn ʿAbbās something whose apparent sense supports its soundness.

semin-durr:33-33.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ جِئْنَاكَ بالحق}: this exception is "emptied" (mufarragh). The clause is accusative in position as a ḥāl, that is, "they do not come to you with a parable except in the state of Our coming to you with such-and-such." The meaning: they do not come to you with a wondrous question except that We come to you with the true matter. {تَفْسِيراً} is tamyīz (specification), and the thing compared against (al-mufaḍḍal ʿalayhi) is omitted, that is, "a better explanation than theirs."

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {الذين يُحْشَرُونَ}: it may be nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "they are those who …". It may be accusative in the manner of censure (ʿalā l-dhamm). It may be nominative by being a mubtadaʾ, its khabar being the clause {أولئك شَرٌّ مَّكَاناً}. It is also possible that {أولئك} is a badal (substitute) of, or an explication (bayān) of, the relative noun, and {شَرٌّ مكاناً} the khabar of the relative noun.

semin-durr:35-35.t: His saying: {هَارُونَ}: a badal or an explication, or accusative by the manner of severance (qaṭʿ). {وَزِيراً} is the second object; it was also said that it is a ḥāl, the second object being His saying {مَعَهُ}.

semin-durr:36-36.t: His saying: {فَدَمَّرْنَاهُمْ}: the majority read {فَدَمَّرْنَا} as a past verb, conjoined to an omitted element, that is, "so the two of them went, and they (the people) called them liars, so We destroyed them." ʿAlī, may Allah honour his face, read {فَدَمِّرَاهُمْ} as an imperative addressed to Mūsā and Hārūn. On his authority also {فَدَمِّرَانِّهُمْ}, likewise, but emphasized with the heavy nūn. On his authority also {فَدَمِّرَا بِهِمْ} with an added genitive bāʾ after the imperative verb, which resembles the preceding reading in writing. al-Zamakhsharī reported from him {فَدَمَّرْتُهُمْ} with the tāʾ of the first-person speaker.

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying: {وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ}: it may be accusative, conjoined to the object of {دَمَّرْنَاهُمْ}. It may be accusative by an implied verb which His saying {أَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ} explains; this is favoured by the verbal clause that precedes it. This is if we say that {لَمَّا} is an adverb of time; but if we say that it is a particle of "occurrence due to occurrence" (ḥarf wujūb li-wujūb), that is not possible, because {أَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ} would then be the apodosis (jawāb) of {لَمَّا}, and its apodosis does not explain (another word). It may also be accusative by an implied verb not by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation), that is, "Remember the people of Nūḥ."

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying: {وَعَاداً}: there are three views on it: that it is conjoined to {قَوْمَ نُوحٍ}; that it is conjoined to the object of {جَعَلْنَاهُمْ}; and that it is conjoined to the position of {لِلظَّالِمِينَ}, because it has the force of "We promised the wrongdoers a punishment."

His saying: {وَأَصْحَابَ الرس}: there are two views on it. One: that it is a conjunction of a different thing (ʿaṭf al-mughāyir), which is the apparent sense. The second: that it is a conjunction of some attributes on others. By "the people of al-Rass" is meant Thamūd, because al-rass is a well that has not been lined (with stones), on the authority of Abū ʿUbayd, and Thamūd were people of wells. It was also said: al-Rass is a river in the east; and it is said that they were a people who worshipped idols and killed their prophet and "rassawhu" in a well, that is, they thrust him into it.

His saying: {بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ}: {ذَلِكَ} refers to those mentioned before, who are many groups; that is why {بَيْنَ} is good with it.

semin-durr:39-39.t: His saying: {وَكُلاًّ ضَرَبْنَا لَهُ الأمثال}: it may be accusative by a verb that what follows explains, that is, "We warned" or "We reminded", since both are in the sense of "We struck parables for him." It may also be conjoined to what preceded, with {ضَرَبْنَا} an explanation of the reason for their destruction. As for the second {كُلاًّ}, it is a fronted direct object.

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {مَطَرَ السوء}: there are three views on it. First: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) with the augments removed, that is, imṭār al-sawʾ ("the raining of evil"). Second: that it is a second object, since the meaning is "I gave it and bestowed upon it the rain of evil." Third: that it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "a raining like the rain of evil."

Zayd ibn ʿAlī read {مُطِرَتْ}, triliteral and passive, and maṭara is transitive. He said:

3485 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كَمَنْ بِوادِيْه بعد المَحْلِ مَمْطورِ (… like one in whose valley, after drought, rain has fallen)

Abū l-Sammāl read {مَطَرَ السُّوء} with ḍamma on the sīn. The discussion of al-sūʾ and al-sawʾ has already been given in Barāʾa.

His saying: {أَتَوْا عَلَى القرية}: atā is made transitive with ʿalā only because it was made to include the meaning of "passed by" (marra).

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {إِن يَتَّخِذُونَكَ}: {إِنْ} is negative, and {هُزُواً} is a second object. It is possible that the implied form is "an object of mockery", or "mocked at in you". This negated clause admits two views. One: that it is the jawāb (apodosis) of the conditional. {إذا} is distinguished in that when its apodosis is negated by mā, in or lā, it does not need the fāʾ, unlike the other conditional particles. On this view, His saying {أهذا الذي} is accusative in position as the object of an implied saying; and that implied saying is accusative in position as a ḥāl, that is, "they take you only as an object of mockery, saying that." The second: that it is a parenthetical clause between {إذا} and its apodosis; its apodosis is that implied saying which is quoted by {أهذا الذي}, and the implied form is: "When they see you they say: 'Is this the one whom Allah sent …?'", the negated clause having interposed. The object of {بَعَثَ} is omitted; it is the relative pronoun's returning referent, that is, baʿathahu. {رَسُولاً} is on its regular footing in being an adjective, so it is accusative as a ḥāl. It was also said that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of risāla (message), in which case it is by omission of a muḍāf, that is, "possessing a message" (dhā rasūl, meaning dhā risāla); or the maṣdar itself is made the thing for emphasis; or it is in the sense of "one sent" (mursal). This is strained.

[Translator's note: the source has a slash mark ("/") after "maṣdar"; it appears to be a printing artefact and is not translated.]

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying: {إِن كَادَ لَيُضِلُّنَا}: its like has already been given in Sūrat Subḥān (al-Isrāʾ).

His saying: {لَوْلاَ أَن صَبَرْنَا}: its apodosis is omitted, that is, "we would have gone astray from our gods." al-Zamakhsharī said: "In speech of this kind lawlā runs its course, in terms of meaning though not in terms of the craft, as a qualification of an unrestricted ruling."

His saying: {مَنْ أَضَلُّ}: the interrogative clause is suspended (muʿallaqa) from {يَعْلَمُونَ}, so it takes the place of its two objects if it is used in its usual sense, and the place of one if it is in the sense of "knew" (ʿarafa). It is possible that {مَنْ} is a relative noun, with {أَضَلُّ} as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, which is the returning referent to {مَنْ}, its implied form being man huwa aḍallu. It was omitted only because of the lengthening caused by the tamyīz, like their saying "I am not the one who is a sayer of evil to you." This is clear if it is transitive to one object; if it is transitive to two, it needs a second implied element, and there is no need for that.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
His saying: {مَنِ اتخذ إلهه هَوَاهُ}: the two objects of ittikhādh (taking), without fronting or delaying, since they are equal in definiteness. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why did He put {هَوَاهُ} last, when the original is your saying 'he took desire as a god'? I say: it is only the fronting of the second object before the first out of concern for it, as you say 'I knew the one departing to be Zayd', because of your greater concern for the one departing." The Shaykh said: "The claim of inversion, meaning fronting, is not good, because it is one of the necessities of poetry." I said: Three views on this have already been presented. In any case this is not the inversion mentioned at all; it is only fronting and delaying.

Ibn Hurmuz read {إِلَاهَةً هَوَاهُ} on the pattern fiʿāla. al-Ilāha means "that which is worshipped" (al-maʾlūh), and the hāʾ is for emphasis, like ʿallāma and nassāba. {إِلَاهَةً} is a second object that was fronted because it is indefinite, and that is why it is fully declined (muṣraf). It was also said: al-Ilāha is the sun. This was refuted: it should have been a diptote because of being a proper name and feminine. The reply was that al- often enters upon it, so when it was removed from it, it became indefinite and ran in the way of attributes. It is also said: ulāha, with ḍamma on the hamza, as a name for the sun.

Some of the Medinese read {آلِهَةً هَوَاهُ}, the plural of ilāh; it too is a fronted object, and it was made plural with regard to kinds, for a man used to worship various gods. The first object of {أَرَأَيْتَ} is {مَنْ}, and the second is the interrogative clause.

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying: {كَيْفَ}: it is accusative by {مَدَّ}, and it suspends (muʿallaqa) {تَرَ}, so it is in the position of the accusative. What is said of {أَلَمْ تَرَ} has already been given.

His saying: {ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the position of {ثُمَّ} in these two places? I say: its position is to show the gradation of the three matters, as though the second were greater than the first, and the third greater than both in comparison, because of the distance between them in excellence, as the distance between them in time."

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying: {لِّنُحْيِيَ بِهِ}: there are two views on it. The clearer: that it is attached to the sending down. The second, which is weak: that it is attached to {طَهُوراً}. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: the sending down of water described as pure, and giving the reason for it as giving life and water to drink, signals that purity is a condition for the soundness of that, as you say 'The prince carried me on a fine horse so that I might hunt wild game on it'? I say: since the watering of human beings was among the things for which the water was sent down, it was described as pure, to honour them and to complete the favour upon them."

{طَهُورٌ} may be an intensive adjective transferred from ṭāhir (pure), like His saying the Exalted: {شَرَاباً طَهُوراً} [al-Insān: 21], and he said:

3486 - إلى رُجَّح الأَكْفالِ غِيْدٍ من الصِّبا ... عِذابِ الثَّنايا رِيْقُهُنَّ طَهُوْرُ (Toward heavy-hipped women, soft-necked from youth, sweet of front teeth, whose saliva is pure)

It may be a noun for that with which one purifies oneself, like al-saḥūr; and it may be a maṣdar like al-qabūl and al-walūʿ. {بَلْدَةً} is described by {مَيْتاً}, which is an adjective of the thing mentioned because it is in the sense of "land" (balad).

His saying: {وَنُسْقِيَهُ}: the majority read it with ḍamma on the nūn. Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim, in a transmission from them, and Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with fatḥa. It has already been given that it was read so in al-Naḥl and al-Muʾminūn, and what people said of the two has also been given.

His saying: {مِمَّا خَلَقْنَآ}: it may be attached to {نُسْقِيَهُ}, and it is for the starting-point of the goal (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya). It may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from {أَنْعَاماً}. The cattle and the human beings are indefinite. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because the elite of the people and most of them are camped by the wadis and rivers, they have no need of water being given to drink; but their descendants, and there are many of them, are kept alive only by what Allah sends down of His mercy and the watering of His sky."

His saying: {وَأَنَاسِيَّ}: there are two views on it. One, the position of Sībawayh: that it is the plural of insān. The original is insān, anāsīn; the nūn was replaced by yāʾ and the yāʾ before it assimilated into it, like ẓirbān and ẓarābiyy. The second, the position of al-Farrāʾ, al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjāj: that it is the plural of insiyy. This is open to question, because the pattern faʿālī is the plural only of what has a doubled yāʾ that does not indicate relation (nisba), such as kursiyy and karāsiyy. If by kursiyy the relational sense were intended, it would not be permissible to pluralize it as karāsiyy. And it is unlikely to say that the yāʾ in insiyy is not relational, since it should have been pluralized as anāsiya like mahālaba for al-Muhallabī and azāriqa for al-Azraqī.

[Translator's note: the source has a slash mark ("/") before "If by kursiyy the relational sense"; it appears to be a printing artefact and is not translated.]

Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥārith al-Dhimārī and al-Kisāʾī, in a transmission, read {وَأَنَاسِيَ} with lightened yāʾ. al-Zamakhsharī said: "By dropping the yāʾ of afāʿīl, as you say anāʿim for anāʿīm." And he said: "If you say: why did He put the giving of life to the earth and the watering of the cattle before the watering of human beings? I say: because the life of human beings is through the life of their earth and the life of their cattle, so He put first what is the cause of their life; and because when they have gained the watering of their earth and of their cattle, they will not lack their own watering."

semin-durr:50-50.t: His saying: {وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَاهُ}: the pronoun may refer to the Qurʾān, or to the water, that is, "We have varied its descent: in downpour, dew, heavy rain, drizzle and the like." ʿIkrima read {صَرَفْنَاهُ} with a light rāʾ.

semin-durr:52-52.t: His saying: {وَجَاهِدْهُمْ بِهِ}: that is, with the Qurʾān; or with refusing obedience, indicated by His saying {فَلاَ تُطِعِ}; or with what is indicated by {وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَبَعَثْنَا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ نَّذِيراً}, namely that he is a warner to all the towns; or with the sword.

semin-durr:53-53.t:
His saying: {مَرَجَ البحرين}: there are two views on maraja. One: that it means "mixed" (khalaṭa) and "mingled"; from it comes maraja l-amr, that is, "the matter became confused"; so said Ibn ʿArafa. It was also said: maraja means "made flow", and amraja is a dialectal variant of it. It was said: maraja is the dialect of the Hijaz and amraja the dialect of Najd. In the speech of one of the eloquent: "Two seas, each mixed (mamrūj) with the other, and the sweet water of them mixed with the bitter."

His saying: {هذا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ وهذا مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ}: this clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive, an answer to an implied question, as though someone had asked: "How is their mixing?" and it was said: "This one is sweet, and this one is salty." It may, though weakly, be a ḥāl. al-Furāt is that which is extreme in sweetness. The tāʾ in it is radical, the lām of the word; its pattern is fuʿāl, and some Arabs pause on it with a hāʾ. This is like what was given earlier for al-tābūt. It is said that sweet water was called furāt because it "furtu" the thirst, that is, splits and cuts it. al-Ujāj: that which is extreme in saltiness. It was also said: in heat; and it was said: in bitterness. This is among the finest antitheses, in that the Exalted says "sweet furāt" and "salty ujāj". I recited some verses of one of them:

3487 - فلا واللهِ لا أَنْفَكُّ أَبْكي ... إلى أَنْ نَلْتَقِي شُعْثاً عُراتا (No, by Allah, I shall not cease weeping until we meet, dishevelled and bare)
أألحى إنْ نَزَحْتُ أُجاجَ عَيْني ... على جَدَثٍ حوى العَذْبَ الفُراتَا (Am I to be blamed if I drain the bitter water of my eye over a grave that holds the sweet, fresh water?)

How fine that he alluded to his tears as ujāj, and to the one wept for as the sweet furāt. The reason I recited these two verses was that some people had accused their speaker of a solecism in his saying ʿurātā: "How can he pause on the feminine tāʾ with tanwīn, using an alif?" I said: It is a widespread dialect; they treat the tāʾ like other letters and replace its tanwīn, after a fatḥa, with an alif. They related of them: akaltu tamratā, like akaltu zaytā.

Ṭalḥa and Qutayba, from al-Kisāʾī, read {مَلِحٌ} with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the lām, and likewise in Sūrat Fāṭir; it is a shortened form of mālih, as in their saying baridun for bārid. He said:

3488 - وصِلِّيانا بَرِدا (… and a cool ṣilliyān plant)

and "māʾ mālih" is an irregular dialect. Abū Ḥātim said: "This is an objectionable reading."

[Translator's note: the sentence "وماء مالح لغة شاذة" is printed as written; it follows the verse fragment in the source, and its exact sense there is unclear.]

His saying: {وَحِجْراً مَّحْجُوراً}: the apparent sense is that it is conjoined to {بَرْزَخاً}. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the meaning of {حِجْراً مَّحْجُوراً}? I say: it is the phrase said by one seeking refuge, which we have already explained, and it occurs here figuratively, as though each of the two seas says to its fellow: 'Ḥijran maḥjūran', and this is among the finest metaphors." On what he says, it is accusative by an implied saying.

His saying: {بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخاً}: it is possible that the adverbial phrase is attached to the making (al-jaʿl), and possible that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from {بَرْزَخاً}; the first is clearer.

semin-durr:54-54.t: His saying: {مِنَ المآء}: it may be attached to {خَلَقَ}, and it may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from {ماء}; {مِنْ} is for the starting-point or for partitioning. As for al-ṣihr (relation by marriage), al-Khalīl said: "It is said of the family of the woman's house only aṣhār, and of the family of the man's house only akhtān." He said: "Some of the Arabs apply aṣhār to all of them," and this is the more common.

semin-durr:55-55.t: His saying: {على رَبِّهِ}: it may be attached to {ظَهِيراً}, which is the apparent sense, or it may be attached to an omitted element as the khabar of {كَانَ}, with {ظَهِيراً} a ḥāl. al-Ẓahīr: the helper.

semin-durr:57-57.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ}: there are two views on it. One: that it is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ), that is, "but whoever wishes to take a way to his Lord, let him do so." The second: that it is connected, with an omitted muḍāf, meaning "except the reward of the one who …", that is, the reward obtained for his calling to faith and the other's acceptance of it, because the Exalted will reward me for that. So the Shaykh related it. This is open to question, because the negated asking is not, in the apparent sense, ascribed to Allah the Exalted; it is ascribed only to those addressed. How, then, can this implied form be sound?

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying: {الذي خَلَقَ السماوات}: on the reading of the majority, with {الرَّحْمَنُ} nominative, there are several views on it. One: that it is a mubtadaʾ with {الرَّحْمَنُ} as its khabar; that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is, "He is the One who created"; that it is accusative by an implied verb; and that it is an adjective of {الْحَيِّ الَّذِي لَا يَمُوتُ}, or a badal, or a bayān. As for the reading of Zayd ibn ʿAlī, {الرَّحْمَنِ} in the genitive, it is necessarily the case that {الذي خلق} is only an adjective of {الْحَيِّ}, so that there is no separation between the adjective and what it describes by a foreign element.

His saying: {الرحمن}: for the one who read it nominative, there are several views. One: that it is the khabar of {الذي خَلَقَ}, which has already been given; or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is, "He is al-Raḥmān"; or a badal from the pronoun in {اسْتَوَى}; or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause {فَاسْأَلْ بِهِ}, in the view of al-Akhfash, as in his saying:

3489 - وقائلةٍ خَوْلانُ فانكِحْ فتاتَهُمْ ... (And one saying: "Khawlān! so marry their girl …")

or an adjective of {الذي خلق}, if we say it is nominative. As for the reading of Zayd, it is necessarily an adjective.

His saying {بِهِ}: there are two views on the bāʾ. One: that it is on its regular footing, attached to the asking. By {خَبِيراً} is meant Allah the Exalted, and it is a case of tajrīd (abstraction), as you say "I met a lion in him." The meaning: "So ask Allah, the One informed of all things." al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or: ask, by asking Him, one who is informed, as you say: 'I saw a lion in him', that is, by seeing him." End. It is possible that the bāʾ is a complement of {خَبِيراً}, and {خَبِيراً} is the object of {اسْأَلْ} on this view, or accusative as a confirmatory ḥāl. Abū l-Baqāʾ considered it weak. He said: "It is weak for {خَبِيراً} to be a ḥāl from the agent of {اسْأَلْ}, because the one informed is asked only by way of emphasis, like His saying {وَهُوَ الحق مُصَدِّقاً} [al-Baqara: 91]." Then he said: "It may be a ḥāl from {الرحمن} if you make it nominative by {اسْتَوَى}."

The second: that the bāʾ means ʿan ("about"), either absolutely, or with asking in particular, as in this noble verse and as in the poet's saying:

3490 - فإنْ تَسْأَلُوني بالنِّساءِ . . . (If you ask me about women …)

the verse. The pronoun in ʿanhu refers to Allah the Exalted, and {خَبِيراً} is among the attributes of the angel, namely Jibrīl, peace be upon him. On this view, that is, that {خَبِيراً} is among the attributes of Jibrīl, the bāʾ may be on its regular footing, attached to {خَبِيراً} as already said, that is, "So ask the well-informed about Him."

[Translator's note: the source has a slash mark ("/") after "badal" in the first paragraph; it appears to be a printing artefact and is not translated.]

semin-durr:60-60.t: His saying: {لِمَا تَأْمُرُنَا}: the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read {يَأْمُرُنَا} with the yāʾ of the third person, meaning Muḥammad ﷺ. The rest read it in the second person, meaning: "what you command us, O Muḥammad." {مَا} may mean "that which" (alladhī), with the returning referent omitted, because it is attached, since amara is made to govern a second object by dropping the preposition. There is no need for the gradual derivation that Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned, namely that the original is: li-mā tamurunā bi-l-sujūd lahu, then bi-sujūdihi, then tamurunāhu, then tamurunā. So he put it, then said: "This is on the position of Abū l-Ḥasan; as for the position of Sībawayh, it is omission of that without the gradual derivation." I said: This is not the position of Sībawayh. {مَا} may also be indefinite-qualified (mawṣūfa), and what is said about its returning referent is the same as when it is relative. It may also be maṣdariyya, with the lām for cause, that is, "Shall we prostrate because of your command?" and on this view the one prostrated to is omitted, that is, "Shall we prostrate to al-Raḥmān because of what you command us?" On this view {مَا} does not refer to a rational being, whereas in the first two views that is possible, and that is what comes to mind first.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying: {سِرَاجاً}: the majority read it in the singular, and the sun is meant by it; this is supported by the mention of the moon after it. The two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read {سُرُجاً} with two ḍammas, a plural, like ḥumur for ḥimār. It was made plural with regard to the shining stars. The moon is mentioned only to honour it, as in His saying {وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ} [al-Baqara: 98], after both were included among the angels. al-Aʿmash, al-Nakhaʿī and Ibn Waththāb read likewise, except that the rāʾ has sukūn for lightness. al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash, al-Nakhaʿī and ʿĀṣim, in the transmission of ʿIṣma, read {قُمْراً} with ḍamma and sukūn, which is the plural of qamrāʾ (moonlit), like ḥumr for ḥamrāʾ. The meaning is: "and possessor of moonlit nights, giving light," in which the muḍāf was dropped and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place, then attention turned back to the muḍāf after its omission, so he described it with {مُنِيراً}. Had he not taken it into account, he would have said munīratan (feminine). The like of paying regard to it after its omission is the saying of Ḥassān:

3491 - يَسْقُون مَنْ وَرَدَ البَريْصَ عليهمِ ... بردى يُصَفَّقُ بالرَّحيقِ السَّلْسَلِ (They give to drink whoever comes to al-Barīṣ, over them, Baradā, mixed with pure, flowing wine)

The original is "the water of Baradā"; he dropped it, then paid regard to it in his saying yuṣaffaqu with yāʾ from below; had it not been so, he would have said tuṣaffaqu with tāʾ from above. Yet Ḥassān's verse may be like his saying:

3492 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا أرضَ أَبْقَلَ إبْقالها (… nor any land that put forth herbage as its (land) put forth herbage)

though Ibn Kaysān permits it as a general latitude.

semin-durr:62-62.t:
His saying: {خِلْفَةً}: there are two views on it. One: that it is a second object. The second: that it is a ḥāl, according to the two views on {جَعَلَ}. khilfa may be a maṣdar of khalafahu yakhlufuhu, when it comes in his place; it may be a noun of manner, like al-rikba; and it may be from "difference" (ikhtilāf), as in his saying:

3493 - ولها بالماطِرُوْنَ إذا ... أكلِ النملُ الذي جَمَعا (And she has at al-Māṭirūn, when the ants have eaten what she had gathered,)
خِلْفةً حتى إذا ارتَبَعَتْ ... سَكَنَتْ مِنْ جِلَّقٍ بِيعاً (succession (khilfa) until, when she had pastured in the spring, she dwelt in the churches of Jilliq,)
في بيوتٍ وَسْطَ دَسْكَرةٍ ... حَوْلَها الزيتونُ قد يَنَعا (in houses in the midst of a village, around which the olives have ripened)

and similar is the saying of Zuhayr:

3494 - بها العِيْنُ والآرام يَمْشِيْنَ خِلْفَةً ... (There the wild cattle and the gazelles walk in succession …)

{خِلْفَةً} is in the singular. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Because the meaning is that one of the two succeeds the other, and this is realized only through both of them." End.

al-Shukūr, with ḍamma, is a maṣdar in the sense of al-shukr; with fatḥa it is an intensive adjective.

[Translator's note: the source has a slash mark ("/") after "yakhlufu"; it appears to be a printing artefact and is not translated.]

semin-durr:63-63.t:
His saying: {وَعِبَادُ الرحمن}: nominative as a mubtadaʾ. There are two views on its khabar. One: the last clause at the end of the sūra: {أولئك يُجْزَوْنَ} [verse 75], with which al-Zamakhsharī began; {والذين يَمْشُونَ} and what follows are attributes of the mubtadaʾ. The second: that the khabar is {يَمْشُونَ}. The majority read ʿibād. The Yemeni (reader) read ʿubbād, with ḍamma on the ʿayn and doubled bāʾ, the plural of ʿābid. al-Ḥasan read ʿubud, with two ḍammas.

The majority read {يَمْشُونَ} lightened, active. The Yemeni and al-Sulamī read it with doubling, passive.

His saying: {هَوْناً}: either a naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar, that is, "a gentle walking", or a ḥāl, that is, "gentle." al-Hawn: softness and gentleness.

His saying: {سَلاَماً}: it may be accusative as a maṣdar of an omitted verb, that is, "we say salām", or "we offer a greeting from you, we do not act ignorantly toward you", salām having been put in the place of tasllīm. It may be accusative as a direct object, that is, "they said this utterance." al-Zamakhsharī said: that is, "they said sound speech in which they are safe from harm." What is meant is their safety from foolishness, as in:

3495 - ألا لا يَجْهَلَنْ أحدٌ علينا ... فنجهلَ فوقَ جَهْلِ الجاهِلينا (Let none act ignorantly toward us, lest we outdo the ignorance of the ignorant)

Sībawayh preferred that by salām is meant safety (salāma) and not greeting, because the believers were never commanded to greet the disbelievers, but were commanded only to coexist peacefully; then that was abrogated. Sībawayh did not mention abrogation anywhere in his book except in this verse.

semin-durr:64-64.t: His saying: {سُجَّداً}: the khabar of {يَبِيتُونَ}; it is weak to take it as complete (tāmma), that is, "they entered into spending the night". {سُجَّداً} is a ḥāl. {لِرَبِّهِمْ} is attached to {سُجَّداً}. He put prostration before standing, although it comes after it in the action, to keep the verse endings in agreement. sujjadan is the plural of sājid, like ḍurrab for ḍārib. Abū l-Barhasam read {سُجُوداً} on the pattern quʿūd. yabītu is the common dialect; the Azd of al-Sarāt and Bujayla say yabātu, which is the dialect of the common people today.

semin-durr:65-65.t:
His saying: {غَرَاماً}: that is, clinging and permanent. From al-Ḥasan: every creditor (gharīm) leaves his debtor except the creditor of Hell. They recited the saying of Bishr ibn Abī Khāzim:

3496 - ويومُ النِّسَارِ ويومُ الجِفا ... رِ كانا عَذاباً وكانا غَراما (And the day of al-Nisār and the day of al-Jifār, both were torment and both were ghirām)

And al-Aʿshā said:

3497 - إن يُعاقِبْ يكُنْ غَراماً وإنْ يُع ... طِ جَزِيلاً فإنَّه لا يُبالي (If He punishes, it will be ghirām, and if He gives abundantly, He does not care)

So ghirām means "clinging" (lāzim).

semin-durr:66-66.t:
His saying: {سَآءَتْ}: it may be in the sense of "grieved" (aḥzanat), in which case it is a fully conjugated verb governing a direct object, which here is omitted: "it, that is Jahannam, grieved its inmates and those who enter it." {مُسْتَقَرّاً} may be tamyīz (specification) or ḥāl. {سَاءَتْ} may also mean bi'sat ("how evil is"), in which case it is given its ruling, and the specified (al-makhṣūṣ) is omitted. In sāʾat there is an indeterminate pronoun, and {مُسْتَقَرّاً} must be tamyīz, that is, "it is evil, she (is)"; so "she" is the specified and is the link between this clause and that of which it was made the predicate, namely {إنَّهَا}; so the Shaykh also took it to be implied. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "{مُسْتَقَرّاً} is tamyīz, and sāʾat is in the sense of bi'sa." If it is said: this entails a difficulty, namely that the verb of a masculine agent must be made feminine without any warrant, for the agent in sāʾat on this view is a pronoun referring to what comes after it, namely {مُسْتَقَرّاً وَمُقَاماً}, and both are masculine; whence then the feminine? The answer: al-mustaqarr is an expression for Jahannam, so it was permissible to make its verb feminine. Similar to it is his saying:

3498 - أَوْ حُرَّةٌ عَيْطَلٌ ثَبْجاءُ مُجْفَرَةٌ ... دعائمُ الزَّوْرِ نعْمَتْ زَوْرَقُ البلدِ (Or a free, tall, full-bodied she-camel, broad in the chest, its chest-supports strong; how excellent a (small boat) of the land she is)

{مُسْتَقَرّاً وَمُقَاماً}: it was said that they are synonyms, one being conjoined to the other because their two words differ. And it was said: rather they differ in meaning: al-mustaqarr is for the sinners, since they will come out; and al-muqām is for the disbelievers, since they will abide for ever.

A group read {مَقَاماً} with fatḥa on the mīm, that is, "a place of standing". The reading of the majority is the one that agrees with the meaning, that is, a place of residence and dwelling. His saying: {إِنَّهَا سَآءَتْ مُسْتَقَرّاً}: it may be part of their speech, in which case it is accusative in position as the object of the saying, and it may be from the speech of Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:67-67.t:
His saying: {وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُواْ}: the Kufans read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the tāʾ; Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr with fatḥa and kasra; Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir with ḍamma and kasra, from aqtara, and on it {وَعَلَى المقتر قَدَرُهُ} [al-Baqara: 236]. Abū Ḥātim rejected aqtara and said: "It does not suit here, for aqtara means 'became poor' (iftaqara), and from it is {وَعَلَى المقتر قَدَرُهُ}." He was answered: al-Aṣmaʿī and others related aqtara in the sense of "was strait".

al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayyāba and al-Yazīdī read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ, fatḥa on the qāf and kasra on the doubled tāʾ, from qattara, in the sense of "was strait".

His saying: {وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ قَوَاماً}: there are two views on the subject of kāna. The better known: that it is a pronoun referring to the spending understood from His saying {أَنفَقُوا}, that is, "and their spending was even, moderate, neither extravagant nor miserly". There are two views on its khabar. One: that it is {قَوَاماً}, with {بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ} either governed by it, or by kāna according to those who hold that it operates on an adverb, or by an omitted element as a ḥāl from {قَوَاماً}. It is also possible that {بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ} and {قَوَاماً} are two predicates of kāna, according to those who hold that, who are the majority, contrary to Ibn Durustawayh. The second: that the khabar is {بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ} and {قَوَاماً} is a confirmatory ḥāl.

The second of the first two views: that its subject is {بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ}, made indeclinable because it is annexed to something not fully declinable, and {قَوَاماً} is its khabar. So al-Farrāʾ said. al-Zamakhsharī said: "In terms of i'rab there is no harm in it, but in terms of meaning it is not strong, because what is between extravagance and miserliness is inevitably moderation, so there is no benefit in the khabar, which is the support of the benefit." I said: It resembles your saying "the master of the girl was her owner."

Ḥassān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read {قِوَاماً} with kasra. It was said: the two have the same meaning. It was said: with kasra it is the name of that by which a thing is upheld. And it was said: in the sense of "rightness" and "stay".

[Translator's note: the source has a slash mark ("/") after "Abū Ḥātim"; it appears to be a printing artefact and is not translated.]

semin-durr:68-68.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ بالحق}: the bāʾ may be attached to {يَقْتُلُونَ} itself, that is, "they do not kill it for any of the causes except for the cause of the truth"; or attached to an omitted element as an adjective of the maṣdar, that is, "a killing accompanied by the truth"; or as a ḥāl, that is, "except being accompanied by the truth".

His saying {ذلك}: it refers to everything before it, since it is in the sense of "what was mentioned"; that is why it is singular. The majority read {يَلْقَ} jussive, as the apodosis of the condition, with the alif omitted. ʿAbd Allāh and Abū Rajāʾ read yalqā with it retained, as in {فَلاَ تنسى} [al-Aʿlā: 6] according to one of two views, and as the reading {لاَّ تَخَفْ دَرَكاً وَلاَ تخشى} [Ṭā Hā: 77], also according to one of two views; that is, by taking the sign of the jussive to be the omission of an implied ḍamma.

Some read {يُلَقَّ} with ḍamma on the yāʾ, fatḥa on the lām and doubled qāf, from laqqāhu such-and-such. {أَثَاماً} is an object on the reading of the majority, and a second object on the reading of these. al-Athām: punishment. The poet said:

3499 - جزى اللهُ ابنَ عُرْوَةَ حيث أمسى ... عَقوقاً والعُقوقُ له أَثامُ (May Allah requite Ibn ʿUrwa, who became disobedient, and disobedience has its athām)

that is, punishment. It was also said: it is sin (ithm) itself. The meaning: "he will meet the requital of sin", the name of the thing being applied to its requital. al-Ḥasan said: "al-Athām is one of the names of Jahannam." It was said: a well in it. It was said: a valley. ʿAbd Allāh read ayyāman, plural of yawm, meaning hardships, for the Arabs express that with "days".

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His saying: {يُضَاعَفْ}: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read {يُضَاعَفُ} and {يَخْلُدُ} nominative on one of two views: either as a ḥāl, or as resumptive. The rest read them jussive, as a badal from the requital, a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl). Similar to it is his saying:

3500 - متى تأتِنا تُلْمِمْ بنا في ديارِنا ... تَجِدْ حَطَباً جَزْلاً وناراً تَأَجَّجا (Whenever you come to us and visit us in our dwellings, you will find thick firewood and a fire blazing)

He made a badal of the condition, as here a badal was made of the requital. Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir follow what was given earlier for them in al-Baqara, namely shortening (of the long vowel) and doubling the ʿayn. The Shaykh did not mention Ibn ʿĀmir with Ibn Kathīr, but mentioned him with the group in their reading.

Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read {نُضَعِّفْ} with a nūn with ḍamma and doubled ʿayn, with {العَذَابَ} accusative as direct object. Ṭalḥa read {يُضَاعِفْ} active, the agent being Allah, with {العَذَابَ} accusative. Ṭalḥa ibn Sulaymān read {وَتَخْلُدْ} with the tāʾ of the second person, by way of iltifāt (shift of person). Abū Ḥaywa read {وَيُخَلَّدْ} doubled, passive. It is related from Abū ʿAmr likewise, except lightened.

His saying: {مُهَاناً}: a ḥāl. It is a passive participle, from ahānahu yuhīnuhu, that is, "he humiliated him and made him taste humiliation."

semin-durr:70-70.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَن تَابَ}: there are two views on it. One, which is the only one people have known: that it is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), because it is of the same genus. The second: that it is disconnected. The Shaykh said: "The connected sense is not clear, because the one from whom the exception is made has been judged to have his punishment doubled, so the implied form becomes: 'except the one who repented, believed and did righteous deeds, whose punishment is not doubled.' It does not follow from the negation of doubling that there is a negation of undoubled punishment. So in my opinion it is better that it be a disconnected exception, that is, 'but the one who repented, believed and did a righteous deed, to those Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds'; and if that is so, he will not meet any punishment at all." I said: The apparent sense is the position of the majority. As for what he said, it is not necessarily so; for the intention is the report that whoever does such-and-such, what was mentioned will befall him, unless he repents. As for the occurrence or non-occurrence of the punishment in itself, the verse does not touch on it.

His saying: {سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ}: it is the second object of the substitution (tabdīl), which is the one bound by the preposition, and it was omitted only because the meaning is understood; {حَسَنَاتٍ} is the first, the one let go, which is the one taken, and the one governed by the bāʾ is the one left. He stated this explicitly in His saying the Exalted: {بَدَّلْنَاهُمْ بِجَنَّتَيْهِمْ جَنَّتَيْنِ} [Sabaʾ: 16]. The rajaz poet said:

3501 - تَضْحَكُ منِّي أختُ ذاتِ النِّحْيَيْنْ ... أَبْدلكِ اللهُ بلونٍ لَوْنَيْنْ (The sister of Dhāt al-Niḥyayn laughs at me; may Allah exchange for you two colours for one,)
سوادَ وجهٍ وبياضَ عَيْنَيْنُ (blackness of face and whiteness of two eyes)

The investigation of this has already been given in al-Baqara at His saying {وَمَن يُبَدِّلْ نِعْمَةَ الله} [al-Baqara: 211].

[Translator's note: the source has a slash mark ("/") after "whom" in the Shaykh's quotation ("لكن مَنْ/ تابَ"); it appears to be a printing artefact and is not translated.]

semin-durr:72-72.t:
His saying: {الزُّورَ}: there are two views on it. One: that it is a direct object, that is, "they do not attend falsehood (al-zūr)"; it was explained as the idol and as diversion. The second: that it is a maṣdar, and what is meant is false testimony.

His saying {بِاللَّغْوِ}: that is, with its people.

semin-durr:73-73.t: His saying: {لَمْ يَخِرُّواْ عَلَيْهَا صُمّاً}: the negation bears on the qualifier, namely deafness and blindness, that is, "they do fall down upon them, but not in these two states." In it is an allusion to the hypocrites.

semin-durr:74-74.t:
His saying: {مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا}: {مِنْ} may be for the starting-point of the goal, and it may be explicative (bayān). So said al-Zamakhsharī, who made it a case of tajrīd (abstraction), that is, "grant us a coolness of the eyes from our spouses", like your saying "I saw in you a lion." Abū ʿAmr, the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Abū Bakr read {ذُرِّيَّتِنَا} in the singular, and the rest in the sound plural. Abū Hurayra, Abū l-Dardāʾ and Ibn Masʿūd read {قُرَّاتِ} in the plural. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Here He used aʿyun, the form of paucity, and not ʿuyūn, the form of plurality, to signal that the eyes of the God-fearing are few compared with the eyes of others." The Shaykh refuted this, saying that aʿyunan is applied to ten or fewer, whereas the eyes of the God-fearing are many, more than ten. This is a strained reading of him, because he only meant fewness relative to the multitude of others, and did not intend a specific number.

His saying: {إِمَاماً}: there are two views on it. One: that it is singular, and was brought in the singular for the sake of the genus, and its being the head of the verse-ending made it good; or the meaning is "make each one of us an imām"; or because of their unity and agreement in word; or because it is originally a maṣdar like ṣiyām and qiyām. The second: that it is a plural of āmm, like ḥāll and ḥilāl, or a plural of imāma, like qilāda and qilād.

semin-durr:75-75.t:
His saying: {الغرفة}: the second object of {يُجْزَوْنَ}. al-Ghurfa is what is raised up of a building; the plural is ghuraf.

His saying: {بِمَا صَبَرُواْ}: that is, "by their patience", i.e. because of it, or because of that which they endured. The original: ṣabarū ʿalayhi, then the preposition and pronoun were omitted gradually. The bāʾ is causal, as already given. It was also said: for exchange, as in his saying:

3502 - فليت لي بهُم قَوْماً . . . (Would that I had, in place of them, a people …)

the verse. There is no need for that.

His saying: {وَيُلَقَّوْنَ}: the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Abū Bakr read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ and sukūn on the lām, from laqiya yalqā. The rest read it with ḍamma, fatḥa and a doubled qāf, built in the passive.

semin-durr:77-77.t:
His saying: {لَوْلاَ دُعَآؤُكُمْ}: its apodosis is omitted, indicated by what came before, that is, "were it not for your supplication, He would not have cared about you nor concerned Himself." {مَا} may be negative, which is the apparent sense; it was said: interrogative in the sense of negation, but there is no need for figurative reading in something that can be literal in itself. {دُعَاؤُكُمْ} may be annexed to the agent, that is, "were it not for your supplicating Him", and may be annexed to the object, that is, "were it not for His calling you to guidance." It is said: mā ʿabaʾtu bika, meaning "I did not care or concern myself." It is said: ʿabaʾtu l-jaysh and ʿabbaʾtuhu, that is, "I prepared it and made it ready"; and al-ʿibʾ is heaviness.

His saying: {لِزَاماً}: the khabar of {يَكُونُ}, whose subject is implied, that is, "the punishment will be possessed of clinging." al-Lizām, with kasra, is a maṣdar, as in:

3503 - فإمَّا يَنْجُوَا مِنْ حَتْفِ أرضٍ ... فقد لَقِيا حُتوفَهما لِزاما (If the two escape the death of one land, they have met their deaths inescapably)

al-Minhāl, Abān ibn Taghlib and Abū l-Sammāl read {لَزَاماً} with fatḥa on the lām; it too is a maṣdar, like al-bayāt. Abū l-Sammāl also read {لَزَامِ} with kasra on the mīm, as though he made it a deviated maṣdar like badād, and built it in the Hijazi dialect; it is a deviation from al-lazma, as fajāri from al-fajra. He said:

3504 - إنَّا اقْتَسَمْنا خُطَّتَيْنا بينَنا ... فَحَمَلْتُ بَرَّةَ واحْتَمَلْتَ فَجارِ (We divided our two courses between us; I took on Barra (righteousness) and you took on Fajār (wickedness))

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {لِيَكُونَ}: the lām is attached to «نَزَّل». For the ism (subject) of «يكون» there are three views. First: that it is a pronoun referring to the One who sent down, that is: "that the One who sent down the Furqān may be a warner". Second: that it refers to the Furqān, which is the Qur'an, that is: "that the Furqān may be a warner". Third: that it refers to «عبدِه», that is: "that His servant Muḥammad ﷺ may be a warner". This is the best of the views in meaning and in technique because of its nearness to what it refers to, and the pronoun refers to the nearest mentioned. «للعالمين» is attached to «نذيراً», and was placed first only for the sake of the verse endings. The claim that it gives restriction is far-fetched since that does not apply here. The Shaykh preferred its referring to «الذي», saying: "because it is the mainstay to which the verb is attributed, and it is among His descriptions, the Exalted, as in {إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ} [الدخان: 3]. As for «نذيراً», the apparent sense is that it has the meaning of «مُنْذِر»." They also allowed it to be a maṣdar with the meaning of «الإِنذار», like «النكير» with the meaning of «الإنكار», and from it is {فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ} [القمر: 16].

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {الذي لَهُ مُلْكُ}: for «الذي» the nominative is permissible, as a naʿt (adjective) of the first «الذي», or as an explanation, or as a badal (substitute), or as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; or the accusative for praise. What comes after «نَزَّل» is part of the completion of the ṣila, so it is not extraneous, and the separation by it between the first relative and the second does no harm if we make the second a follower of it.
His saying: {وَخَلَقَ}: creation here is an expression for bringing into being and preparing for what suits it, so that His saying {فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيراً} comes out meaningful; for if we took {خَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ} in its original meaning of measuring, the speech would become: "and He measured everything and measured it".

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {واتخذوا}: the pronoun may refer to the disbelievers whom the word «العالمين» includes; it may refer to whoever claimed a partner and a child for Allah, as indicated by His saying {وَلَمْ يَتَّخِذْ وَلَداً وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُ شَرِيكٌ فِي المُلْكِ}; and it may refer to those warned, as «نذيراً» indicates them.
His saying: {لاَّ يَخْلُقُونَ} is a ṣifa (adjective) of «آلهةً». He gave precedence to the rational over the others, because the disbelievers / used to worship rational beings such as ʿUzayr, the Messiah and the angels, and others such as the stars and idols. The meaning of «لا يَخْلُقُون» is "they are not able to measure", and creation (khalq) is predicated of human beings. Zuhayr said:
3471 - وَلأَنْتَ تَفْري ما خَلَقْتَ وبَعْ ... ضُ القوم يَخْلُقُ ثم لا يَفْري
(You cut what you have measured, whereas some of the people measure and then do not cut.)
One says «خَلَقْتُ الأَديمَ», that is, I measured the leather. This is when khalq is taken to mean measuring. If bringing into existence is meant by it, it is not predicated of anyone other than the Creator the Exalted, and this has already been given. It is also said: it has the meaning of «يَخْتَلِقون» (they fabricate), as in His saying: {وَتَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكاً} [العنكبوت: 17].

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {افتراه}: the hāʾ refers to «إفك». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The hāʾ refers to «عَبْدِه» at the beginning of the sūra." I think it is nothing but a mistake, and it is as if he wanted to say: the nominative pronoun in «افتراه», and slipped.
His saying: {ظُلْماً}: there are several views on it. First: that it is a direct object, because «جاء» takes its object directly, and likewise «أتى». Second: that it is on the omission of the preposition, that is: "they came with injustice". Third: that it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), so the views given for your saying «جاء زيدٌ عَدْلاً» apply to it.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {اكتتبها}: three views are possible on it. First: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أساطيرُ», the operator in it being the implied sense of alerting or pointing; for «أساطيرُ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, whose implied form is: "these are the tales of the ancients, written down". Second: that it is in the position of a second khabar of «هذه». Third: that «أساطيرُ» is a mubtadaʾ and «اكْتَتَبها» is its khabar. As for «اكْتَتَبها», the form iftaʿala here may mean that he commanded their writing, like «اقتصد» and «احتَجم» when he commanded that to be done, and it may mean that he wrote them. This is part of their fabrication against him, because he, peace be upon him, was unlettered, neither reading nor writing; and it would be like their saying «اسْتَكَبَّه» and «اصْطَبَّه», that is, he poured it out and poured it. The form iftaʿala signals effort. It may also be from «كَتَبَ» in the sense of "gather", from «الكَتْب», which is gathering, not from writing with a pen.
Ṭalḥa read «اكْتُتِبَها» as a passive. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is: a scribe wrote them down for him, because he was unlettered and did not write by his hand; then the lām was omitted, so the verb reached the pronoun, becoming: «اكتتبها إياه كاتبٌ», like His saying {واختار موسى قَوْمَهُ} [الأعراف: 155]; then the verb was built passive for the pronoun that is «إياه», so it turned into a latent nominative after having been an overt accusative, and the pronoun of «الأساطير» remained as it was, so it became «اكْتُتِبَها» as you see."
The Shaykh said: "That is not correct according to the school of the majority of the Basrans; because in «اكتتبها له كاتب» the verb reaches two objects, one of them direct, namely the pronoun of «الأساطير», and the other restricted, namely his pronoun, peace be upon him; then the verb was extended by omitting the preposition, becoming «اكتتبها إياه كاتبٌ». When this is built passive, what takes the place of the agent is only the object that is direct in wording and in implication, not the one direct in wording but restricted in implication. On this the construction would be «اكْتُتِبَه», not «اكتتبها», and the attested usage came on what we said. Al-Farazdaq said:
3472 - ومِنَّا الذي اختير الرجالَ سماحةً ... وجوداً إذا هَبَّ الرياحُ الزَّعازِعُ
(Among us is the one chosen from among men for magnanimity and generosity when the violent winds blow.)
Had it come as al-Zamakhsharī presented, the construction would have been «ومنا الذي اختيره الرجالُ», because «اختير» takes «الرجال» by omission of the preposition, its implied form being: chosen from among men." I say: it is a good objection with regard to the school of the majority, but al-Zamakhsharī may not be bound by it and agrees with al-Akhfash and the Kufans; and if al-Akhfash and they leave the direct object in wording and implication and put the noun governed by a preposition in its place with the preposition present, then this is more fitting and proper.
The apparent point is that the clause {اكتتبها فَهِيَ تملى} is part of the completion of the disbelievers' statement. From al-Ḥasan it is reported that it is from the speech of the Creator the Exalted, and the proper form of speech on this would be to read «أَكْتَتَبها» with a detached, fatḥa-voweled hamza for interrogation, like His saying: {أفترى عَلَى الله كَذِباً أَم بِهِ جِنَّةٌ} [سبأ: 8]. It may be excused: that he omitted the hamza as it is known, like His saying the Exalted: {وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَيَّ} [الشعراء: 22]. And the saying of another:
3473 - أَفْرَحُ أَنْ أُرْزَأَ الكرامَ وأَنْ ... أُوْرَثَ ذَوْداً شَصائِصا نَبْلا
(Shall I rejoice that I am bereaved of the noble and that I inherit a few barren, tiny camels?)
He means: "or that" and «أَأَفْرَحُ»; it was omitted as the situation indicates. By right one pauses at «الأوَّلين». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "How is it said: «اكْتَتَبها فهي تُمْلَى عليه», when one only says «أَمْلَيْتُ عليه فهو يكتتبها»? I say: there are two views on it. One: he meant seeking and requesting its writing, so it is dictated to him; or it was written for him while he is unlettered, so it is dictated to him, that is, recited to him from a book so that he memorises it; for the form of reciting to a memoriser is like the form of dictating to a writer."
ʿĪsā and Ṭalḥa read «تُتْلَى» with two tāʾs (two dots above), from recitation. {بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلاً} are two time adverbials of the dictation. The yāʾ in «تملَى» is a substitute for the lām, as in His saying: {فَلْيُمْلِلْ} [البقرة: 282], and this has already been given.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {مَالِ هذا}: «ما» is interrogative, a mubtadaʾ. The preposition-phrase after it is the khabar. «ويَأْكل» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause, and with it the benefit of the report is completed, like His saying: {فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ التذكرة مُعْرِضِينَ}. It was given in al-Nisāʾ that the preposition [lām] is written separate from its governed noun, which is outside the norm of orthography.
/ The operator in the ḥāl is the "being" (istiqrār) that operates in the preposition-phrase, or the preposition-phrase itself; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it.
His saying: {فَيَكُونَ}: the majority put it in the accusative. There are two views on it. One: accusative as the answer to a request for urging (taḥḍīḍ). The second, which Abū al-Baqāʾ stated: «فيكونَ» is accusative as the answer to a question. There is room for objection, because what follows the fāʾ is not consequent upon this question. The condition for the accusative is that a condition and a result be formed from them. It was read «فيكونُ» in the nominative, conjoined to «أُنْزِل». It is permissible to conjoin it to the past, because the past is meant as the future, the implied form being: "why do we not send down".

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {أَوْ يلقى}: «أو تكونُ» are both conjoined to «أُنْزِلَ», because of what preceded about its being in the sense of «نُنَزِّل». It is not permissible to conjoin them to «فيكونَ», accusative in the answer, because they are included in the urging, in the ruling of what occurs after «لولا». The meaning is not that they are an answer to the urging so that they would be conjoined to its answer. Al-Aʿmash and Qatāda read «أو يكونُ له» with yāʾ (two dots below), because the feminine of «الجنة» is figurative.
His saying: {يَأْكُلُ مِنْهَا}: the clause is in the position of nominative as a ṣifa (adjective) of «جنةٌ». The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «نَأْكُلُ» with the nūn of the plural. The others read with yāʾ (two dots below), that is, the Messenger.
His saying: {وَقَالَ الظالمون}: he put the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, since the original is «وقالوا». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He meant by the wrongdoers those very ones." The Shaykh said: "His words are not a permissible construction; rather the Arabic construction is for him to say: «أرادَهم بأعيانِهم»."

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {جَنَّاتٍ}: it may be a badal (substitute) of «خيراً»; it may be an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) according to those who allow it with indefinites; and it may be accusative by an implied "I mean". {تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الأنهار} is a ṣifa (adjective).
His saying: {وَيَجْعَل لَّكَ}: Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read «ويجعَلُ» in the nominative, and the others assimilate the lām of «يَجْعَلْ» into the lām of «لك». As for the nominative, there are two views on it. One: that it is resumptive. The second: that it is conjoined to the apodosis of the condition. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "because when the condition is a past verb, the jussive and the nominative are both permissible in its apodosis, as in his saying:
3474 - وإنْ أتاه خليلٌ يومَ مَسْألةٍ ... يقولُ لا غائبٌ مالي ولا حَرِمُ
(If a friend comes to him on a day of asking, he says: my wealth is neither absent nor forbidden.)"
The Shaykh said: "This is not Sībawayh's school; rather his school is that the apodosis is omitted and that this imperfect is intended to be placed earlier. The school of al-Mubarrad and the Kufans is that it is the apodosis with omission of the fāʾ. The school of others is that it is the apodosis, not by omission of it, but because, when the condition is a past verb, the influence of «إنْ» weakened and so it became nominative." I say: al-Zamakhsharī built his statement on these two schools. Then the Shaykh said: "This construction is permissible and eloquent. Some of our colleagues claimed that it occurs only by poetic necessity."
As for the second reading, it admits two views. One: that the sukūn of the lām is for the jussive, conjoined to the position of «جَعَل», because it is the apodosis of the condition. The second: that it is nominative, and was given sukūn only for the assimilation. Al-Zamakhsharī and others said this, and there is room for objection, in that among those who read so, namely Nāfiʿ, the two brothers and Ḥafṣ, assimilation is not among their principles, so that it could be claimed for them in this place. Yes, Abū ʿAmr's principle is assimilation and he reads here with sukūn on the lām, so that is possible on his reading, and this is among the merits of the science of grammar and of the readings together.
Ṭalḥa ibn Sulaymān read «ويَجْعَلَ» in the accusative; that is by implying «أنْ» in the answer to the condition, and Ibn Jinnī considered it weak. Like this reading is:
3475 - فإنْ يَهْلَكْ أبو قابوسَ يَهْلَكْ ... رَبيعُ الناسِ والبَلدُ الحرامُ
ونَأْخُذْ بعدَه بذِنابِ عيشٍ ... أَجبَّ الظهرِ ليسَ له سَنامُ
(If Abū Qābūs perishes, the spring of the people and the sacred land perish; and after him we take hold of the tail of a life, with a cut-off back, with no hump.)
with the three vowel options in «نَأْخذ».

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {إِذَا رَأَتْهُمْ}: this conditional clause is in the position of accusative as a ṣifa (adjective) of «سَعيراً», because it is feminine.
His saying: {سَمِعُواْ لَهَا تَغَيُّظاً وَزَفِيراً}: if it is said: raging (taghayyuẓ) is not heard; the answer is in three ways. One: that it is on the omission of a muḍāf, that is: the sound of its raging. The second: that it is on an omission whose implied form is: "they heard and saw raging and roaring", so each is assigned to what suits it, that is: they saw raging and heard roaring. The third: that «سمعوا» is made to imply a meaning that covers both things, that is: "they perceived raging and roaring from it". These last two views are taken from his saying:
3476 - يا ليتَ زوجَك قد غَدا ... متقلِّداً سيفاً ورُمْحاً
(Would that your husband had set out girded with a sword and a spear.)
and from his saying:
3477 - فَعَلَفْتُها تِبْناً وماءً بارداً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I fed her chopped straw and cold water...)
that is: "and bearing a spear" and "I gave her water to drink"; or «مُتَقَلِّداً» is made to imply the meaning "armed", and «عَلَفْتُها» the meaning "I fed her straw and cold water".

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {مَكَاناً}: accusative as an adverbial, and «منها» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مكان», because it is originally a ṣifa of it. «مُقَرَّنين» is a ḥāl from the object of «أُلْقُوا». «ثُبوراً» is a direct object: they say "O my destruction!" It may also be a maṣdar from the meaning of «دُعُوا», and it was said: it is accusative by an implied verb of its own root, whose implied form is: «ثَبَرْنا ثُبوراً». / Muʿādh ibn Jabal read «مُقَرَّنُوْنَ» with wāw. Its ground is that it is a badal of the object of «أُلْقُوا».
ʿUmar ibn Muḥammad read «ثَبورا» with fatḥa on the thāʾ. Maṣdars on the pattern «فَعُوْل» with fatḥa are very few. This should be added to them, and I have listed them in al-Baqara at His saying {وَقُودُهَا الناس} [البقرة: 24].

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {خَالِدِينَ}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial): either from the agent of «يَشاؤون» or from the agent of «لهم», since it occurs as a khabar. The returning pronoun to «ما» is omitted, that is: "they have in it what they wish, while they are abiding forever".
His saying: {كَانَ على رَبِّكَ}: for the ism of «كان» there are two views. One: that it is the pronoun of «ما يَشاؤون»; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it. The second: that it refers to the promise understood from His saying {وُعِدَ المتقون}. {مَّسْئُولاً} is figurative, that is: it is asked "has it been fulfilled for you or not?", or the one promised it asks for it.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ}: Ibn ʿĀmir read «نَحْشُرهم» and «فنقول» with nūn in both. Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafṣ read with yāʾ (two dots below) in both. The others read with nūn in the first and yāʾ in the second. These are all clear. Al-Aʿraj read «نَحْشِرُهم» with kasra on the shīn throughout the Qur'an. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is rare in usage but strong in analogy, because «يَفْعِل» with kasra on the ʿayn in the transitive is more analogical than «يَفْعُل» with ḍamma on the ʿayn." Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī said: "It is the analogy in transitive triliteral verbs, because «يَفْعُل» with ḍamma on the ʿayn may be from the intransitive that is «فَعُل» with ḍamma in the past." The Shaykh said: "It is not as the two of them said; rather for the sound transitive verb, all of whose letters are sound, when it is not of the competitive type and has no guttural ʿayn or lām, it frequently came on both «يَفْعِل» and «يَفْعُل». If one of the two usages is well known it is followed, otherwise there is choice. So much so that some of our colleagues allowed a choice in both, whether heard for the word or not heard." I say: the one who allowed a choice in that is Ibn ʿUṣfūr, so he permits you to say «زيد يَفْعِل» with kasra on the ʿayn and «يَضْرُب» with [ḍamma] on the rāʾ, though the ḍamma was heard in the first and kasra in the second. Ibn Durustawayh preceded him in that, but the grammarians are against it.
His saying: {وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ} is conjoined to the object of «نَحْشُرهم», and putting it in the accusative as an object of accompaniment is weak. He gave precedence to the non-rational, so he brought «ما» rather than «مَنْ».
His saying: {هَؤُلاَءِ}: it may be a naʿt (adjective) of «عِبادي», or a badal, or an explanation.
His saying: {ضَلُّوا السبيل}: on the omission of the preposition, which is «عن», as He stated explicitly in His saying {يَضِلُّ عَن سَبِيلِهِ} [الأنعام: 117]; then it was extended by omitting it, as in «هَدَى», which takes «إلى» and may be omitted by extension. «ظَلَّ» is the mutāwiʿ (middle-voice) of «أَضَلَّ».

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {يَنبَغِي}: the majority read it as an active. Abū ʿĪsā al-Aswad, the reader, read «ينبغى» as a passive. Ibn Khālawayh said: "Sībawayh claimed that «ينبغى» is a dialect."
His saying: {أَن نَّتَّخِذَ} is the agent of «ينبغي», or an object standing in the place of the agent in the reading of al-Aswad. The majority read «نَتَّخِذَ» as an active. «من أولياء» is its object, and «مِنْ» was added to it. It may be a first object, on the basis that «اتَّخَذَ» takes two; it may also be that it does not take two but one, and on this «مِنْ دونِك» is attached to the taking, or to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أولياء».
Abū al-Dardāʾ, Zayd ibn Thābit, Abū Rajāʾ, al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar, among others, read «نُتَّخَذَ» as a passive. There are several views on it. First: that it is the one taking two objects, the first being the pronoun of the first-person plural that is the subject (the nūn). The second: His saying «مِنْ أولياء», and «مِنْ» is partitive, that is: "it was not fitting that we be taken as some of the protectors". Al-Zamakhsharī said this. Second: that «مِنْ أولياء» is also the second object, except that «مِنْ» is redundant in the second object. This is rejected: «مِنْ» is not added in the second object, but only in the first. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "What weakens this reading is the entry of «مِنْ» in His saying «مِنْ أولياء». Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and others objected with that." Third: that «مِنْ أولياء» is in the position of a ḥāl. Ibn Jinnī said this, except that he said: "«مِنْ» entered as redundant because of the preceding negation, as in your saying: «ما اتَّخذت زيداً مِنْ وكيل»." I say: the apparent sense is that he made the preposition-phrase be in the position of a ḥāl, and then it is impossible for «مِنْ» to be redundant; but he means that this governed noun is itself the ḥāl and «مِنْ» is redundant in it, except that the redundancy of «مِنْ» in the ḥāl is not preserved, even if negated; only the redundancy of the bāʾ in it is preserved, with disagreement about that.
His saying: {أَأَنتُمْ أَضْلَلْتُمْ} {أَمْ هُمْ ضَلُّوا}: he put the noun before the verb only for a meaning which I mentioned at His saying the Exalted: {أَأَنتَ قُلتَ لِلنَّاسِ} [المائدة: 116].
Al-Ḥajjāj read «نتخذ مِنْ دونِك [أولياءَ]»; it reached ʿĀṣim and he said: "Accursed is the stunted one! Did he know that «مِنْ» is in it?"
His saying: {ولكن مَّتَّعْتَهُمْ}: since their speech implied that we did not lead them astray and did not make them go astray, this correction was good, namely that they mentioned its cause, that is: "You favoured them and bestowed bounty on them, and they made that a pretext for their going astray, reversing the matter."
His saying: {بُوراً}: two views are possible on it. One: that it is a plural of «بائر», like «عائذ» and «عُوذ». The second: that it is originally a maṣdar, so the singular, dual, plural, masculine and feminine are alike in it. It is from «البَوار», which is destruction. It was also said: from corruption. It is a dialect of Azd; they say: / «بارَتْ بضاعتُه», that is, it spoiled. And «أمرٌ بائِرٌ», that is, corrupt. This is the meaning of their saying «كَسَدَتِ البضاعةُ» (the goods went unsold). Al-Ḥasan said: "It is from their saying «أرضُ بُوْرٌ», that is, no vegetation in it." This returns to the meaning of destruction and corruption.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {بِمَا تَقُولُونَ}: this clause is, by agreement, from the speech of Allah the Exalted, so it rests on an implied "saying" and a shift (iltifāt). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This sudden confrontation with argument and obligation is fine and splendid, especially when a shift and omission of the saying are joined to it. Similar to it is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: {يَا أَهْلَ الكتاب قَدْ جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولُنَا يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ على فَتْرَةٍ مَّنَ الرسل أَن تَقُولُواْ مَا جَآءَنَا مِن بَشِيرٍ وَلاَ نَذِيرٍ فَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بَشِيرٌ وَنَذِيرٌ} [المائدة: 19], and the saying of the poet:
3478 - قالوا خُراسانُ أَقْصى ما يُرادُ بنا ... ثم القُفُوْلُ فقد جِئْنا خُرسانا
(They said: Khurasan is the farthest we are meant to go, and then the return; and now we have come to Khurasan.)"
End of quotation. He means that the original in the noble verse is: "so We said: they have denied you", and in the verse of poetry: "so we said: we have come". The address in «كَذَّبوكم» is to the disbelievers, so the meaning is: "the objects of worship have denied you in what you say, namely that they led you astray." It was also said: the meaning is: "they have denied you in what you say of fabrication against them, that they led you astray." It was also said: it is an address to the believers in this world, that is: "the disbelievers have denied you, O believers, in what you say of monotheism in this world."
Abū Ḥaywa and Qunbul, in the transmission of Ibn Abī al-Ṣalt from him, read with yāʾ (two dots below), that is: "the gods have denied you in what they say: {سُبْحَانَكَ مَا كَانَ يَنبَغِي لَنَآ أَن نَّتَّخِذَ}" to its end. It was also said: the meaning: "the disbelievers have denied you, O believers, in what they say of fabrication against you."
His saying: {فَمَا تَسْتَطِيعُونَ}: Ḥafṣ read with the tāʾ of address, and what is meant is its worshippers. The others read with the yāʾ of the third person, and what is meant is the gods they used to worship, rational and non-rational; and for that reason the rational was given precedence, so the wāw of the pronoun was brought.
His saying: {نُذِقْهُ}: the majority read with the nūn of majesty, and it was read with yāʾ. There are two views on the agent. The more apparent: that it is Allah the Exalted, because the majority reading indicates that. The second: that it is the pronoun of the wrongdoing understood from the verb. There is figurative extension in it, by attributing the making-taste of the punishment to its cause, which is wrongdoing.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ إِنَّهُمْ لَيَأْكُلُونَ}: there are three views on this clause. First: that it is in the position of accusative as a ṣifa (adjective) of an omitted object. Al-Zamakhsharī, following al-Zajjāj, implied it: "We sent before you no one of the messengers except eating and walking"; it was omitted only because of the preposition-phrase after it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya implied it: "men" or "messengers". The pronoun in «إنهم» and what follows refers to this omitted described noun. The second: that it has no position in the iʿrāb, being only the ṣila of an omitted relative that is the object of «أَرْسَلْنا», its implied form being: "except those who, indeed, they...", so the pronoun in «إنهم» and what follows refers to the meaning of the implied «مَنْ»; this is the school of al-Farrāʾ. It is rejected: omission of the relative is permissible only in places that were pointed out in al-Baqara. The third: that the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). This is the school of Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī. He said: the implied form is «إلاَّ وإنهم», meaning that it is circumstantial, so he implied the wāw with it to show the circumstantial nature. It was rejected, because what follows «إلاَّ» is a ṣifa of what precedes it. Abū al-Baqāʾ also implied it.
The majority read the kasra on «إنَّ» because of the presence of the lām in its khabar, and because the clause is a ḥāl according to the preferred view. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It was also said: even without the lām it would be kasra, because the clause is circumstantial, as the meaning is: «إلاَّ وهم [يأْكلون]»." It was read «أنهم» with fatḥa, on the basis of a redundant lām, with «أَنْ» maṣdarī. The implied form: «إلاَّ لأنَّهم», that is: "We did not make them messengers to the people except because they are like them."
