The majority read «يَمْشُوْن» light. The Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and ʿAbd Allāh read «يُمَشَّوْن» with shadda, as a passive, that is: their needs make them walk, or the people do. [Abū] ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read «يُمَشُّون» with shadda as an active, and it has the meaning of «يَمْشُون». The poet said:
3479 - ومشى بأعطانِ المَبَأءَةِ وابتغى ... قلائِصَ مِنْها صَعْبَةٌ ورَكُوْبُ
(He walked among the watering-places of the camel pens and sought young she-camels, some of them unruly and some ridable.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Had «يُمَشُّون» been read, it would have been more fitting, were it not for the transmission", meaning with shadda. I say: al-Sulamī did read it, and praise be to Allah.
His saying: {أَتَصْبِرُونَ}: the counterpart is omitted, that is: "or do you not endure?" Al-Zamakhsharī said of this interrogative clause: "Its place after the trial is the place of «أيُّكم» after the testing in His saying {لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ} [الملك: 2]", meaning that it is suspended (muʿallaqa) because of the sense of a verb of the heart in it, so it is in the position of accusative, on the omission of the preposition.

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {عُتُوّاً}: a maṣdar. It remains sound here, which is the more frequent, and was weakened in Sūrat Maryam in {عِتِيّاً} [الآية: 8] for a reason mentioned there, namely the harmony of the verse-endings.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ}: there are several views on it. First: that it is accusative by an implied verb indicated by His saying «لا بشرى», that is: "they are denied the glad tidings on the day they see". Second: that it is accusative by «اذْكُر» (remember), so it is a direct object. Third: that it is accusative by an implied «يُعَذَّبون». It is not permissible for «البشرى» itself to operate on it / for two reasons. One: that it is a maṣdar, and a maṣdar does not operate on what precedes it. The second: that it is negated by «لا», and what comes after it does not operate on what precedes it.
His saying: {لاَ بشرى}: this clause is the object of an implied saying, that is: "they see the angels saying: there are no glad tidings", so the saying is a ḥāl from the angels. It is parallel to the implication in His saying the Exalted: {وَالمَلاَئِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن كُلِّ بَابٍ سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُم} [الرعد: 23]. The Shaykh said: "«بُشْرَى» may be indeclinable with «لا», and it may be intended with tanwīn and accusative in form, and prevented from tanwīn because of the inseparable feminine. If it is indeclinable with «لا», it is possible that «يومئذٍ» is the khabar, and «للمجرمين» a khabar after a khabar, or a naʿt of «بشرى», or attached to what the khabar is attached to; and that «يومئذٍ» is a ṣifa of «بُشْرَى» and the khabar is «للمجرمين». The disagreement of Sībawayh and al-Akhfash arises here: is the khabar for «لا» itself, or is the khabar for the mubtadaʾ which is the whole of «لا» and what is built with it? If it is intended with tanwīn and is declinable, it is permissible that «يومئذٍ» and «للمجرمين» be two khabars, and it is permissible that «يومئذٍ» be the khabar and «للمجرمين» a ṣifa. And the khabar, when the noun is not indeclinable, is for «لا» itself by consensus."
I say: his saying "it may be intended with tanwīn" to the end is possible only on the view of Abū Isḥāq, who holds that the noun of the «لا» of generic negation is declinable, and excuses the omission of the tanwīn by frequency of use, and argues for it by the return to it in poetic necessity. And he recites:
3480 - أَلا رجلاً جزاهُ اللهُ خيراً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Is there not a man — may Allah reward him with good...)
The Basrans interpret it on an implied "do you not see me a man". The Shaykh could have made it declinable, as he claimed, by another route: namely by making «بشرَى» operate on «يومَئذٍ» or on «للمجرمين», so that it becomes of the kind of the mutṭawwal (elongated noun), and the elongated one is declinable; but he did not touch on that. Something of this will come in the words of Abū al-Baqāʾ, may Allah have mercy on him. It is also possible that «بُشرى» is declinable, accusative, by another route, namely that it is accusative by an implied verb, that is: "they are given no glad tidings", like His saying the Exalted: {لاَ مَرْحَباً بِهِمْ} [ص: 59], «لا أهلا ولا سهلاً». Except that the Shaykh's words cannot be applied to this because of his saying: "it is permissible that «يومئذٍ» and «للمجرمين» be two khabars", for he judged that it has a khabar.
If it is made accusative by an implied verb, «لا» then has no khabar, because it enters that implied verb. This is a fine point, so consider it.
His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُجْرِمِينَ}: several views on «يومئذٍ» have already preceded. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be accusative by «بشرى», saying: "if you imply that it has tanwīn and is not indeclinable with «لا», and the khabar is «للمجرمين»."
He and al-Zamakhsharī also allowed «يومئذٍ» to be a repetition of «يومَ يَرَوْن». The Shaykh rejected it, whether repetition is meant as verbal emphasis or as a badal. He said: "because «يوم» is accusative by what was mentioned earlier, namely «اذْكُر», or by 'they are deprived of the glad tidings'. And what comes after the «لا» that operates on the noun is not operated on by what precedes it. On the assumption of what the two of them mentioned, the operator in it would be what precedes «لا»." I say: what he rejected it with is not apparent, because the negated clause is the object of the implied saying that is a ḥāl from «الملائكة», and the angels are the object of «يَرَوْن», and «يَرَوْن» is governed by «يوم» as genitive by annexation; so «لا» and what falls within its scope are part of the completion of the first adverbial, in that it is governed by some of what is within its scope, and so it is neither extraneous nor an obstacle to what precedes it operating on what follows it. It is astonishing how he imagined this and overlooked what I said, for it is clear on reflection.
«للمُجْرمين» is a case of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, as testimony against them to that effect. The pronoun in «يقولون» may refer to the disbelievers and to «الملائكة».
«حِجْراً» is among the maṣdars whose governing verb must be implied and which are not inflected. Sībawayh said: "A man says to a man: will you do such-and-such? and he says: «حِجراً»." It is from «حَجَره» when he prevented him; for the one seeking refuge asks Allah to prevent the harmful thing so that it does not reach him. It is as if the meaning: "I ask Allah to prevent it with a prevention and bar it with a barring."
The majority read kasra on the ḥāʾ. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ read ḍamma, which is a dialect in it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its coming on «فِعْل» or «فُعْل» in the reading of al-Ḥasan is inflection of it, since it is specific to a single place, as «قَعْدَك» and «عَمْرك» are likewise.
And I recited a verse by one of the rajaz poets:
3481 - قالَتْ وفيها حَيْدَةٌ وذُعْرُ ... عَوْذٌ بربِّي منكُمُ وحُجْرُ
(She said, with shying and fright in her: I seek refuge in my Lord from you, and a barrier!)"
What al-Zamakhsharī recited requires «حجراً» to be inflected, and Sībawayh's text has already preceded, that it must be accusative. Abū al-Baqāʾ related a third dialect in it, namely fatḥa. He said: "It has also been read with it." On this three dialects are complete in it, all of them read.
«مَحْجُوْراً» is a ṣifa that reinforces the meaning, like their saying «ذَيْل ذائِل» and «مَوْت مائتِ». And «الحِجْر» is the intellect, because it restrains its possessor.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ الْفُرْقَانَ عَلَى عَبْدِهِ لِيَكُونَ لِلْعَالَمِينَ نَذِيرًا (١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِيَكُونَ): there are three views on the noun (ism) of كان. The first: the Furqān. The second: the servant. The third: Allah the Exalted. It has also been read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, عَلَى عِبَادِهِ ("upon His servants"); then the pronoun does not refer to it.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَلَمْ يَتَّخِذْ وَلَدًا وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ شَرِيكٌ فِي الْمُلْكِ وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيرًا (٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِي لَهُ): it may be a badal (substitute) of the first «الَّذِي»; it may be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); and it may be in the position of the accusative on the implied wording "I mean" (أَعْنِي).

ukberi-tibyan:4-5.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا إِفْكٌ افْتَرَاهُ وَأَعَانَهُ عَلَيْهِ قَوْمٌ آخَرُونَ فَقَدْ جَاءُوا ظُلْمًا وَزُورًا (٤) وَقَالُوا أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ اكْتَتَبَهَا فَهِيَ تُمْلَى عَلَيْهِ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا (٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (افْتَرَاهُ): the hāʾ refers to «عَبْدِهِ» at the beginning of the sūra.
His saying, Exalted is He: (ظُلْمًا): the object of جاءوا, i.e. "they brought injustice" (أَتَوْا ظُلْمًا).
It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). الأساطير ("tales") was mentioned in al-Anʿām.
(اكْتَتَبَهَا): in the position of a ḥāl from الأساطير, i.e. "they said: these are the tales of the ancients, written down" (قَالُوا هَذِهِ أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ مُكْتَتَبَةً).

ukberi-tibyan:7-8.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَالُوا مَالِ هَذَا الرَّسُولِ يَأْكُلُ الطَّعَامَ وَيَمْشِي فِي الْأَسْوَاقِ لَوْلَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ فَيَكُونَ مَعَهُ نَذِيرًا (٧) أَوْ يُلْقَى إِلَيْهِ كَنْزٌ أَوْ تَكُونُ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ يَأْكُلُ مِنْهَا وَقَالَ الظَّالِمُونَ إِنْ تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا رَجُلًا مَسْحُورًا (٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَأْكُلُ الطَّعَامَ): it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the operator governing it is the operator in «لِهَذَا», or the adverbial phrase itself. (فَيَكُونَ): accusative as the answer to the interrogative, or to the urging (taḥḍīḍ).
(أَوْ يُلْقَى) – (أَوْ تَكُونُ): conjoined to أُنزل, because أُنزل has the sense of يُنزَل, or يُلقى has the sense of أُلقي.
And (يَأْكُلُ) is read with yāʾ and with nūn, and the meaning in both is clear.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي إِنْ شَاءَ جَعَلَ لَكَ خَيْرًا مِنْ ذَلِكَ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ وَيَجْعَلْ لَكَ قُصُورًا (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَنَّاتٍ): a badal (substitute) of «خَيْرًا».
(وَيَجْعَلْ لَكَ): in the jussive (majzūm), conjoined to the position of «جَعَلَ», which is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and in the nominative as resumptive. It is also possible that whoever reads it in the jussive has made the nominative form vowelless for lightness and assimilated it.

ukberi-tibyan:12-13.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِذَا رَأَتْهُمْ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ سَمِعُوا لَهَا تَغَيُّظًا وَزَفِيرًا (١٢) وَإِذَا أُلْقُوا مِنْهَا مَكَانًا ضَيِّقًا مُقَرَّنِينَ دَعَوْا هُنَالِكَ ثُبُورًا (١٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذَا رَأَتْهُمْ) to the end of the verse: in the position of the accusative as an adjective of سعير.
And (ضَيِّقًا), with doubling and without it, was mentioned in al-Anʿām.
And (مَكَانًا) is an adverb (ẓarf), and «مِنْهَا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, i.e. "a place of it" (مَكَانًا مِنْهَا).
And (ثُبُورًا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); it may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) derived from the meaning of دعوا.

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَهُمْ فِيهَا مَا يَشَاءُونَ خَالِدِينَ كَانَ عَلَى رَبِّكَ وَعْدًا مَسْئُولًا (١٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (خَالِدِينَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يَشَاءُونَ» or from the pronoun in «لَهُمْ».
(كَانَ عَلَى رَبِّكَ): the pronoun in «كَانَ» refers to «مَا». The implied wording may also be: "the promise was a promise" (كَانَ الْوَعْدُ وَعْدًا); this maṣdar is indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: «وَعْدًا», and by His saying: «لَهُمْ فِيهَا». The khabar (predicate) of كان is «وَعْدًا» or «عَلَى رَبِّكَ».

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ فَيَقُولُ أَأَنْتُمْ أَضْلَلْتُمْ عِبَادِي هَؤُلَاءِ أَمْ هُمْ ضَلُّوا السَّبِيلَ (١٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ), i.e. "and mention" (وَاذْكُرْ).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا) [Translator's note: so in the source; the words discussed here are evidently (وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ) of this verse.]: the wāw may be a conjunction, and it may be in the sense of "with" (مَعَ).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَؤُلَاءِ): it may be a badal (substitute) of عبادي, and it may be a naʿt (adjective).

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا سُبْحَانَكَ مَا كَانَ يَنْبَغِي لَنَا أَنْ نَتَّخِذَ مِنْ دُونِكَ مِنْ أَوْلِيَاءَ وَلَكِنْ مَتَّعْتَهُمْ وَآبَاءَهُمْ حَتَّى نَسُوا الذِّكْرَ وَكَانُوا قَوْمًا بُورًا (١٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ نَتَّخِذَ): it is read with fatḥa on the nūn and kasra on the khāʾ, in the active voice; «مِنْ أَوْلِيَاءَ» is then the first object and «مِنْ دُونِكَ» the second. The entry of «مِنْ» is permitted because it is in the context of negation, so it is like His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ مِنْ وَلَدٍ).
It is also read with ḍamma on the nūn and fatḥa on the khāʾ, in the passive; the first object is then latent (implied), and «مِنْ أَوْلِيَاءَ» is the second.
This is not permissible according to most grammarians, because «مِنْ» is not added redundantly to the second object, but only to the first, as in your saying: "I did not take anyone as a protector" (مَا اتَّخَذْتُ مِنْ أَحَدٍ وَلِيًّا); it is not permissible to say مَا اتَّخَذْتُ أَحَدًا مِنْ وَلِيٍّ. Were that permissible, it would be permissible to say: فَمَا مِنْكُمْ أَحَدٌ عَنْهُ مِنْ حَاجِزِينَ. It is also possible that «مِنْ دُونِكَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from أولياء.

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ إِلَّا إِنَّهُمْ لَيَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعَامَ وَيَمْشُونَ فِي الْأَسْوَاقِ وَجَعَلْنَا بَعْضَكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ فِتْنَةً أَتَصْبِرُونَ وَكَانَ رَبُّكَ بَصِيرًا (٢٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا أَنَّهُمْ) [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; the reading discussed first is إِنَّهُمْ with kasra, as in the verse quoted.]: «إِنَّ» is given a kasra because of the lām in the khabar (predicate).
It is also said: even if there were no lām, it would still have a kasra, because the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), since the meaning is: "except while they eat" (إِلَّا وَهُمْ يَأْكُلُونَ).
It has also been read with fatḥa, on the view that the lām is redundant (zāʾida); أنْ [i.e. أنّ] is then maṣdar-forming, and the implied wording is "except that they eat" (إِلَّا أَنَّهُمْ يَأْكُلُونَ), i.e. "We did not make them messengers to the people except because of their being like them".
It may also be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied wording being: "that they are people who eat" (إِنَّهُمْ ذَوُو أَكْلٍ).

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ الْمَلَائِكَةَ لَا بُشْرَى يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ وَيَقُولُونَ حِجْرًا مَحْجُورًا (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ): concerning what governs it there are three views:
The first: "mention the day" (اذْكُرْ يَوْمَ).
The second: "they will be punished on the day" (يُعَذَّبُونَ يَوْمَ); the words after it indicate this.
The third: "they will not be given good tidings on the day they see" (لَا يُبَشَّرُونَ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ).
البشرى cannot govern it, for two reasons:
The first: a maṣdar (verbal noun) does not govern what comes before it.
The second: what is negated does not govern what comes before لا.
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَوْمَئِذٍ): there are several views on it:
The first: it is a repetition of the first يوم.
The second: it is the khabar (predicate) of بشرى, so that what is omitted governs it; and «لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ» is a clarification (tabyīn), or a second khabar. The third: the khabar is «لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ», and what governs يومئذ is what the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to.
The fourth: that «بُشْرَى» governs it, if you suppose that it is nunated and not made indeclinable (mabnī) with لا; the khabar is then «لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ», and the nunation has dropped because it is a diptote. «بُشْرَى» cannot govern it if you make it indeclinable together with «لَا».
His saying, Exalted is He: (حِجْرًا مَحْجُورًا): it is a maṣdar, and the implied wording is: "we forbid a forbidding" (حِجْرُنَا حِجْرًا) [Translator's note: so in the source; the expected wording would be a verb, e.g. نَحْجُرُ حِجْرًا.]. The fatḥa and the kasra [on the ḥāʾ] are two dialectal forms, and it has been read with both.

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ السَّمَاءُ بِالْغَمَامِ وَنُزِّلَ الْمَلَائِكَةُ تَنْزِيلًا (٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ):
It is read with doubling and without it; the original form is تَنْشَقُّ [Translator's note: so in the source; the usual analysis gives the original as تَتَشَقَّقُ.]. This verb may be meant for the present and the future, and it may be meant for the past; this has been reported, and the evidence for it is that «وَنُزِّلَ», which is past, is conjoined to it, and that it is mentioned after His saying «وَيَقُولُونَ حِجْرًا», and that happens after the splitting of the sky.
As for the accusative of «يَوْمَ», it is on the implied wording "mention" (اذْكُرْ), or on the meaning: "and Allah alone holds dominion on the day the sky is split".
(وَنُزِّلَ): the majority read it with doubling.
It is also read without doubling and with fatḥa.
And (تَنْزِيلًا), on this reading, is a maṣdar (verbal noun) not from the wording of the verb; the implied wording is: "they were sent down a sending down, and so they came down" (نُزِّلُوا تَنْزِيلًا فَنَزَلُوا).

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الْمُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْحَقُّ لِلرَّحْمَنِ وَكَانَ يَوْمًا عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ عَسِيرًا (٢٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الْمُلْكُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); there are three views on the khabar (predicate). The first: «لِلرَّحْمَنِ»; on this view «الْحَقُّ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «الْمُلْكُ», and «يَوْمَئِذٍ» is governed by الملك, or by what the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to; «الْحَقُّ» does not govern it, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that comes after it.
The second: the khabar is «الْحَقُّ», and «لِلرَّحْمَنِ» is a clarification (tabyīn), or is attached to الحق itself, i.e. "it is established for the All-Merciful". The third: the khabar is «يَوْمَئِذٍ», and الحق is a naʿt of الرحمن.

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَالَ الرَّسُولُ يَا رَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِي اتَّخَذُوا هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ مَهْجُورًا (٣٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَهْجُورًا): it is the second object of اتخذوا, i.e. "they made the Qurʾān abandoned by their turning away from it".

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الْقُرْآنُ جُمْلَةً وَاحِدَةً كَذَلِكَ لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِ فُؤَادَكَ وَرَتَّلْنَاهُ تَرْتِيلًا (٣٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جُمْلَةً): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the Qurʾān, i.e. "all together" (مُجْتَمِعًا).
(كَذَلِكَ), i.e. "it was sent down thus" (أُنْزِلَ كَذَلِكَ); so the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, or is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). The lām in «لِنُثَبِّثَ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted verb.

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا يَأْتُونَكَ بِمَثَلٍ إِلَّا جِئْنَاكَ بِالْحَقِّ وَأَحْسَنَ تَفْسِيرًا (٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جِئْنَاكَ بِالْحَقِّ), i.e. "with the true parable", or "with a parable better in explanation than the explanation of their parable".

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلَى وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلَى جَهَنَّمَ أُولَئِكَ شَرٌّ مَكَانًا وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا (٣٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ): the implied wording may be "they are those who" (هُمُ الَّذِينَ), or "I mean those who" (أَعْنِي الَّذِينَ).
And (أُولَئِكَ) is resumptive. It is also possible that «الَّذِينَ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «أُولَئِكَ» its khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ وَجَعَلْنَا مَعَهُ أَخَاهُ هَارُونَ وَزِيرًا (٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَارُونَ): it is a badal (substitute).

ukberi-tibyan:36-39.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَقُلْنَا اذْهَبَا إِلَى الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا فَدَمَّرْنَاهُمْ تَدْمِيرًا (٣٦) وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ لَمَّا كَذَّبُوا الرُّسُلَ أَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ وَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ لِلنَّاسِ آيَةً وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا (٣٧) وَعَادًا وَثَمُودَ وَأَصْحَابَ الرَّسِّ وَقُرُونًا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ كَثِيرًا (٣٨) وَكُلًّا ضَرَبْنَا لَهُ الْأَمْثَالَ وَكُلًّا تَبَّرْنَا تَتْبِيرًا (٣٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَدَمَّرْنَاهُمْ): it is also read «فَدَمَّرْنَاهُمْ» [Translator's note: so in the source; the variant meant is evidently an imperative form such as فَدَمِّرَاهُمْ, since it is said to be conjoined to the imperative اذهبا.], and this is conjoined to اذهبا. The well-known reading is conjoined to an omitted verb, its implied form being: "so they went, and warned, and they denied them, so We destroyed them" (فَذَهَبَا فَأَنْذَرَا فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَدَمَّرْنَاهُمْ).
(وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ): it may be conjoined to what precedes it, i.e. "and We destroyed the people of Noah".
And (أَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ) is an explanation of the destruction. The implied wording may also be: "and We drowned the people of Noah".
(وَعَادًا), i.e. "and We destroyed", or "We annihilated, ʿĀd".
(وَكُلًّا): conjoined to what precedes it. The implied wording may also be: "and We mentioned each" (وَذَكَرْنَا كُلًّا), because «ضَرَبْنَا لَهُ الْأَمْثَالَ» has this meaning.
As for the second (كُلًّا), it is accusative by (تَبَّرْنَا) and nothing else.

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ أَتَوْا عَلَى الْقَرْيَةِ الَّتِي أُمْطِرَتْ مَطَرَ السَّوْءِ أَفَلَمْ يَكُونُوا يَرَوْنَهَا بَلْ كَانُوا لَا يَرْجُونَ نُشُورًا (٤٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَطَرَ السَّوْءِ): there are three views on it:
The first: it is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the basic form is "the town was rained a rain" (أُمْطِرَتِ الْقَرْيَةُ مَطَرًا), i.e. "I brought it upon it" or "I gave it to it".
The second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) with its additional letters omitted, i.e. "an evil raining" (إِمْطَارَ السَّوْءِ). The third: it is a naʿt (adjective) of something omitted, i.e. "a raining like the evil rain" (إِمْطَارًا مِثْلَ مَطَرِ السَّوْءِ).

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا رَأَوْكَ إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا أَهَذَا الَّذِي بَعَثَ اللَّهُ رَسُولًا (٤١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هُزُوًا), i.e. "an object of mockery" (مَهْزُوًّا بِهِ). There is an omission in the expression, its implied form being: "saying: «أَهَذَا»"; what is omitted is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the pronoun referring back to «الَّذِي» is omitted, i.e. "sent him" (بَعَثَهُ).
And (رَسُولًا) may be in the sense of «مُرْسَلٍ» ("one sent"), and it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) from which the muḍāf has been omitted, i.e. "one bearing a message" (ذَا رَسُولٍ), رسول here being the message.

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنْ كَادَ لَيُضِلُّنَا عَنْ آلِهَتِنَا لَوْلَا أَنْ صَبَرْنَا عَلَيْهَا وَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ حِينَ يَرَوْنَ الْعَذَابَ مَنْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا (٤٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنْ كَادَ): it is the lightened form of the heavy one (إنّ); the disagreement about it has been mentioned in other places.
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ أَضَلُّ): it is an interrogative.

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا وَالنَّوْمَ سُبَاتًا وَجَعَلَ النَّهَارَ نُشُورًا (٤٧)).
And (نُشُورًا) was mentioned in al-Aʿrāf.

ukberi-tibyan:49-52.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لِنُحْيِيَ بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَيْتًا وَنُسْقِيَهُ مِمَّا خَلَقْنَا أَنْعَامًا وَأَنَاسِيَّ كَثِيرًا (٤٩) وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَاهُ بَيْنَهُمْ لِيَذَّكَّرُوا فَأَبَى أَكْثَرُ النَّاسِ إِلَّا كُفُورًا (٥٠) وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَبَعَثْنَا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ نَذِيرًا (٥١) فَلَا تُطِعِ الْكَافِرِينَ وَجَاهِدْهُمْ بِهِ جِهَادًا كَبِيرًا (٥٢))
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِنُحْيِيَ بِهِ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أنزلنا; its attachment to طهور is weak, because the water was not made pure in order that We might give life.
(مِمَّا خَلَقْنَا): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أَنْعَامًا وَأَنَاسِيَّ»; the implied wording is "cattle from what We created" (أَنْعَامًا مِمَّا خَلَقْنَا).
«مِنْ» may also be attached to «نُسْقِيَهُ», for the beginning of the extent, as in your saying: "I took money from Zayd" (أَخَذْتُ مِنْ زَيْدٍ مَالًا), for they allowed both views in it.
أناسيّ: its original form is أناسين, the plural of إنسان, like سرحان and سراحين; the nūn in it was replaced by a yāʾ and assimilated.
It is also said that it is the regular plural of إنسيّ.
The hāʾ in «صَرَّفْنَاهُ» refers to the water, and the hāʾ in «بِهِ» refers to the Qurʾān.

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ هَذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ وَهَذَا مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخًا وَحِجْرًا مَحْجُورًا (٥٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِلْحٌ): the well-known reading follows regular usage; one says مَاءٌ مِلْحٌ ("salty water"). It has also been read «مَلِحٍ» with kasra on the lām; its original form on this reading is مالح, which occurs as an irregular form; the alif was then dropped, as they said بَرِدٌ for بارد.
The tāʾ in «فُرَاتٌ» is a radical, and its pattern is fuʿāl.
And (بَيْنَهُمَا) is an adverb (ẓarf) governed by جعل; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from برزخ.

ukberi-tibyan:55-55.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنْفَعُهُمْ وَلَا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَكَانَ الْكَافِرُ عَلَى رَبِّهِ ظَهِيرًا (٥٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَلَى رَبِّهِ): it may be the khabar (predicate) of كان, with «ظَهِيرًا» a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a second khabar. It may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to (ظَهِيرًا), and this is the stronger view.

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ مَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِلَّا مَنْ شَاءَ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ إِلَى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا (٥٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا مَنْ شَاءَ): it is an exception from a different genus (disjunctive exception).

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى الْحَيِّ الَّذِي لَا يَمُوتُ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِهِ وَكَفَى بِهِ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا (٥٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِذُنُوبِ): it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خَبِيرًا», i.e. "Allah suffices as one well-informed of their sins".

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ الرَّحْمَنُ فَاسْأَلْ بِهِ خَبِيرًا (٥٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِي خَلَقَ): it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «الرَّحْمَنُ» the khabar (predicate); it may be a khabar, i.e. "He is the one who" (هُوَ الَّذِي); or it may be accusative by an implied "I mean" (أَعْنِي), so that the statement is complete at العرش. Then «الرَّحْمَنُ» is a mubtadaʾ and «فَاسْأَلْ بِهِ» the khabar, according to the view of al-Akhfash; or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is the All-Merciful" (هُوَ الرَّحْمَنُ); or a badal (substitute) of the pronoun in «اسْتَوَى».
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِهِ): there are two views on it. The first: the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «خَبِيرًا», and خبيرًا is the object of «اسْأَلْ». The second: the bāʾ has the sense of عن ("about"), so it is attached to اسأل.
It is also said that the implied wording is: "ask, by your asking about Him, one who is well-informed" (فَاسْأَلْ بِسُؤَالِكَ عَنْهُ خَبِيرًا).
It is weak for «خَبِيرًا» to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent in اسأل, because one who is well-informed does not ask, except by way of emphasis, like (وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ مُصَدِّقًا). It may also be a ḥāl from الرحمن if you make it nominative by «اسْتَوَى».

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اسْجُدُوا لِلرَّحْمَنِ قَالُوا وَمَا الرَّحْمَنُ أَنَسْجُدُ لِمَا تَأْمُرُنَا وَزَادَهُمْ نُفُورًا (٦٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِمَا تَأْمُرُنَا): it is read with tāʾ and with yāʾ. There are three views on «مَا». The first: it is in the sense of الذي. The second: an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective. On both views it needs a resumptive pronoun; the implied wording is "to what you command us to prostrate to" (لِمَا تَأْمُرُنَا بِالسُّجُودِ لَهُ), then [by stages] "you command us [it]" (ثُمَّ يَأْمُرُنَا) — this according to the view of Abū al-Ḥasan [al-Akhfash]; according to the view of Sībawayh, all of that is omitted at once, without stages.
The third view: it is maṣdar-forming, i.e. "shall we prostrate on account of your command?"; this needs no resumptive pronoun, and the meaning is: "shall we worship Allah because of your command?"

ukberi-tibyan:61-62.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ فِي السَّمَاءِ بُرُوجًا وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سِرَاجًا وَقَمَرًا مُنِيرًا (٦١) وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ خِلْفَةً لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَذَّكَّرَ أَوْ أَرَادَ شُكُورًا (٦٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سِرَاجًا): it is read in the singular, meaning the sun; and in the plural, with two ḍammas [i.e. سُرُجًا], meaning the sun and the stars; or each part of the sun is a lamp, because of its spreading and its shining in one place rather than another.
And (خِلْفَةً) is a second object, or a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is singular because the meaning is that each of them succeeds the other, and this can only be realised from the two of them together.
And الشكور, with ḍamma, is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like الشكر ("thanks").

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَعِبَادُ الرَّحْمَنِ الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ هَوْنًا وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الْجَاهِلُونَ قَالُوا سَلَامًا (٦٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَعِبَادُ الرَّحْمَنِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject). There are two views on the khabar (predicate). The first: «الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ». The second: His saying, Exalted is He: «أُولَئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ», with «الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ» an adjective.
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَالُوا سَلَامًا): «سَلَامًا» here is a maṣdar (verbal noun). At the beginning of Islam, when the ignorant addressed them, they would say this word, because fighting had not yet been prescribed; then it was abrogated.
It is also possible that قالوا has the sense of "they greeted with peace" (سَلَّمُوا), so that «سَلَامًا» is its maṣdar.

ukberi-tibyan:66-68.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّهَا سَاءَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا (٦٦) وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا أَنْفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ قَوَامًا (٦٧) وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ وَلَا يَقْتُلُونَ النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَلَا يَزْنُونَ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثَامًا (٦٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُسْتَقَرًّا): it is a tamyīz (specification), and «سَاءَتْ» is in the sense of بئس ("how evil").
And (يَقْتُرُوا) is with fatḥa on the yāʾ; there are two forms for the tāʾ, kasra and ḍamma, and it has been read with both. The past is triliteral; one says قَتَرَ يَقْتُرُ and يَقْتِرُ.
It is also read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the tāʾ, the past being أَقْتَرَ; this is a dialectal form, and on it comes: (وَعَلَى الْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ).
(وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ), i.e. "and the spending was"; and «قَوَامًا» is the khabar (predicate).
It is also possible that «بَيْنَ» is the khabar and «قَوَامًا» a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ): in the position of a ḥāl; the implied wording is: "except when deserving it" (إِلَّا مُسْتَحِقِّينَ).
And الأثام is a noun, like السلام and الكلام.

ukberi-tibyan:69-70.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يُضَاعَفْ لَهُ الْعَذَابُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ مُهَانًا (٦٩) إِلَّا مَنْ تَابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًا صَالِحًا فَأُولَئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ حَسَنَاتٍ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا (٧٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُضَاعَفْ): it is read in the jussive (majzūm), as a badal (substitute) of «يَلْقَ», since it shares its meaning, because the doubling of the punishment is the meeting with the requital of sins.
It has also been read in the nominative, irregularly (shādhdh), as resumptive.
And (يَخْلُدُ): the majority read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ.
It is also read with ḍamma on it and fatḥa on the lām, in the passive; its past is أَخْلَدَ, in the sense of خَلَدَ.
And (مُهَانًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(إِلَّا مَنْ تَابَ): an exception from the same genus, in the position of the accusative.

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَاجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا (٧٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا): it is read in the singular, it being a generic noun with a plural meaning, and in the plural.
And (قُرَّةَ) is the object. «مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا» may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «قُرَّةَ», and it may be governed by «هَبْ». What is omitted from (هَبْ) is its first radical (fāʾ). The original is a kasra on the hāʾ, because the wāw drops only on this assumption, as in يَعِدُ; but the hāʾ was given a fatḥa in يَهَبُ because it is a guttural letter, so the fatḥa is incidental; for that reason the wāw did not return, just as it did not return in «يَسَعُ» and «يَدَعُ».
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِمَامًا): there are four views on it. The first: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like قيام and صيام, and so it was not put in the plural; the implied wording is "people of leadership" (ذَوِي إِمَامٍ). The second: it is the plural of إمامة, like حالّ and حِلال. [Translator's note: so in the source; the same example is repeated in the third view, and it fits that view.]
The third: it is the plural of آمّ, from أمَّ يؤمّ ("to lead"), like حالّ and حِلال.
The fourth: it is a singular used in place of أئمة, as Allah the Exalted said: (نُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلًا).

ukberi-tibyan:75-76.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أُولَئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ الْغُرْفَةَ بِمَا صَبَرُوا وَيُلَقَّوْنَ فِيهَا تَحِيَّةً وَسَلَامًا خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا حَسُنَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا () ٧٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيُلَقَّوْنَ): it is read without doubling and in the active voice, and with doubling and in the passive.
The agent in «حَسُنَتْ» is the pronoun of الغرفة.

ukberi-tibyan:77-77.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ مَا يَعْبَأُ بِكُمْ رَبِّي لَوْلَا دُعَاؤُكُمْ فَقَدْ كَذَّبْتُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزَامًا (٧٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا يَعْبَأُ بِكُمْ): there are two views on it. The first: He would not care about creating you were it not for your supplication, i.e. your affirmation of His oneness. The second: He would not care about punishing you were it not for your calling upon other gods along with Him.
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ): the noun (ism) of كان is latent, indicated by the preceding words; or it is "the requital" or "the punishment".
And (لِزَامًا), i.e. "something inseparable" (ذَا لِزَامٍ), or "clinging" (مُلَازِمًا); He put the maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of the active participle. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنْ هم إلا كالأنْعامِ بَلْ هم أضَلُّ سَبِيلا﴾ means: they are nothing but like cattle in their lack of discernment regarding the signs and proof that were made an indication for them.
He said: ﴿بَلْ هم أضَلُّ سَبِيلا﴾ because cattle glorify Allah with His praise and prostrate to Him, whereas they are as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكم مِن بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ فَهي كالحِجارَةِ أوْ أشَدُّ قَسْوَةً﴾ [al-Baqara: 74].

zajjaj:45-45.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ الظِّلَّ﴾: "اَلظِّلُّ" (the shade) is from the time of the rising of dawn to the time of the rising of the sun. ﴿وَلَوْ شاءَ لَجَعَلَهُ ساكِنًا﴾, that is: fixed, permanent, never passing away. ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْنا الشَّمْسَ عَلَيْهِ دَلِيلا﴾: the sun is an indication of the shade, and it is what abolishes (tansakhu) the shade.

zajjaj:46-46.t: ﴿ثُمَّ قَبَضْناهُ إلَيْنا قَبْضًا يَسِيرًا﴾: it was said: hidden (gradual); and it was said: easy. The meaning of "ألَمْ تَرَ" is: have you not known? This is from seeing with the heart. It is also possible that here it is from seeing with the eye, the meaning then being: "ألَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ الظِّلَّ رَبُّكَ؟!" (Have you not seen how your Lord extended the shade?!). The better view is that it has the meaning of "ألَمْ تَعْلَمْ؟" (Have you not known?).

zajjaj:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي أرْسَلَ الرِّياحَ بُشْرًا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ — there are six ways (awjuh) of reading it: "نَشْرًا" with fatḥa on the nūn; "نُشْرًا" with ḍamma on it; "نُشُرًا" with ḍamma on the nūn and the shīn; and "بُشْرى" is permissible, "feminine", with the bāʾ, on the pattern "فُعْلى"; and "بُشْرًا" with tanwīn and the bāʾ; and "بُشُرًا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ". These are six ways, four of which are read. As for "نَشْرًا", its meaning is: a reviving that spreads out the clouds which carry the rain, in which is the life of everything. Whoever read "نُشُرًا", it is the plural of "نُشُورٌ", and "نُشُرٌ" is like "رَسُولٌ" and "رُسُلٌ". Whoever read it with sukūn made the shīn quiescent for lightness. These are the three ways with the nūn. As for the bāʾ: whoever read it with tanwīn and the bāʾ, giving it ḍamma, with the shīn quiescent — this is only by making the ʿayn (second radical) quiescent, from your saying "بُشْرًا"; and when he does not give it tanwīn, its alif is for the feminine. Whoever read "بُشْرًا" with tanwīn, it is a plural; one says "رِيحٌ بَشُورٌ" (a wind bearing good tidings), as He said: ﴿وَمِن آياتِهِ أنْ يُرْسِلَ الرِّياحَ مُبَشِّراتٍ﴾ [al-Rūm: 46], that is: bringing good tidings of rain. Whoever read "بُشُرًا" with ḍamma, it is on the original form of the plural. Whoever read "بُشْرى" without tanwīn, it has the meaning of "بِشارَةً" (good tidings).
His saying: ﴿وَأنْـزَلْنا مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً طَهُورًا﴾: all water that comes down from the sky, or comes out of a sea, or is melted from snow or hail, is ṭahūr (purifying). He (peace be upon him) said concerning the sea: "هو الطَّهُورُ ماؤُهُ الحِلُّ مَيْتَتُهُ" (Its water is purifying and its dead animals are lawful).

zajjaj:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿لِنُحْيِيَ بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَيْتًا﴾ — had it been "مَيْتَةً" it would have been permissible. It was said "مَيْتًا" although the word بَلْدَة is feminine, because the meaning of "اَلْبَلَدُ" and "اَلْبَلْدَةُ" is one. And His saying: ﴿وَأناسِيَّ كَثِيرًا﴾: "أناسِيُّ" is the plural of "إنْسِيٌّ", like "كُرْسِيٌّ" and "كَراسِيُّ". It may also be the plural of "إنْسانٌ", with the yāʾ a substitute for the nūn, the original being "أناسِينُ" with the nūn, like "سَراحِينُ".

zajjaj:50-50.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْناهُ بَيْنَهم لِيَذَّكَّرُوا﴾, that is: We distributed the rain among them so that they might take heed, that is: so that they might reflect on Allah's blessings upon them in it and praise Him for that. ﴿فَأبى أكْثَرُ النّاسِ إلا كُفُورًا﴾: these are those who say, "We were rained upon by the nawʾ of such-and-such", that is: by the setting of such-and-such a star, as the astrologers say; so Allah made them disbelievers by that.

zajjaj:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿فَلا تُطِعِ الكافِرِينَ وجاهِدْهم بِهِ جِهادًا كَبِيرًا﴾ — "كَثِيرًا" is also permissible, but the reading is with the bāʾ. The meaning of "بِهِ" is: with the truth, that is: with the Quran that was sent down to you, and it is the truth.

zajjaj:53-53.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَرَجَ البَحْرَيْنِ﴾: the meaning of "مَرَجَ" is: He left the two free (to meet). You say "مَرَجْتُ الدّابَّةَ" and "أمْرَجْتُها" when you leave the animal free to graze, and "اَلْمَرْجُ" (meadow) is named from this. One says "مَرِجَتْ عُهُودُهم وأماناتُهم" (their covenants and trusts became confused) when they become mixed up; this is related from the Prophet ﷺ.
His saying: ﴿هَذا عَذْبٌ فُراتٌ﴾: فُراتٌ is a naʿt (adjective) of "عَذْبٌ", and "اَلْفُراتُ" is the sweetest of waters; the meaning is: "this is sweet, the sweetest of water". ﴿وَهَذا مِلْحٌ أُجاجٌ﴾: "اَلْأُجاجُ" is a naʿt of المِلْح; the meaning is: "and this is salt, of the utmost saltiness". ﴿وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُما بَرْزَخًا﴾: "اَلْبَرْزَخُ" is the barrier. To the sight of the eye the two are mixed, yet by the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, they are separate; neither mixes with the other.

zajjaj:54-54.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ مِنَ الماءِ بَشَرًا فَجَعَلَهُ نَسَبًا وصِهْرًا﴾: the relations by marriage (aṣhār) from among lineage are those with whom marriage is permitted, and the lineage that does not become a relation by marriage is from His saying: ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكم أُمَّهاتُكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 23] up to: ﴿وَأنْ تَجْمَعُوا بَيْنَ الأُخْتَيْنِ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 23].

zajjaj:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿وَكانَ الكافِرُ عَلى رَبِّهِ ظَهِيرًا﴾: the meaning of "اَلظَّهِيرُ" is: the helper, because he follows Satan and helps him in disobedience to Allah, since their worship of idols is help given to Satan.

zajjaj:59-59.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ فاسْألْ بِهِ خَبِيرًا﴾ — "اَلرَّحْمَنِ فاسْألْ" is also permissible. Whoever says "اَلرَّحْمَنُ", it is nominative (marfūʿ) for one of two reasons. One of them is as a badal (substitute) for what is in His saying ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوى﴾ [Translator's note: i.e. the latent pronoun in اسْتَوى], then He made it clear by His saying "اَلرَّحْمَنُ". It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with "فاسْألْ بِهِ" the khabar (predicate); the meaning is: "ask about Him one who is well-informed". Whoever says "اَلرَّحْمَنِ", it is on the meaning of "وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلى الحَيِّ الَّذِي لا يَمُوتُ" … "الرَّحْمَنِ", a naʿt (adjective) of "اَلْحَيِّ".

zajjaj:60-60.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قالُوا وما الرَّحْمَنُ أنَسْجُدُ لِما تَأْمُرُنا﴾ — it is also read "يَأْمُرُنا". "اَلرَّحْمَنُ" is one of the names of Allah, mentioned in the earlier scriptures, but they did not know it as one of the names of Allah. So it was said to them: "It is one of the names of Allah": ﴿قُلِ ادْعُوا اللَّهَ أوِ ادْعُوا الرَّحْمَنَ أيًّا ما تَدْعُوا فَلَهُ الأسْماءُ الحُسْنى﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 110]. Its meaning according to the lexicographers is: the Possessor of mercy beyond which there is no further limit in mercy, because "فَعْلانُ" is one of the patterns of intensification (mubālagha). You say "رَجُلٌ عَطْشانُ" and "رَيّانُ" when he is at the extreme of quenched thirst or of thirst; and likewise "فَرْحانُ", "جَذْلانُ" and "خَزْيانُ" when he is at the utmost of joy, or at the extreme of disgrace.

zajjaj:61-61.t:
His saying: ﴿تَبارَكَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ في السَّماءِ بُرُوجًا﴾: "اَلْبُرُوجُ": it was said they are the great stars. "اَلْبَرَجُ" is a wide space between the eyebrows, and everything that is visible and elevated has "baraja". They were only called "بُرُوجٌ" because of their visibility, their distinctness from one another and their elevation.
﴿وَجَعَلَ فِيها سِراجًا وقَمَرًا مُنِيرًا﴾ — it is also read "سُرُجًا", and "سُرْجًا" with sukūn on the rāʾ is permissible, like "رُسُلٌ" and "رُسْلٌ". Whoever read "سِراجًا" meant the sun, as the Exalted said: ﴿وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِراجًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 16]. Whoever read "سُرُجًا" meant the sun and the great stars along with it.

zajjaj:62-62.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ اللَّيْلَ والنَّهارَ خِلْفَةً لِمَن أرادَ أنْ يَذَّكَّرَ أوْ أرادَ شُكُورًا﴾ — it is also read "لِمَن أرادَ أنْ يَذْكُرَ". Al-Ḥasan said: whoever misses his deed of remembrance and thanks has in the night a chance to make amends, and whoever misses it by night has in the day a chance to make amends. The lexicographers said: "خِلْفَةً" means: this one comes in the track of that one; and they recited the verse of Zuhayr:
بِها العَيْنُ والآرامُ يَمْشِينَ خِلْفَةً ∗∗∗ وأطْلاؤُها يَنْهَضْنَ مِن كُلِّ مَجْثَمِ
(In it the wide-eyed wild cows and the white gazelles walk one after another, while their young rise up from every resting place.)
It also came in the exegesis that "خِلْفَةً" means: the two differ from each other, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إنَّ في خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ واخْتِلافِ اللَّيْلِ والنَّهارِ لآياتٍ لأُولِي الألْبابِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 190] ﴿الَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ قِيامًا﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 191], to the end of the verse.

zajjaj:63-63.t: His saying: ﴿وَعِبادُ الرَّحْمَنِ الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلى الأرْضِ هَوْنًا﴾, that is: they walk with tranquillity, dignity and forbearance. ﴿وَإذا خاطَبَهُمُ الجاهِلُونَ قالُوا سَلامًا﴾, that is: "we keep ourselves safe from you, a keeping-safe (salāman); we do not behave ignorantly towards you", as though they said: "a dissociation from you". "عِبادُ" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). The best view is that the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ here is what comes at the end of the sura, in His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ الغُرْفَةَ بِما صَبَرُوا﴾ [al-Furqān: 75], as though He said: "And the servants of the All-Merciful, who have all these qualities…" up to His saying: ﴿واجْعَلْنا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إمامًا﴾ [al-Furqān: 74]. It is also possible that His saying "وَعِبادُ الرَّحْمَنِ" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ with its khabar being "اَلَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلى الأرْضِ هَوْنًا".

zajjaj:64-64.t: His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا وقِيامًا﴾: everyone whom the night overtakes has "باتَ، يَبِيتُ" (spent the night), whether he slept or did not sleep: "باتَ فُلانٌ البارِحَةَ قَلِقًا" (So-and-so spent last night restless). Al-mabīt is simply being overtaken by the night.

zajjaj:65-65.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿إنَّ عَذابَها كانَ غَرامًا﴾: "اَلْغَرامُ" in the language is the severest punishment. The poet said:
وَيَوْمَ النِّسارِ ويَوْمَ الجِفارِ ∗∗∗ كانا عَذابًا وكانا غَراما
(The Day of al-Nisār and the Day of al-Jifār were a torment and were a lasting ruin.)

zajjaj:66-66.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّها ساءَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا ومُقامًا﴾: "مُسْتَقَرًّا ومُقامًا" are both accusative (manṣūb) as tamyīz (specification); the meaning is: "it is evil in respect of the place of settlement and the place of residence".

zajjaj:67-67.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿والَّذِينَ إذا أنْفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا ولَمْ يَقْتُرُوا﴾: "يُقْتِرُوا" with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the tāʾ, and with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the tāʾ; and "لَمْ يُقَتِّرُوا" — but I know of no one who read it so, I mean with a doubled tāʾ. What came in the exegesis is that extravagance (isrāf) is spending in disobedience to Allah, and that there is no extravagance in spending on what brings one closer to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and everything spent in disobedience to Allah is extravagance, because isrāf is exceeding the limit and the measure. It also came in the exegesis that extravagance is that about which people say: "So-and-so is extravagant". The truth in this is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, taught His Prophet ﷺ, when He said: ﴿وَلا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إلى عُنُقِكَ ولا تَبْسُطْها كُلَّ البَسْطِ فَتَقْعُدَ مَلُومًا مَحْسُورًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 29].

zajjaj:68-68.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ يَلْقَ أثامًا﴾: "يَلْقَ" is jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The interpretation of الأثام is the interpretation of requital for a thing. Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī said: one says "قَدْ لَقِيَ أثامَ ذَلِكَ", that is: the requital of that. Sībawayh and al-Khalīl hold that its meaning is: "he will meet the requital of sin". Sībawayh said: "يُضاعَفْ لَهُ العَذابُ" is jussive because the doubling of the punishment is the meeting of الأثام, as the poet said:
مَتى تَأْتِنا تُلْمِمْ بِنا في دِيارِنا ∗∗∗ تَجِدْ حَطَبًا جَزْلًا ونارًا تَوَقَّدا
(Whenever you come to us — calling on us in our dwellings — you will find thick firewood and a fire blazing.)
because coming is calling on, so he made "تُلْمِمْ" jussive since it has the meaning of "تَأْتِي". Al-Ḥasan alone read "يُضَعَّفْ لَهُ العَذابُ", and it is good and sound; you say "ضاعَفْتُ الشَّيْءَ" and "ضَعَّفْتُهُ". ʿĀṣim read "يُضاعَفُ لَهُ العَذابُ" in the nominative, on the interpretation of its being an explanation of "يَلْقَ أثامًا", as though someone said: what is the meeting of الأثام? and it was said: the punishment will be doubled for the sinner.

zajjaj:70-70.t: His saying: ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ حَسَناتٍ﴾: it is not that the evil deed itself becomes a good deed; rather the interpretation is that the evil deed is erased by repentance and the good deed is written along with the repentance. As for the disbeliever, Allah nullifies his deeds and establishes the evil deeds against him.

zajjaj:72-72.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والَّذِينَ لا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ﴾: it was said: "اَلزُّورُ" is associating partners with Allah. It also came that they do not attend the festivals of the Christians. What came concerning "اَلزُّورُ" is that it is associating partners with Allah. As for the prohibition of false testimony in the Book of Allah, it is His saying: ﴿وَلا تَقْفُ ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ إنَّ السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ كُلُّ أُولَئِكَ كانَ عَنْهُ مَسْؤُولا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 36]. And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإذا مَرُّوا بِاللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا كِرامًا﴾: its interpretation is: they turned away from it, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَإذا سَمِعُوا اللَّغْوَ أعْرَضُوا عَنْهُ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 55]. The interpretation of "مَرُّوا بِاللَّغْوِ" is: they passed by everything that ought to be discarded (yulghā), and the meaning of "يُلْغى" is: it is cast aside. It came in the exegesis that when they wanted to mention sexual relations they spoke of it by allusion; and some of them said: it is the mention of obscene talk (rafath), and the meaning is one. It also came that they do not sit with the people of idle talk, who are the people of sins, and do not side with them (yumāliʾūnahum) in them, that is: do not help them in them. It also came concerning "لا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ": gatherings of singing.

zajjaj:73-73.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والَّذِينَ إذا ذُكِّرُوا بِآياتِ رَبِّهِمْ لَمْ يَخِرُّوا عَلَيْها صُمًّا وعُمْيانًا﴾: its interpretation is: "when they are recited to them, they fall down prostrating and weeping, hearing and seeing what they were commanded and what they were forbidden". The proof of that is His saying: ﴿وَمِمَّنْ هَدَيْنا واجْتَبَيْنا إذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُ الرَّحْمَنِ خَرُّوا سُجَّدًا وبُكِيًّا﴾ [Maryam: 58]. Similar to this in poetry is his saying:
بِأيْدِي رِجالٍ لَمْ يَشِيمُوا سُيُوفَهم ∗∗∗ ولَمْ تَكْثُرِ القَتْلى بِها حِينَ سُلَّتِ
(In the hands of men who did not sheathe their swords without the slain becoming many by them when they were drawn.)
Its interpretation is: in the hands of men who sheathed their swords only when the slain had become many. The meaning of "يَشِيمُوا سُيُوفَهم" is: they sheathe their swords. So the interpretation is: "and those who, when they are reminded of the signs of their Lord, fall down prostrating, obedient".

zajjaj:74-74.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿هَبْ لَنا مِن أزْواجِنا وذُرِّيّاتِنا قُرَّةَ أعْيُنٍ﴾ — it is also read "وَذُرِّيَّتِنا". They asked that Allah join their offspring to them in Paradise, and that He make their families such that their eyes are comforted by them. ﴿واجْعَلْنا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إمامًا﴾, that is: and make us among those by whom the God-fearing are guided, and who are guided by the God-fearing.

zajjaj:77-77.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ ما يَعْبَأُ بِكم رَبِّي لَوْلا دُعاؤُكُمْ﴾, that is: were it not for your affirming His oneness. It came in the exegesis: "ما يَعْبَأُ بِكم" means "what would He do with you?". The interpretation of "ما يَعْبَأُ بِكم" is: what weight would you have with Him?! as you say "ما عَبَأْتُ بِفُلانٍ", that is: "he had no weight or worth with me". The origin of "اَلْعِبْءُ" in the language is: the burden; and from that is "عَبَّأْتُ المَتاعَ": I put some of the goods on top of others.
His saying: ﴿فَقَدْ كَذَّبْتُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزامًا﴾: it came in the exegesis from the group (of exegetes) that the Day of "Badr" is meant by it; and it came that the slain were bound closely together (lūzima) there. It was also read "لَزامًا". Its interpretation — and Allah knows best — is: "your denial will be lizām (binding): it will cling to you, so you will not be granted repentance and punishment will cling to you". So the Day of "Badr" enters into this, along with other punishment that clings to them. Abū ʿUbayda said: "لِزامًا" means: a decisive separation (fayṣal), which is close to what we said, except that (our) statement is more explanatory. Abū ʿUbayda recited, from Ṣakhr, the brother of al-Hudhalī:
فَإمّا يَنْجُوا مِن حَتْفِ أرْضٍ ∗∗∗ فَقَدْ لَقِيا حُتُوفَهُما لِزامًا
(If the two escape the death of one land, they have met their deaths inescapably.)
The interpretation of this is that death, when it is decreed, is binding: if one escapes death in one place, it overtakes him in another place, clinging to him inescapably. Whoever read "لَزامًا" with fatḥa on the lām, it is on the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "لَزِمَ، لَزامًا".

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Furqān
Meccan
﷽
﴿تَبارَكَ الَّذِي نَـزَّلَ الفُرْقانَ عَلى عَبْدِهِ﴾ — "تَبارَكَ": its meaning is "تَفاعَلَ" (the pattern tafāʿala) from "اَلْبَرَكَةُ" (blessing); so say the people of the language, and so it was related from Ibn ʿAbbās. The meaning of "اَلْبَرَكَةُ" is abundance in everything possessing good. "اَلْفُرْقانُ" is the Qurʾān; it is called "فُرْقان" because by it a distinction is made between truth and falsehood.
His saying: ﴿لِيَكُونَ لِلْعالَمِينَ نَذِيرًا﴾ — "اَلنَّذِيرُ" is the one who warns of the punishment of Allah; everyone who causes fear has warned. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَأنْذَرْتُكم نارًا تَلَظّى﴾ [al-Layl: 14].

zajjaj:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿سَمِعُوا لَها تَغَيُّظًا وزَفِيرًا﴾, that is: they heard from it the boiling of rage.

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿دَعَوْا هُنالِكَ ثُبُورًا﴾ — in the sense of "هَلاكًا" (destruction), and its accusative is as a maṣdar (verbal noun), as if they said: "ثُبِرْنا ثُبُورًا" (we have been destroyed utterly).

zajjaj:14-14.t: ﴿لا تَدْعُوا اليَوْمَ ثُبُورًا واحِدًا وادْعُوا ثُبُورًا كَثِيرًا﴾, that is: your destruction is greater than that you should call [for it] a single time. It was said "ثُبُورًا كَثِيرًا" because "ثُبُورًا" is a maṣdar (verbal noun), so it serves for little and much in the singular form, as you say "ضَرَبْتُهُ ضَرْبًا كَثِيرًا" (I struck him much striking) and "ضَرَبْتُهُ واحِدًا", meaning "ضَرَبْتُهُ ضَرْبًا واحِدًا" (I struck him a single blow).

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ أذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ أمْ جَنَّةُ الخُلْدِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ المُتَّقُونَ﴾ — if someone says: how can it be said "Paradise is better than the Fire", when there is no good at all in the Fire, and comparison occurs only among things that fall within a single kind? [The answer is that] Paradise and the Fire both fall under the category of abodes, in a single kind; therefore it was said: "أذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ أمْ جَنَّةُ الخُلْدِ؟" (is that better, or the Garden of Eternity?), as Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿خَيْرٌ مُسْتَقَرًّا وأحْسَنُ مَقِيلا﴾ [al-Furqān: 24].

zajjaj:16-16.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كانَ عَلى رَبِّكَ وعْدًا مَسْؤُولا﴾ — "مَسْؤُولًا" (asked for): that is the saying of the angels: ﴿رَبَّنا وأدْخِلْهم جَنّاتِ عَدْنٍ الَّتِي وعَدْتَهم ومَن صَلَحَ مِن آبائِهِمْ﴾ [Ghāfir: 8].

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيرًا﴾ — Allah created living creatures and determined for them what sets them right and sustains them, and He determined all of that for His creation with wisdom and measure.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إنْ هَذا إلا إفْكٌ افْتَراهُ﴾ — "اَلْإفْكُ" is the lie. ﴿وَأعانَهُ عَلَيْهِ قَوْمٌ آخَرُونَ﴾ — they mean the Jews.
﴿فَقَدْ جاءُوا ظُلْمًا وزُورًا﴾ — "اَلزُّورُ" is falsehood. "ظُلْمًا وزُورًا" is accusative on [the basis of] "فَقَدْ جاؤُوا بِظُلْمٍ وزُورٍ" (they have come with injustice and falsehood); when the bāʾ dropped, the verb reached [the noun directly] and put it in the accusative (accusative by removal of the preposition).

zajjaj:5-5.t:
﴿وَقالُوا أساطِيرُ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ — [أساطِيرُ is] the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); the meaning is: "and they said: that which is his book is the legends of the ancients", meaning: "of what the ancients wrote down". The singular of "اَلْأساطِيرُ" is "أُسْطُورَةٌ", as you say "أُحْدُوثَةٌ" and "أحادِيثُ".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَهِيَ تُمْلى عَلَيْهِ بُكْرَةً وأصِيلا﴾ — "اَلْأصِيلُ" is the evening.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقالُوا مالِ هَذا الرَّسُولِ يَأْكُلُ الطَّعامَ ويَمْشِي في الأسْواقِ﴾ — "ما" is written separately from the lām. The meaning is: "what is the matter with this messenger, in the state of his eating food and walking in the markets?!" They wanted the messenger to be of other than human constitution, but what is required is that the messenger to human beings be a human being, so that he be closer to being understood.
His saying: ﴿لَوْلا أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ فَيَكُونَ مَعَهُ نَذِيرًا﴾ — they demanded that there be a partnership in prophethood and that the partner be an angel, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says: ﴿وَلَوْ جَعَلْناهُ مَلَكًا لَجَعَلْناهُ رَجُلا﴾ [al-Anʿām: 9], that is: he would not be able to make them understand unless he were a man. The meaning of "لَوْلا" is "هَلّا" (why not), and the interpretation of "هَلّا" is interrogation; and [فَيَكُونَ] is in the accusative, being an answer with the fāʾ to the interrogation.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
﴿أوْ يُلْقى إلَيْهِ كَنْـزٌ أوْ تَكُونُ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ﴾ — and if you wish, "أوْ يَكُونُ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ". The accusative is not permissible in "يَكُونُ لَهُ", because "يَكُونُ" is conjoined to the interrogation; the meaning is: "why has not an angel been sent down to him, or a treasure cast to him, or a garden be his?" [Translator's note: the source vocalizes «أنْزِلُ» here.] "اَلْجَنَّةُ" is the orchard. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that had He willed that, and better than it, He would have done it, and He said: ﴿تَبارَكَ الَّذِي إنْ شاءَ جَعَلَ لَكَ خَيْرًا مِن ذَلِكَ جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ ويَجْعَلْ لَكَ قُصُورًا﴾ [al-Furqān: 10], that is: had He willed, He would have done more than what they said. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, offered the Prophet ﷺ the matter of this world, but he declined it and preferred the matter of the Hereafter. As for "يَجْعَلْ", it is jussive (majzūm); the meaning is: "if He wills, He will make for you gardens and make for you palaces". Whoever puts it in the nominative does so as a resumption (istiʾnāf); the meaning is: "and He will make for you palaces", that is: "Allah will give you in the Hereafter more than what they said".
His saying: ﴿أوْ تَكُونُ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ يَأْكُلُ مِنها﴾, and "يَأْكُلْ مِنها" [is also permissible].

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿قالُوا سُبْحانَكَ ما كانَ يَنْبَغِي لَنا أنْ نَتَّخِذَ مِن دُونِكَ مِن أوْلِياءَ﴾ — [this is] when the angels were asked, and it was said: ﴿أأنْتُمْ أضْلَلْتُمْ عِبادِي هَؤُلاءِ أمْ هم ضَلُّوا السَّبِيلَ﴾ [al-Furqān: 17]; and it is possible that the address is to ʿĪsā and ʿUzayr. Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī alone read: "قالُوا سُبْحانَكَ ما كانَ يَنْبَغِي لَنا أنْ نُتَّخَذَ مِن دُونِكَ مِن أوْلِياءَ", with ḍamma on the nūn, as a passive (lit. "that whose agent is not named"). This reading is, in the view of most grammarians, an error. It is an error only because "مِن" enters in this construction only upon nouns when they are the first object; it does not enter upon the object that stands as a ḥāl (circumstantial) [i.e. the second object]. You say "ما اتَّخَذْتُ مِن أحَدٍ ولِيًّا" (I did not take anyone as an ally), but "ما اتَّخَذْتُ أحَدًا مِن ولِيٍّ" is not permissible, because "مِن" enters only because it negates one in the sense of all. You say "ما مِن أحَدٍ قائِمًا" (no one at all is standing) and "ما مِن رَجُلٍ مُحِبًّا لِما يَضُرُّهُ" (no man at all loves what harms him), but "ما رَجُلٌ مِن مُحِبٍّ ما يَضُرُّهُ" is not permissible. There is no valid way for this reading, except that al-Farrāʾ permitted it with weakness, and claimed that he takes "مِن أوْلِياءَ" as the noun (ism) and takes the predicate (khabar) as what is in "نُتَّخَذَ", as if it were made by inversion (qalb). In our view there is no valid way for this at all; were this permissible, it would be permissible in ﴿فَما مِنكم مِن أحَدٍ عَنْهُ حاجِزِينَ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 47] [to say] "ما أحَدٌ عَنْهُ مِن حاجِزِينَ", and this is an error with no valid way. So recognise it, for recognising the error in it is better than reading it; and all the Readers oppose him in this. Of the same kind of slip is in the reading of al-Ḥasan: "وَما تَنَزَّلَتْ بِهِ الشَّياطُونَ".
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَكانُوا قَوْمًا بُورًا﴾ — it was said in the exegesis: "هَلْكى" (perishing). "اَلْبائِرُ" in the language is the corrupt, that in which there is no good; and likewise "أرْضٌ بائِرَةٌ" (fallow land) is land left without being sown.

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوكم بِما تَقُولُونَ﴾ — it is read "بِما يَقُولُونَ", with the yāʾ and with the tāʾ. Whoever reads "بِما تَقُولُونَ" with the tāʾ, the meaning is: "they have belied you through their saying: that they are gods"; and whoever reads with the yāʾ, the meaning is: "they have belied you through their saying: ﴿سُبْحانَكَ ما كانَ يَنْبَغِي لَنا أنْ نَتَّخِذَ مِن دُونِكَ مِن أوْلِياءَ﴾ [al-Furqān: 18]". [Translator's note: the explanations of the two readings are given as in the source; one would expect «تَقُولُونَ» to refer to the idolaters' claim and «يَقُولُونَ» to the angels' denial.] His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَما تَسْتَطِيعُونَ صَرْفًا ولا نَصْرًا﴾, that is: you are not able to avert from themselves the punishment that befalls them, nor to help themselves. [Translator's note: the pronouns shift between "you" and "them" in the source.]

zajjaj:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما أرْسَلْنا قَبْلَكَ مِنَ المُرْسَلِينَ إلا إنَّهم لَيَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعامَ ويَمْشُونَ في الأسْواقِ﴾ — this is an argument against them in their saying: ﴿مالِ هَذا الرَّسُولِ يَأْكُلُ الطَّعامَ ويَمْشِي في الأسْواقِ﴾ [al-Furqān: 7]. It was said to them: "Thus were the messengers who passed away: they ate food and walked in the markets; so how could Muḥammad ﷺ be an innovation among the messengers?" As for the entry of "إنَّهم" after "إلّا", it is on the interpretation: "ما أرْسَلْنا رُسُلًا إلّا هم يَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعامَ، وإلّا إنَّهم لَيَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعامَ" (We sent no messengers except that they ate food, and except that indeed they ate food). "رُسُلًا" (messengers) was omitted because "مِن" in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿مِنَ المُرْسَلِينَ﴾ is an indication of what was omitted from it. As for an example of the lām after "إلّا", it is the saying of the poet:
؎ما أنْطَيانِي ولا سَألْتُهُما ∗∗∗ إلّا وإنِّي لَحاجِزٌ كَرَمِي
(The two did not give to me, nor did I ask them, except that I was indeed restraining my generosity.)
He means "أعْطَيانِي" (they gave me). Some grammarians claimed that "مَن" after "إلّا" is omitted, as if the meaning in his view were: "إلّا مَن لَيَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعامَ" (except those who indeed eat food). This is a clear error, because the ṣila (relative clause) of "مَن" would be "إنَّهم لَيَأْكُلُونَ", and it is not permissible to omit the relative noun and keep the ṣila.
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا بَعْضَكم لِبَعْضٍ فِتْنَةً﴾ — there are two views on it. It was said: a nobleman would sometimes want [to embrace] Islam, then learn that someone beneath him in nobility had embraced Islam before him, so he would refrain from Islam lest it be said that someone beneath him had embraced Islam before him. It was also said: the poor man would say, "Why was I not given the station of the rich man?!", and the afflicted would say, "Why was I not given the station of the healthy?!" — such as the blind, the chronically disabled, and those like them. His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أتَصْبِرُونَ وكانَ رَبُّكَ بَصِيرًا﴾, that is: will you be patient in affliction? For you have been made aware of what the patient are promised.

zajjaj:21-21.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ لا يَرْجُونَ لِقاءَنا لَوْلا أُنْـزِلَ عَلَيْنا المَلائِكَةُ﴾ — the meaning of "لَوْلا" is "هَلّا" (why not). ﴿أوْ نَرى رَبَّنا لَقَدِ اسْتَكْبَرُوا في أنْفُسِهِمْ وعَتَوْا عُتُوًّا كَبِيرًا﴾ — so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that those who are not certain of the resurrection, and do not hope for reward for deeds upon meeting Allah, demanded of signs what had not come to any nation among the nations; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that they had become arrogant within themselves and been insolent with great insolence. "عُتُوًّا كَثِيرًا" with the thāʾ is permissible. "اَلْعُتُوُّ" in the language is exceeding the limit in wrongdoing.

zajjaj:22-22.t: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that the time in which they will see the angels is the Day of Resurrection, and that Allah has deprived them of glad tidings at that time, and He said: ﴿يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ المَلائِكَةَ لا بُشْرى يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾. "يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ" is accusative in two ways. One of them is in the sense of "لا بُشْرى تَكُونُ لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ المَلائِكَةَ" (there will be no glad tidings for the criminals on the day they see the angels), and "يَوْمَئِذٍ" is a reinforcement (muʾakkid) of "يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ المَلائِكَةَ". It may not be accusative by His saying "لا بُشْرى", because what is connected with "لا" does not govern what precedes it; but when it was said "لا بُشْرى لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ", it was made clear on which day that is, so it is as though it were said: "they are denied glad tidings on the day they see the angels, which is the Day of Resurrection". ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ حِجْرًا مَحْجُورًا﴾ — it was also read "حُجْرًا" with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ. The meaning is: "and the angels will say: حِجْرًا مَحْجُورًا", that is: "glad tidings are utterly forbidden to them". The origin of "اَلْحِجْرُ" in the language is what you have placed a restriction upon, that is: what you have prevented from being reached; everything you have prevented [access to], you have restricted (ḥajarta ʿalayhi). Likewise the ḥajr of judges over orphans is only their preventing them from disposing of their property; and likewise "اَلْحُجْرَةُ" (the chamber) in which people lodge is what they have enclosed. [The second way:] "يَوْمَ" may be accusative in the sense of "اُذْكُرْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ المَلائِكَةَ" (remember the day they see the angels); then He gave a statement and said: ﴿لا بُشْرى يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾. "اَلْمُجْرِمُونَ" are those who have committed sins, and in this place they are those who have committed disbelief in Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَدِمْنا إلى ما عَمِلُوا مِن عَمَلٍ﴾ — the meaning of "قَدِمْنا" is "عَمَدْنا" and "قَصَدْنا" (We turned to, We proceeded to), as you say "قامَ فُلانٌ يَشْتُمُ فُلانًا" (so-and-so set about reviling so-and-so), meaning "he proceeded to revile so-and-so", and you do not mean "قامَ" in the sense of standing on the two feet. ﴿فَجَعَلْناهُ هَباءً مَنثُورًا﴾ — "اَلْهَباءُ" is what comes out of a window-opening with the sunlight, resembling dust. Its interpretation is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, rendered their deeds void until they became like scattered motes. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known the superiority of the people of Paradise over the people of the Fire, and said: ﴿أصْحابُ الجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُسْتَقَرًّا وأحْسَنُ مَقِيلا﴾ [al-Furqān: 24]. "اَلْمَقِيلَ" is the abode at the time of the midday rest; it was also said: it is sleep at midday. It came in the exegesis that the people of Paradise go to their families in Paradise at midday.

zajjaj:25-25.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ السَّماءُ بِالغَمامِ﴾ — it is also read "تَشَّقَّقُ", with the shīn doubled, and the meaning is "تَتَشَقَّقُ" (it splits open). ﴿وَنُـزِّلَ المَلائِكَةُ تَنْـزِيلا﴾ — it came in the exegesis that heaven after heaven will split open and the angels will descend to the earth, and that is His saying: ﴿وَجاءَ رَبُّكَ والمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا﴾ [al-Fajr: 22].

zajjaj:26-26.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿المُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍ الحَقُّ لِلرَّحْمَنِ﴾ — "اَلْحَقُّ" is a ṣifa (adjective) of "اَلْمُلْكُ". Its meaning is that the sovereignty which is truly sovereignty is the sovereignty of the All-Merciful on the Day of Resurrection, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿لِمَنِ المُلْكُ اليَوْمَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 16], because a passing sovereignty is as if it were not sovereignty. "اَلْمُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍ الحَقَّ لِلرَّحْمَنِ" (accusative) is permissible, but it has not been read thus, so do not read it. The accusative would be in two ways: one of them in the sense of "the sovereignty on that day belongs to the All-Merciful — I affirm that truly (aḥuqqu dhālika al-ḥaqqa)", and [the other] on [an implied] "أعْنِي الحَقَّ" (I mean: the true one).

zajjaj:27-27.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ الظّالِمُ عَلى يَدَيْهِ يَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي اتَّخَذْتُ مَعَ الرَّسُولِ سَبِيلا﴾ — it is related that ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ is the wrongdoer here, and that he will eat his hand out of regret, and then [it] will grow back. He had resolved upon Islam, and that reached Umayya ibn Khalaf, and Umayya said to him: "My face is forbidden to your face if you embrace Islam — [I will not] ever speak to you." So Umayya refrained from Islam because of Umayya's saying. [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense requires "ʿUqba refrained from Islam because of Umayya's saying".] So when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will eat his hand out of regret and wish that he had believed and taken with the Prophet, upon him be peace, a way to Paradise; and that is His saying: ﴿يا ويْلَتى لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أتَّخِذْ فُلانًا خَلِيلا﴾ [al-Furqān: 28] ﴿لَقَدْ أضَلَّنِي عَنِ الذِّكْرِ بَعْدَ إذْ جاءَنِي﴾ [al-Furqān: 29]. It has also been said concerning "لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أتَّخِذْ فُلانًا خَلِيلًا": that is, I wish I had not taken Satan as a close friend; and the confirmation of this view is: ﴿وَكانَ الشَّيْطانُ لِلإنْسانِ خَذُولا﴾ [al-Furqān: 29]. And it is not impossible that his accepting [the advice] from Umayya was of the work of Satan and his helpers. "اِتَّخَتُّ" is permissible, with the dhāl pronounced distinctly or assimilated into the tāʾ, and assimilation is more common and better.

zajjaj:30-30.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقالَ الرَّسُولُ يا رَبِّ إنَّ قَوْمِي اتَّخَذُوا هَذا القُرْآنَ مَهْجُورًا﴾ — they made it like "al-hujr"; "اَلْهُجْرُ" is speech from which no benefit is derived, and they used to say that the Prophet ﷺ was talking nonsense (yahjuru). "مَهْجُورًا" may also mean: abandoned, that is: they made it abandoned, not listening to it nor seeking to understand it.

zajjaj:31-31.t:
﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوًّا مِنَ المُجْرِمِينَ﴾ — "عَدُوًّا" is singular in form, and it may carry the meaning of both the group and the individual, as He said: ﴿فَإنَّهم عَدُوٌّ لِي إلا رَبَّ العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 77]; so it may be in the sense of "أعْداءٌ" (enemies). It came in the exegesis that the enemy of the Prophet ﷺ was Abū Jahl ibn Hishām.
His saying: ﴿وَكَفى بِرَبِّكَ هادِيًا ونَصِيرًا﴾ — "هادِيًا ونَصِيرًا" are both accusative in two ways. One of them is the ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "your Lord suffices in the state of guiding and helping". The second way is that it be accusative as tamyīz (specification), in the sense of "your Lord suffices as guides and helpers".

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلا نُـزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ القُرْآنُ جُمْلَةً واحِدَةً﴾ — its meaning is: "why was the Qurʾān not sent down to him at a single time?" Between the first revelation of the Qurʾān and the last there were twenty years, and they said: why was it not sent down all at once, as the Torah was sent down? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He sent it down in parts so that it would be made firm in the heart of the Prophet ﷺ, and He said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِ فُؤادَكَ﴾, that is: We sent it down thus, in parts; because the meaning of their saying ﴿لَوْلا نُـزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ القُرْآنُ جُمْلَةً واحِدَةً﴾ indicates the meaning "why was the Qurʾān sent down to him in parts?", so they were informed why that was, that is: for making firm. ﴿وَرَتَّلْناهُ تَرْتِيلا﴾, that is: We sent it down in measured sequence (tartīl), which is the opposite of haste; it is deliberateness.

zajjaj:33-33.t: His saying: ﴿إلا جِئْناكَ بِالحَقِّ وأحْسَنَ تَفْسِيرًا﴾ — its meaning is: "they do not bring you any likeness except that We bring you what is the truth and better in explanation than their likeness", except that "مِن" (than) was omitted because there is an indication of it in the speech. If you said "رَأيْتُ زَيْدًا وعَمْرًا، فَكانَ عَمْرٌو أحْسَنَ وجْهًا" (I saw Zayd and ʿAmr, and ʿAmr was better of face), the speech would contain an indication that you mean "than Zayd".

zajjaj:34-34.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ إلى جَهَنَّمَ أُولَئِكَ شَرٌّ مَكانًا وأضَلُّ سَبِيلا﴾ — "اَلَّذِينَ" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); "أُولَئِكَ" is nominative, a second mubtadaʾ; "شَرٌّ" is the khabar (predicate) of "أُولَئِكَ"; and "أُولَئِكَ" together with "شَرٌّ" is the khabar of "اَلَّذِينَ". It came in the exegesis that people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in three kinds: a kind on mounts, a kind on their feet, and a kind on their faces. «It was said: O Messenger of Allah, how will they walk on their faces?! The Prophet ﷺ said: "The One who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces."»

zajjaj:35-35.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى الكِتابَ وجَعَلْنا مَعَهُ أخاهُ هارُونَ وزِيرًا﴾ — "اَلْوَزِيرُ" in the language is the one to whom one has recourse and in whose counsel one finds protection; and "اَلْوَزَرُ" is that in which refuge is sought and by which one holds fast. From it is His saying: ﴿كَلا لا وزَرَ﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 11], that is: no refuge and no escape on the Day of Resurrection, except for whomever Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has mercy upon.

zajjaj:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿فَدَمَّرْناهم تَدْمِيرًا﴾ — by it He means Pharaoh and his people, and those who were transformed into apes and swine.

zajjaj:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ لَمّا كَذَّبُوا الرُّسُلَ أغْرَقْناهُمْ﴾ — this wording indicates that the people of Nūḥ also belied others besides Nūḥ, because of His saying "اَلرُّسُلَ" (the messengers). It is also possible that by "اَلرُّسُلَ" Nūḥ alone is meant, because whoever belies one prophet has belied all the prophets, since he is opposed to the prophets, because the prophets believe in Allah and in all His messengers. It is also possible that one is meant while the generic term is mentioned, as a man says to a man who spends a single dirham: "أنْتَ مِمَّنْ يُنْفِقُ الدَّراهِمَ" (you are one of those who spend dirhams), that is: one whose spending is of this kind; and "فُلانٌ يَرْكَبُ الدَّوابَّ" (so-and-so rides mounts), even if he rides only one.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَعادًا وثَمُودَ وأصْحابَ الرَّسِّ وقُرُونًا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ كَثِيرًا﴾ — "قَوْمَ نُوحٍ" are accusative in the sense of "وَأغْرَقْنا قَوْمَ نُوحٍ" (and We drowned the people of Nūḥ). "عادًا وثَمُودَ وأصْحابَ الرَّسِّ" are accusative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the hāʾ and mīm in His saying ﴿وَجَعَلْناهم لِلنّاسِ آيَةً﴾ [al-Furqān: 37]. It may also be conjoined to the sense of ﴿وَأعْتَدْنا لِلظّالِمِينَ عَذابًا ألِيمًا﴾ [al-Furqān: 37], the interpretation being: "We promised the wrongdoers punishment, and We promised ʿĀd, Thamūd and the people of al-Rass". Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: and the proof of that is His saying ﴿وَأعْتَدْنا لِلظّالِمِينَ عَذابًا ألِيمًا﴾ [al-Furqān: 37]. "اَلرَّسُّ" is a well. It is related that they were a people who belied their prophet and threw him into a well, that is: they thrust him into it. It is related that "اَلرَّسُّ" is a village in al-Yamāma called "Malḥ"; and it is related that "اَلرَّسُّ" is the dwellings of a group of Thamūd.
His saying: ﴿وَقُرُونًا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ كَثِيرًا﴾ — it is related that the span of a qarn (generation) is seventy years.

zajjaj:39-39.t: His saying: ﴿وَكُلا ضَرَبْنا لَهُ الأمْثالَ﴾ — "كُلًّا" is accusative by an implied (muḍmar) verb which the overt one explains; the meaning is: "وَأنْذَرْنا كُلًّا ضَرَبْنا لَهُ الأمْثالَ" (and We warned each one; We struck likenesses for him). ﴿وَكُلا تَبَّرْنا تَتْبِيرًا﴾ — "اَلتَّتْبِيرُ" is destruction and ruin; everything you have broken and crumbled, you have "tabbartahu". From this, broken glass is called "اَلتِّبْرُ", and likewise "تِبْرُ الذَّهَبِ" (gold dust/nuggets).

zajjaj:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أتَوْا عَلى القَرْيَةِ الَّتِي أُمْطِرَتْ مَطَرَ السَّوْءِ﴾ — "أتَوْا" (they came), that is: the polytheists of Mecca. By it is meant the town of the people of Lūṭ upon which Allah rained down stones. [Translator's note: the source has «أمَرَ» (commanded), apparently for «أمْطَرَ» (rained).] So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that what emboldened them to belie [the truth], and [the reason] that they paid no heed to the punishment they had witnessed in this world, was that they did not believe in the resurrection, and He said: ﴿أفَلَمْ يَكُونُوا يَرَوْنَها بَلْ كانُوا لا يَرْجُونَ نُشُورًا﴾. It was said: [it means] they do not fear the punishment they were promised after the resurrection. But what the people of the language hold is that rajāʾ (hope) is not in the sense of fear — this is the position of those who reject [words having] opposite meanings (al-aḍdād), and it is, in my view, the truth. The meaning is: "rather, they did not hope for the reward of whoever does good after the resurrection, so they committed sins".

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿وَإذا رَأوْكَ إنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إلا هُزُوًا أهَذا الَّذِي بَعَثَ اللَّهُ رَسُولا﴾ — the meaning is: "they say: is this the one whom Allah has sent to us as a messenger?"

zajjaj:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿أرَأيْتَ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إلَهَهُ هَواهُ﴾ — it is related that one of the people of the Jāhiliyya would worship a stone, and when he passed a stone better than it, he would leave the first and worship the second. It was also said: "مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إلَهَهُ هَواهُ", that is: he obeyed his desire and followed it, and did not heed the consequence of that.
His saying: ﴿أفَأنْتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ وكِيلا﴾, that is: a guardian.
